name: 1PointFive
tech_note: Liquid-solvent (KOH) Direct Air Capture using Carbon Engineering technology, with CO2 stored via geologic sequestration in saline formations.
description: 1PointFive is Occidental Petroleum's CCUS subsidiary developing the STRATOS Direct Air Capture facility in Ector County, Texas, designed to capture up to 500,000 tonnes of CO2 per year. Phase 1 is in final startup with Q2 2026 initial operations expected and Phase 2 commissioning beginning the same quarter. The company has signed CDR offtake deals with Microsoft, Amazon, AT&T, Airbus, Bain & Company, and others, and is also developing the Pelican Sequestration Hub in Louisiana.

name: 280 Earth
tech_note: 280 Earth operates a solid-sorbent direct air capture system using a continuous-flow granular sorbent process, co-producing water and able to run on industrial waste heat.
description: 280 Earth is a Google X / Alphabet spin-out (2022) headquartered in Mountain View, CA that operates a 500 t/yr DAC commercial demonstration plant in The Dalles, Oregon (online May 2024). It holds a $40M Frontier offtake for 61,571 tons of CDR between 2024-2030, raised a $50M Series B led by Builders VC in 2024, and is scaling to 5,000 t/yr Gen-1 modules with a targeted 20,000+ t/yr site capacity by late 2025/early 2026.

name: 30 Carbon Capture Utilization & Storage Startups To Watch in 2026
323ppm
tech_note: A one-person French consultancy (bureau d'étude) promoting biochar adoption among farmers, municipalities and businesses; it does not produce biochar itself but partners with certified biochar producers for regenerative agriculture, urban plantings, soil remediation and stormwater filtration projects.
description: 323ppm is a small French biochar-focused consultancy that works to develop the French biochar market. It does not operate pyrolysis equipment; instead it advises farmers, municipalities and companies on biochar applications and sources material from certified producers. The company reports it is currently running its first pilot project with a regional farmer.

name: 350solutions
tech_note: Independent third-party Validation & Verification Body (VVB) providing project validation, credit verification, and technical due diligence for CDR registries (Puro.Earth, Isometric) and credit buyers/investors.
description: 350Solutions is a Raleigh, NC-based independent Validation & Verification Body (VVB) for CDR projects. <cite index="2-6">They are accredited by ANAB under ISO 17020 for Environmental Technology Verification via ISO 14034 and are approved by both Puro and Isometric as VVBs.</cite> <cite index="8-1">Their diligence efforts have been a part of over $200M in CDR purchase agreements and technology investments.</cite> They do not physically remove CO2 themselves — they are part of the CDR ecosystem as a third-party verifier.

name: 3Degrees
tech_note: Climate consultancy, project developer, and credit retailer that sources, brokers, and manages portfolios of carbon removal credits (biochar, ERW, BECCS, IFM) for corporate buyers via its CDR Bridge and CDR Catalyst products.
description: 3Degrees is a San Francisco-based global climate solutions consultancy and B Corp that operates as a carbon credit project developer and retailer, helping Fortune 500 companies and utilities procure renewable energy and carbon removal credits. Through its Carbon Removal Suite (CDR Bridge and CDR Catalyst), it aggregates and brokers third-party removal credits across biochar, BECCS, ERW, and improved forest management — notably facilitating Microsoft's 80,000-tonne IFM purchase from Western Rivers Conservancy. It is part of the CDR ecosystem as a broker/retailer/aggregator rather than a direct removal operator.

name: 3R-BioPhosphate
tech_note: Zero-emission high-temperature pyrolysis (up to 850°C) of food-grade animal bones to produce animal bone char biofertilizer (phosphorus recovery) with carbon-negative biochar and bio-oil as co-products.
description: 3R-BioPhosphate Ltd. is a Hungary-based pyrolysis engineering company that upcycles food-grade animal bones into ABC BioPhosphate fertilizer and carbon-negative biochar at its 30-hectare 3R-BIOFARM Upcycling Centre in Trans-Danubia. Led by inventor Edward Someus, the company operates EU-permitted, REACH-registered zero-emission pyrolysis systems with 2,000–20,800 t/y throughput capacities and has advanced to TRL9 industrial readiness. Primary products are phosphorus biofertilizer and biochar, with bio-oil and renewable energy as co-products.

tech_note: Injects CO2 dissolved in water into peridotite rock formations to permanently mineralize it into stable carbonate minerals underground.
description: 44.01 is an Omani climate-tech supplier that accelerates natural peridotite mineralization to permanently sequester CO2 captured from DAC or industrial point sources. The company won the XPRIZE Carbon Removal with Project Hajar and operates pilots in Oman and the UAE with partners including ADNOC, Masdar, Aircapture, Mission Zero, and Holcim.

name: 5 Top Startups building Enhanced Weathering Solutions
8 Rivers/Calcite
tech_note: Calcite is a calcium-looping DAC technology that uses hydrated lime to absorb atmospheric CO2, forming limestone that is then calcined in an oxygen-fired kiln to release concentrated CO2 for sequestration while regenerating the sorbent.
description: 8 Rivers Capital is a Durham, NC-based decarbonization technology developer whose Calcite process is a calcium-looping direct air capture technology anchoring the DOE-funded Southeast DAC (SEDAC) Hub in Mobile County, Alabama. Project Cardinal, the first commercial Calcite deployment, is planned for the US Gulf Coast with FEED commencing in 2025 (Wood was awarded the FEED in March 2025), backed by a September 2024 investment from JX Nippon (now ENEOS Xplora). The company is majority-owned by SK Group.

name: 8 direct air capture startups slashing carbon removal costs
A Healthier Earth
tech_note: Operates PYREG pyrolysis equipment (PX6000, PX1500, P500) to convert local organic waste (joinery offcuts, garden waste) into biochar for durable carbon storage and carbon-removal credits, alongside side projects in tree-planting ('Tiny Forests') and international biochar agriculture trials.
description: A Healthier Earth (AHE) is a UK climate-tech subsidiary of Pure Data Centres Group (Pure DC) that develops and operates industrial-scale biochar carbon removal. Its £24M PureBiochar facility in Royal Wootton Bassett, Wiltshire — billed as the UK's largest biochar plant — uses PYREG PX6000/PX1500/P500 pyrolysis systems and is designed to produce up to 11,500 tonnes of biochar and remove up to 18,500 tonnes of CO2 annually. Phase 1 commissioning began in November 2025 with production slated to start the same month.

name: A startup using minerals to draw down CO2 has scored funding – and its first buyer
ACT Group
tech_note: Biochar
description: ACT Group is a sustainability solutions provider that offers decarbonization products and services, including biochar projects, to help organizations reduce and mitigate their carbon footprint.

name: ADM
tech_note: BECCS
description: ADM operates a large-scale Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Storage (BECCS) facility in Decatur, Illinois, capturing CO2 from its corn-to-ethanol plant and sequestering it.

name: ADNOC
tech_note: ADNOC, via its investment arm XRG, co-develops megaton-scale DAC facilities with Occidental/1PointFive in both the UAE and South Texas, and is building CO2 sequestration infrastructure including a fully sequestered CO2 injection well in a carbonate saline aquifer in Abu Dhabi.
description: ADNOC is Abu Dhabi's state-owned energy and petrochemicals group that has entered CDR through joint ventures with Occidental and 1PointFive to develop Direct Air Capture facilities and CO2 storage infrastructure. In May 2025, its investment company XRG signed a Strategic DAC Framework Agreement to consider investing up to $500 million in a 500,000 tpa DAC facility in South Texas, alongside an earlier Joint Study Agreement for a 1 Mtpa DAC plant in the UAE linked to ADNOC's CO2 infrastructure. While ADNOC's main business remains hydrocarbons, its active co-development of DAC capacity and dedicated sequestration wells places it as a CDR division/supplier in this directory.

name: AEROC
tech_note: Spreads crushed basalt rock flour on agricultural fields in Germany to accelerate silicate weathering, forming bicarbonates that sequester atmospheric CO2.
description: AEROC (Aeroc GmbH) is a German startup based in Cologne that develops and scales Enhanced Rock Weathering (ERW) projects by spreading basalt rock flour on agricultural fields to permanently remove CO2 while improving soil quality and crop yields. The company handles procurement, logistics, application, and MRV of the ERW process and works with farmers via a participation model.

name: APChemi
tech_note: APChemi designs and supplies proprietary PYROMAX biomass pyrolysis reactors that convert agricultural and woody biomass waste into biochar for carbon sequestration and CDR carbon credits.
description: APChemi is an Indian pyrolysis technology company offering biomass-to-biochar plants alongside plastic and tire pyrolysis systems. <cite index="3-5">In April 2025 it partnered with PRESPL and Intellecap to set up Biochar India Private Limited (BiocharIND), intended to be India's largest biochar-based carbon credit platform</cite>, with a <cite index="7-5">first facility in Punjab-Haryana producing 10,000 MT of biochar per annum and generating ~25,000 tCO2e of carbon credits per annum</cite>.

name: APD
tech_note: Operates certified pyrolysis plants converting Swiss green-waste biomass into biochar for soil amendment and animal feed, generating biochar carbon removal credits.
description: APD (Auen Pflege Dienst AG) is a Swiss company based in Flaach, Zürich, that produces biochar via certified pyrolysis plants using local biomass feedstocks. It is one of the earliest biochar carbon-credit projects (operating since 2019) and partners with First Climate for credit issuance, with annual audits by Carbon Standards International (EBC certification).

name: ARC
tech_note: BECCS
description: ARC (Amager Resource Center) is a Danish company that operates a waste-to-energy plant and implements BECCS (Bio-Energy with Carbon Capture and Storage) by capturing CO₂ from its operations.

name: ASF GmbH
tech_note: Municipal waste utility that carbonizes regional green-cuttings into biochar via its own on-site pyrolysis unit, selling the resulting char to the agricultural sector.
description: ASF GmbH (Abfallwirtschaft und Stadtreinigung Freiburg GmbH) is the municipal waste management and street cleaning company for the city of Freiburg, Germany, jointly owned by the city (53%) and Remondis (47%). Alongside its core waste-management business, ASF operates its own pyrolysis plant producing biochar from regional green cuttings for agricultural use. Biochar production is a side activity of a ~400-employee municipal utility rather than a dedicated CDR company.

name: AWN
tech_note: Municipal pyrolysis of woody green-waste fraction into biochar used in compost/Terra Preta products and for agriculture and livestock.
description: AWN (Abfallwirtschaftsgesellschaft des Neckar-Odenwald-Kreises mbH) is a municipal waste-management company in Buchen, Germany, which operates the Biomassezentrum at the Sansenhecken disposal center. Among compost and Terra Preta substrates, they pyrolyze the woody fraction of roughly 20,000 tonnes of regional green waste per year into biochar for agricultural and livestock use. While waste management is their core mandate, they physically produce biochar and thus act as a CDR supplier at a small, municipal scale.

name: Abatable
tech_note: Carbon credit procurement platform helping companies source and evaluate high-quality carbon credits.
description: Abatable is a CDR platform and marketplace that provides access to carbon market data, intelligence, and tools to help companies procure high-quality carbon offsets and manage their climate strategies.

name: Absolute Climate
tech_note: Independent standards-setter and quality-assurance provider for CDR credits; develops the Absolute Carbon Standard (ACS) and MRV methodologies applied across pathways, with credit issuance handled by partner registries such as Evident's C-Capsule.
description: <cite index="9-9,9-10">Absolute Climate designs independent quality-assurance standards for CDR that certify whether a project's claims match their atmospheric impacts, with a universal approach where every removal project is evaluated the same way across all pathways.</cite> <cite index="9-21,9-22,9-23">The company separates quality assurance from credit issuance — it builds standards but does not operate its own registry.</cite> It partners with registries (e.g., Evident/C-Capsule) and financial infrastructure providers (Northern Trust) and certifies projects such as Cowboy Clean Fuels and Vesta.

name: Accend
tech_note: Consultancy providing LCA/MRV services and credit brokerage for biochar and mass-timber producers pursuing Puro.earth CORC certification.
description: Accend is a Norwegian consultancy/broker (founded 2020, based in Fredrikstad) that helps biochar and mass-timber producers in Europe and North America qualify for Puro.earth CORC certification through LCA services, and then brokers the resulting carbon removal credits to corporate buyers. They do not operate pyrolysis plants themselves — their clients (OBIO, Biopower Tana, Moelven) are the physical CDR suppliers.

name: Actanol Energie
tech_note: Operates and contracts pyrolysis plants (CarboForce/Carbo-CAP-TEC technology) that convert biomass into biochar, heat, and electricity, generating CO2 removal certificates.
description: ACTANOL Energie GmbH is a German (Kempten, Allgäu) company focused on planning, financing and operating pyrolysis plants for renewable energy and biochar production. It offers contracting models for pyrolysis installations and is a member of the German Biochar e.V. network.

name: Adaptavate
tech_note: Adaptavate manufactures carbon-negative plasterboard ("Breathaboard") by binding ligno-cellulosic crop wastes with minerals that absorb CO2 during curing, and incorporates biochar from pyrolysis to lock biogenic carbon into the building material permanently.
description: Bristol, UK-based construction materials company that has developed a drop-in, carbon-storing alternative to gypsum plasterboard. The technology combines CO2 absorption during mineral curing with biochar incorporation to achieve permanent carbon storage in buildings, and the company licenses its platform to global manufacturers.

name: Adsorb Carbon
tech_note: Biochar
description: Adsorb Carbon is a South African manufacturer of premium activated carbon products sourced from sustainably grown wood, sawmill residues, and invasive vegetation. While they produce activated carbon, the search results do not explicitly state they are involved in biochar-based carbon dioxide removal (CDR).

name: Advanced Cooling Technologies
tech_note: Solid sorbent DAC
description: Advanced Cooling Technologies (ACT) is developing a novel acid/base ion-exchange direct air capture (DAC) process using a hydroxide-coated amine solid sorbent, which has demonstrated high CO₂ capture rates and low-temperature thermal regeneration.

name: Aemetis
tech_note: Through its Aemetis Carbon Capture subsidiary, the company plans to capture and sequester biogenic CO2 from dairy digesters, ethanol, and renewable jet/diesel production into a Class VI injection well at its Riverbank, California site.
description: <cite index="8-14,8-15,8-16">Aemetis is a renewable natural gas, renewable fuel and biochemicals company headquartered in Cupertino, California, operating a dairy biogas digester network and a 65-million-gallon-per-year ethanol facility in the Central Valley.</cite> Its Aemetis Carbon Capture subsidiary is developing BECCS projects — <cite index="9-11">engineering and permitting two CCS injection well projects to capture, dehydrate, compress, and sequester CO2 from the Aemetis Biogas anaerobic dairy digester projects, the Aemetis biofuel plants, and CO2 from oil refineries in California.</cite> <cite index="6-3">In 2023 the subsidiary was awarded the first CO2 sequestration characterization well permit issued by the State of California.</cite>

name: Aeon Blue
tech_note: Liquid solvent DAC
description: Aeon Blue develops eFuel using direct air capture (DAC) with a liquid solvent (cold capture via chloralkali technology) to produce carbon-absorbing commodities and renewable hydrocarbons.

name: Aerleum
tech_note: DAC-powered sustainable aviation fuel company.
description: Aerleum is a climate tech company that uses a proprietary dual-functional material to capture CO2 directly from the atmosphere and convert it into high-value commodities like fuels and chemicals.

name: Ag Carbon Solutions
tech_note: TSB
description: Ag Carbon Solutions uses a "Dry Decay Method" to convert clean, carbonaceous waste streams into soil amendments, which capture and sequester carbon dioxide and nitrates in the ground and soil.

name: AgroCCS
tech_note: Biochar
description: AgroCCS is a BiCRS company that transforms agricultural waste into biochar using advanced pyrolysis technology to sequester carbon, enhance soil health, and generate certified CO₂ removal credits.

name: AiS
tech_note: Operates a slow-pyrolysis plant coupled to a heating center that converts biomass into biochar for agricultural/circular-economy use.
description: AiS (Arbeit in Selbsthilfe gGmbH) is a German non-profit inclusion enterprise based in Bodelshausen that primarily provides employment to people with disabilities across multiple work areas (agriculture, gastronomy, retail, landscaping). As part of its Kastanienhof site it operates a heating center with a pyrolysis plant that produces biochar within a regional circular-economy concept, though biochar is a side activity rather than its core mission.

name: Air View Engineering
tech_note: Solid sorbent DAC
description: Air View Engineering Ltd is a Direct Air Capture (DAC) startup that aims to provide smaller, more cost-efficient solid sorbent carbon capture solutions to increase their use globally.

name: Air to Earth
tech_note: Solid sorbent DAC
description: AIR TO EARTH® is a developer of industrial gas infrastructure, specializing in purifying CO2 to high-grade pipeline and beverage grade specification, for use or sequestration, and is a CDR credit supplier.

name: AirMyne
tech_note: Liquid-solvent DAC using a proprietary low-temperature thermal regeneration process that can be powered by geothermal heat, waste heat, or electricity.
description: <cite index="9-7,9-8,9-9">AirMyne is a next-generation Direct Air Capture company whose patented process uses a liquid capture agent and a low-temperature thermal regeneration process that can integrate with various low-carbon energy sources.</cite> <cite index="2-17">The company was selected for two DOE Regional DAC Hub projects, including the Red Rocks DAC Hub led by Fervo Energy and the CALDAC Hub led by UC Berkeley.</cite> <cite index="1-3">AirMyne is planning its DeltaDAC initial project for deployment in the Port of Stockton with support from the California Energy Commission.</cite>

name: AirZyme
tech_note: BECCS
description: AirZyme is a climate tech company that enhances carbon capture and removal technologies, specifically BECCS and Bio-DAC, by leveraging the enzyme Carbonic Anhydrase to transform CO2 into bicarbonate.

name: Airbuild
tech_note: Biochar
description: Airbuild is a climate infrastructure company that utilizes microalgae and pyrolysis to clean polluted water and permanently remove carbon by transforming algae biomass and organic waste into biochar.

name: Airbus
tech_note: Modular solid amine-based DAC system derived from Airbus Defence and Space's ISS life-support technology, using temperature-swing regeneration with heat-recovery energy loop; first commercial 250 tCO2/year unit deployed at Deep Sky Alpha, Alberta in late 2025.
description: Airbus, through its Defence and Space division, has commercialized a modular Direct Air Capture unit derived from International Space Station life-support technology, using a solid amine-based filter with thermal regeneration. In November 2025, Airbus delivered a 250 ton/year DAC unit to Deep Sky Alpha in Alberta, Canada, marking its first operational deployment. Airbus also purchases DAC credits from 1PointFive (400,000 tonnes pre-purchase) and resells them to airlines via its Carbon Capture Offer.

name: Aircapture
tech_note: Solid sorbent DAC
description: Aircapture develops modular, onsite Direct Air Capture (DAC) units that use a proprietary Amine-functionalized solid sorbent to capture CO2 from the atmosphere, which can then be converted into liquid CO2 or dry ice for industrial and retail use.

name: Airex Energy
tech_note: Airex Energy develops proprietary CarbonFX torrefaction/pyrolysis technology and operates industrial biochar plants that convert forestry biomass residues into biochar, biocarbon, and biocoal for carbon sequestration and industrial use.
description: <cite index="1-16,1-17">Airex Energy is a Canadian biochar supplier that uses its patented CarbonFX™ technology to transform biomass into biochar, biocarbon and biocoal, and has operated Canada's first industrial biochar production plant since 2016.</cite> Through its Carbonity joint venture with SUEZ and Groupe Rémabec, <cite index="2-17,2-18,2-19">the Port-Cartier facility is ramping up to 10,000 tonnes/year and will ultimately produce up to 30,000 tonnes of biochar annually, representing roughly 75,000 tonnes of CO₂ permanently removed from the atmosphere each year.</cite> <cite index="2-10">The project secured a three-year forward offtake agreement with Microsoft for 36,000 carbon credits, with the first credits delivered in 2025 after Puro.earth certification.</cite>

name: Airfix
tech_note: BECCS project developer and CO₂ transport/storage structurer working with biogenic emitters (biogas, waste-to-energy) to deliver permanent geological storage of biogenic CO₂.
description: Airfix is a Swiss subsidiary of South Pole, backed by the Migros Pioneer Fund, focused on activating the European BECCS (Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Storage) market. It acts as a project developer and CO₂ transport/storage structurer for biogenic emitters, enabling BECCS projects such as the CO2 Energie AG biogas plant near Zurich and a cross-border storage deal with INEOS Greensand announced in January 2026.

name: Airhive
tech_note: Fluidised-bed DAC reactor using a low-cost geochemical metal-oxide sorbent with electric calcination for CO2 release, deployed in modular container-sized 1,000 t/yr units.
description: <cite index="4-2">Airhive, founded in 2022, is a UK-based DAC company developing a low-cost, energy-efficient and rapidly scalable technology to capture carbon from the atmosphere.</cite> <cite index="1-5,1-6">Its system uses a novel DAC method based on fluidised beds, a proven industrial technology, and the speed and efficiency of this fluidisation-based capture method, combined with heat recovery and reuse, helps Airhive lower costs.</cite> <cite index="1-9,1-10">Airhive's 1,000-tonne-per-year system is one of the largest operational DAC systems in the world and is operating as part of Deep Sky Alpha, a cross-technology DAC hub in Innisfail, Alberta.</cite>

name: Alcom
tech_note: Biochar
description: Alcom is a Singapore-based BiCRS company that converts agricultural waste into high-quality biochar, delivering durable carbon removals and producing bio-oil, electricity, and heat.

name: Alithic
tech_note: Liquid solvent DAC
description: Alithic develops an energy-efficient Direct Air Capture (DAC) system that uses a liquid solvent (sodium carbonate aqueous solution) to capture CO2, which is then mineralized with industrial solid wastes to produce valuable CaCO₃.

name: Alkali Earth
tech_note: Carbon mineralization via spreading reactive steel slag aggregates in gravel roadbeds, where CO2 precipitates as carbonate minerals for permanent storage.
description: Alkali Earth was a US-based CDR startup that attempted to commercialize carbon mineralization using steel slag aggregates in gravel roadbeds. The company has wound down operations after finding its approach difficult to commercialize, and is now publishing its learnings openly for the CDR community.

name: Alpine X
tech_note: Solid-sorbent DAC using metal-organic framework (MOF) pellets in a vertical reactor column, designed to operate at high-altitude Alpine sites (>1500m) where cold, dry air and strong solar insolation enhance adsorption efficiency and power the system.
description: Alpine X is a France-based direct air capture startup developing compact, modular DAC units optimized for high-altitude mountain deployment. <cite index="1-5,1-6,1-7">The company pairs altitude-optimized conditions with MOF materials that work better at low temperatures and low humidity naturally found at high altitude.</cite> <cite index="2-3,2-7,2-8">The technology is currently in an early pilot phase, moving from research into real-world operation with initial modular systems being tested under Alpine conditions.</cite>

name: Alt Carbon
tech_note: Spreads waste basalt rock dust on tea estates and croplands, using multi-layer MRV (soil, groundwater, river sampling plus reactive transport and ML models) to quantify CO2 removal.
description: Alt Carbon is an India-based CDR supplier deploying Enhanced Rock Weathering by spreading basalt rock dust from the Rajmahal Traps on tea estates and farm fields in Darjeeling/eastern India. The company raised a $12M seed round in May 2025 (India's largest climate-tech seed), holds a Frontier $500K prepurchase, a NextGen offtake, and a 10,000-ton MOL Group agreement, and is delivering its first credits via Isometric.

name: Altitude Carbon
tech_note: CDR financier and offtake aggregator that signs forward purchase agreements for Puro-certified biochar CORCs from third-party project developers.
description: Altitude Carbon is a Switzerland-based CDR financier that procures biochar carbon removal credits (CORCs) from project developers globally, including facilities in Argentina, West Africa, and Southeast Asia. They do not physically remove CO2 themselves but operate a purchasing facility (Ascent 1) to provide offtake financing to biochar CDR developers. Their entire business exists to scale the CDR market through capital deployment, placing them squarely in the CDR ecosystem.

name: Alto
tech_note: Corn-ethanol producer partnering with Vault 44.01 to capture biogenic fermentation CO2 at its Pekin, IL plant and inject it into the Mt. Simon sandstone formation for permanent geologic storage.
description: Alto Ingredients (NASDAQ: ALTO), formerly Pacific Ethanol, is a U.S. producer of specialty alcohols and renewable fuels based in Pekin, Illinois. The company is developing a BECCS project with Vault 44.01 to capture ~600,000 metric tons/year of biogenic CO2 from corn fermentation at its Pekin campus and permanently sequester it in the Mt. Simon sandstone formation. The CCS project has been delayed by Illinois SB 1723 (signed Aug 2025) and may not start generating revenue until 2029-2030.

name: American BioCarbon
tech_note: Pyrolyzes sugarcane bagasse (waste from Cora Texas Sugar Mill in White Castle, LA) into biochar soil amendment and renewable fuel pellets using a patented Biomass Separation Unit.
description: American BioCarbon is a Louisiana-based biochar producer that transforms sugarcane bagasse from the co-located Cora Texas Sugar Mill into biochar and fuel pellets. It is Puro.earth-certified, currently generates ~3,000 CORCs/year from a pilot plant, and is building a larger commercial facility slated to go live in 2026.

name: American BioChar Company
tech_note: Biochar
description: American BioChar Company produces and sells biochar blends in liquid and granular forms, as well as pure biochar, for soil amendment to improve plant health and sequester carbon.

name: Andes
tech_note: Andes applies beneficial microorganisms alongside crop seeds on agricultural fields to accelerate conversion of atmospheric CO2 into stable soil carbonate minerals via microbially-enhanced silicate weathering.
description: <cite index="10-2">Andes is a carbon removal company focused on the generation of inorganic carbon in agricultural soils</cite>, headquartered in Alameda, CA. <cite index="3-9">Andes has partnered with Gold Standard to release the world's first CDR methodology based on microbial carbon dioxide mineralization in agricultural fields.</cite> <cite index="14-12">The company has raised $38M to date</cite> and deploys microbes across tens of thousands of acres of Midwestern US farmland.

name: Anew Climate
tech_note: Anew Climate is a carbon project developer and marketer/trader specializing in Improved Forest Management (IFM) nature-based removals plus a multi-pathway portfolio including BECCS (via Summit Carbon Solutions marketing agreement), climate-smart agriculture, and avoidance credits.
description: <cite index="8-1">Anew Climate was formed through the combination of Element Markets and Bluesource</cite> and is a Houston-based carbon project developer and credit marketer majority-owned by TPG Rise. <cite index="2-3,2-10">They were the first to develop and transact improved forest management (IFM) carbon dioxide removal credits, with verified credits spanning IFM, grasslands, wildfire mitigation, climate-smart agriculture, and afforestation/reforestation.</cite> They also market BECCS credits from Summit Carbon Solutions' bioethanol CCS project and have signed major offtake deals with Microsoft.

name: Anglo American
tech_note: Applies magnesium-rich ferronickel slag (a mining by-product) to Brazilian agricultural soils to accelerate silicate weathering, drawing down CO2 as bicarbonate while providing fertiliser co-benefits.
description: Anglo American is a major global mining company running Project Earthstone in Brazil, which uses magnesium-rich ferronickel slag from its mining operations as feedstock for Enhanced Rock Weathering on agricultural land. In September 2025 Anglo American partnered with Isometric (registry) and ZeroEx (MRV) to issue verified Enhanced Weathering credits, with stockpiles estimated to have potential for up to 15 million tonnes of CO2 removal.

name: AntMind
tech_note: Gasifies forestry/wood waste to produce hydrogen energy while capturing CO2 (for underground storage) and producing biochar as a stable carbon byproduct.
description: AntMind is a Canadian startup developing a biomass gasification platform that converts wood waste into hydrogen fuel while capturing CO2 for sequestration and producing biochar as a stable carbon byproduct. The company is currently in a funding phase and designing a pilot facility to process waste from a single sawmill.

name: Anvil
tech_note: Anvil uses a low-energy reactor to contact highly reactive alkaline-bearing ores with atmospheric CO2, accelerating mineralization into stable solid carbonate minerals stored durably on-site.
description: Anvil Capture Systems is a US-based (New York/Somerville, MA) carbon dioxide removal company developing direct-air mineralization using alkaline-bearing ores in a proprietary low-energy reactor. The company received a Frontier prepurchase in Fall 2024 and was awarded a MassCEC climatetech grant in 2025, and is a Greentown Labs member.

name: Aperam
tech_note: Aperam BioEnergia pyrolyzes eucalyptus biomass from its FSC-certified plantations in Minas Gerais, Brazil, and applies the resulting biochar to soil as a durable carbon removal, selling CORCs via Puro.earth.
description: Aperam BioEnergia is the Brazilian forestry/renewable-energy subsidiary of global stainless-steel producer Aperam, historically supplying charcoal to Aperam's Timóteo steel plant and, since 2022, marketing biochar-based carbon removal credits. It is Puro.earth-certified and one of the largest biochar CDR suppliers globally, producing ~10,000 t biochar/yr in 2025 with plans to scale further. The company has sold 100,000+ tonnes of CDR credits, mostly through Puro.earth.

name: Applied Carbon
tech_note: Builds a tractor-pulled mobile pyrolyzer that collects agricultural crop residues and converts them into biochar in a single pass in the field, applying the biochar back onto the soil.
description: Applied Carbon (formerly Climate Robotics) is a Houston-based biochar supplier that deploys automated in-field pyrolysis machines to convert crop waste into biochar for durable carbon removal and soil health benefits. The company has raised a $21.5M Series A led by TO VC with participation from Microsoft Climate Innovation Fund, Congruent Ventures, and Elemental Excelerator, and is an XPRIZE Carbon Removal finalist and DOE CDR Purchase Pilot semifinalist. It sells biochar carbon removal credits including to Microsoft's portfolio and is registered with Puro.earth.

name: Applied Gaia
tech_note: Biochar
description: Applied Gaia specializes in the design, manufacture, and sale of pyrolysis machines and technology for converting biomass into high-carbon biochar, a method for carbon dioxide removal (CDR). They also offer engineering and full system project design for profitable biochar operations.

name: Aquafin
tech_note: Pyrolysis of municipal wastewater sewage sludge into biochar for permanent carbon storage, co-developed with partner companies at the RWZI Menen plant.
description: Aquafin is Belgium's Flemish wastewater treatment utility, established in 1990, which treats household wastewater across Flanders. The company is developing a biochar project at its RWZI Menen site, in partnership with Ebema, D-CRBN, and Stadsbader Group, that will pyrolyze sewage sludge into biochar. While wastewater treatment is its core business, the Menen biochar plant represents a CDR-producing division/project within the larger utility.

name: Aquarry
tech_note: Dissolves alkaline minerals (e.g. crushed kimberlite) into flooded post-mining pit lakes to drive CO2 uptake and precipitation of carbonate minerals that sink to the lake bottom for durable storage.
description: Aquarry is a US-based deep-tech CDR startup (founded 2023, Denver/California) applying pit lake alkalinity enhancement — a hybrid of enhanced rock weathering and ocean alkalinity enhancement — to flooded open-pit mines. The process uses alkaline tailings/waste rock to raise lake alkalinity, absorb atmospheric CO2, and form stable carbonates while remediating mine water. The company is partnered with Winsome Resources at the Renard site in Quebec and with Isometric as registry, with limited-scale field trials planned for spring 2026.

name: Aramco/Siemens Energy
tech_note: N/A DAC tech
description: Aramco, in partnership with Siemens Energy, launched Saudi Arabia's first Direct Air Capture (DAC) test unit, capable of removing 12 tons of CO2. Aramco is also involved in other carbon capture collaborations.

name: Arbon
tech_note: Arbon develops a humidity-swing (moisture-swing) solid sorbent Direct Air Capture technology that captures CO2 in dry conditions and releases it when wet, avoiding heat-based regeneration.
description: Arbon is a Brooklyn, NY-based DAC startup spun out of Columbia University, developing humidity-swing sorbent technology for atmospheric CO2 capture. The company has a Frontier Climate offtake contract (2023) and was selected into the Activate Fellows 2025 cohort. It is small (~5 employees) but clearly an early-stage CDR technology supplier.

name: Arbon Earth
tech_note: Biomass sinking
description: Arbon Earth is a marine-based Carbon Dioxide Removal (CDR) company that removes CO₂ from the atmosphere by cultivating and sequestering macroalgae in the deep ocean.

name: Arbor
tech_note: BECCS
description: Arbor is a BiCRS company that uses a novel BECCS (Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Storage) system to convert waste biomass into synthetic gas, producing low-carbon heat and electricity while capturing and storing CO2.

name: Arca
tech_note: Arca accelerates surficial carbon mineralization in ultramafic mine tailings and other alkaline industrial waste using autonomous Smart Churning rovers and microwave-based mineral activation, with on-site MRV.
description: Arca (Arca Climate Technologies Inc.), headquartered in Vancouver, BC, is a carbon mineralization supplier that repurposes alkaline industrial waste such as ultramafic mine tailings to permanently store atmospheric CO2 as carbonate rock. The company completed an 18-month pilot at BHP's Mt. Keith nickel mine in Western Australia, has an ISO 14064-2 DNV-validated methodology, and signed a 10-year ~300,000-tonne offtake agreement with Microsoft in October 2025.

name: Aries Clean Technologies
tech_note: Aries operates patented fluidized bed and downdraft gasification systems that convert wastewater biosolids and wood waste into syngas energy and biochar, which is used as a concrete additive and soil amendment for carbon sequestration.
description: <cite index="2-11,2-12">Aries Clean Technologies, based in Franklin, Tennessee, develops, designs, and builds proprietary fluidized bed and downdraft gasification systems that convert biosolids and biomass into clean thermal and electrical energy plus Aries GREEN biochar or Bio-Fly-Ash.</cite> <cite index="9-4,9-5">The biochar product is used as an ingredient in green concrete manufacturing and offers permanent carbon sequestration.</cite> <cite index="8-8,8-9">Their first large plant in Linden, NJ operated intermittently for a year before being idled in late 2025 for drier technology upgrades, while the company advances a new $180M Sanford, Maine facility.</cite>

name: Arigna Fuels
tech_note: Produces biochar via pyrolysis/torrefaction of biomass residues (including olive stones) at a Roscommon facility, selling Harvest Flame biochar briquettes as a smokeless fuel alternative and biochar for agriculture/horticulture.
description: Arigna Fuels (part of Arigna Group) is an Irish fifth-generation family firm that transitioned from coal mining/smokeless fuel manufacture to biochar production. It operates what has been described as one of Europe's largest biochar production facilities in Co. Roscommon, producing biochar for fuel (Harvest Flame), horticulture, construction and carbon sequestration applications.

name: Arkansas biochar facility to open in early 2026
Arrhenius
tech_note: Grows microalgae in outdoor photobioreactors using sunlight, then buries the biomass geologically for permanent CO2 storage.
description: <cite index="1-2">Arrhenius AG is a spin-off of Lucerne University of Applied Sciences and Arts</cite> based in Switzerland that <cite index="1-3">permanently removes CO2 from the atmosphere by growing and burying microalgae biomass</cite>. The company is pursuing a pilot plant, <cite index="6-9,6-10">identifying sites in Portugal with Algae for Future SA (A4F), with two locations identified in Lisbon and Matacães</cite>, and plans to adapt an existing reactor for ~2 years of microalgae cultivation data collection.

name: Arukah
tech_note: Arukah operates biochar pyrolysis plants (claiming the largest in Southeast Asia, in Cambodia) converting agricultural waste into durable biochar, alongside household/industrial biogas digesters, with a proprietary dMRV stack for carbon credit issuance.
description: <cite index="5-9,5-10">Arukah has commissioned Southeast Asia's largest biochar plant in Cambodia together with local partners, transforming agricultural by-products into durable carbon removal and climate-smart fertiliser, while allocating 50% of gross carbon credit revenues to participating smallholder farmers.</cite> The Singapore-headquartered firm also deploys household biodigesters and operates a digital MRV platform (CarbonCast) using IoT sensors and computer vision to track biomass and issue high-integrity carbon credits.

name: Ashwood Biochar
tech_note: Produces wood-based biochar via pyrolysis from sustainable woody biomass waste, sold in bulk and granulated forms for soil amendment and carbon sequestration.
description: <cite index="10-1,10-4">Ashwood Biochar produces carbon-rich biochar from 100% sustainable woody biomass waste in Lexington, Kentucky, used as a soil amendment to improve fertility, water retention, and as a method of permanent carbon sequestration.</cite> <cite index="2-1,2-2">They supply large volumes of wood-based biochar in the Southeast US, offering both bulk and granulated products.</cite> The company is part of Ashwood Trinity, which invests in soil health and biochar projects and operates a farmer sign-up program offering per-acre incentives.

name: AspiraDAC/Corporate Carbon
tech_note: Solid sorbent DAC
description: AspiraDAC is an Australian company that develops and deploys modular, scalable, solar-powered Direct Air Capture (DAC) technology using solid sorbents to remove CO2 directly from the air.

name: Atalanta Climate
tech_note: Compact indoor DAC appliance using next-generation solid sorbents that automatically regenerate and convert captured CO₂ into a stable mineral for permanent storage.
description: Atalanta Climate is a Vancouver, Canada-based climate-tech startup that designs compact, plug-and-play direct air capture devices (their first product is called Ovi) for homes and offices. The units use solid sorbents to capture indoor CO₂ and mineralize it into limestone-like rock dust for permanent storage, while also acting as air purifiers.

name: AtmosClear
tech_note: BECCS
description: AtmosClear is a BiCRS company that uses Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Storage (BECCS) to remove carbon dioxide. They have a major contract with Microsoft to deliver 6.75 million metric tons of engineered carbon removal over 15 years from their planned facility in Louisiana.

name: Atmosfuture Limited
tech_note: Cryogenic DAC
description: Atmosfuture Limited develops REVFRACC, a novel Direct Air Capture (DAC) system that uses a cryogenic method to capture CO2 without requiring a fan, while also providing renewable energy for data centers.

name: Atoco
tech_note: Atoco develops solid-state sorbent modules based on metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) and covalent organic frameworks (COFs) for Direct Air Capture and post-combustion capture, alongside atmospheric water harvesting.
description: <cite index="15-2">Atoco is a California-based startup founded by Omar Yaghi in 2020 focused on commercializing advancements in MOF and COF technologies for carbon capture and atmospheric water harvesting.</cite> The company develops solid-state DAC and post-combustion capture modules using nano-engineered reticular materials, and its founder won the 2025 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for the development of MOFs. <cite index="19-8">The startup is also targeting data centers in water-stressed regions as customers for its water-harvesting technology.</cite>

name: Avnos
tech_note: Hybrid DAC using moisture-swing solid sorbents that capture CO2 and co-produce clean water without requiring external heat.
description: Avnos is a Los Angeles-based Direct Air Capture company developing its proprietary Hybrid Direct Air Capture (HDAC) technology, which uses moisture-swing sorbents to capture CO2 while co-producing clean water and eliminating the need for external heat input. The company operates a pilot in Bakersfield, CA, an R&D center in Bridgewater, NJ, and in November 2025 announced Project Cedar, a commercial-scale facility backed by $17M from Shell and Mitsubishi, scheduled to come online by end of 2026.

name: Aymium
tech_note: Biochar
description: Aymium produces high-value biocarbon and biohydrogen products from renewable biomass, serving as a carbon-negative alternative to traditional fuels for industries like metals. Their CDR method involves biochar production.

name: B10
tech_note: Pyrolysis of timber/biomass waste in automated continuous kilns to produce biochar sold as agricultural soil amendment, generating carbon removal credits.
description: B10 (B10 Char) is a biochar producer with a Swiss holding (B10 Char Trading AG) and operations in South Africa. Its first pyrolysis plant near Nelspruit became operational in Q3 2025 with capacity of around 6,000-7,000 tonnes of biochar per year from timber waste, equivalent to roughly 15,000 tCO2 sequestered annually. The company plans to generate most of its revenue from carbon credits while distributing biochar to farmers.

name: BAIE Minerals
tech_note: Develops ex-situ carbon mineralization technology that processes asbestos mine tailings from the Baie Verte, Newfoundland site to produce magnesium oxide which absorbs CO2 and forms stable magnesium carbonate, alongside extracting silica and other critical minerals.
description: <cite index="5-15,5-17,5-18,5-19">BAIE Minerals is a Canadian startup extracting critical minerals from mining waste and using what's left over to draw CO2 from the atmosphere, by leveraging magnesium-rich ultramafic tailings that react with atmospheric CO2 to form magnesium carbonate and permanently sequester carbon.</cite> <cite index="5-8,5-9,5-10">Their process produces high-purity magnesium oxide that absorbs 1.1 tons of CO2 per ton of material within hours; the pilot facility currently processes around 200 pounds of tailings an hour and the company aims to build a full-scale facility in 2027.</cite> Business model combines carbon removal credits with sales of extracted minerals for cement and fertilizer.

name: BC Biocarbon
tech_note: Uses a proprietary continuous-feed pyrolysis/gasification biorefinery to convert wood residuals into biochar (Black Bear Biochar), generating Puro.earth-certified CORCs.
description: BC Biocarbon is a Canadian biochar producer based in McBride, British Columbia, that transforms forest and sawmill wood residuals into biochar via a proprietary continuous pyrolysis process. Its Black Bear Biochar is sold as an OMRI-listed soil amendment (including through Walmart, Menards and Home Depot soil mixes) and generates Puro.earth-certified carbon removal credits. The company is co-developing a biorefinery in Carrot River, Saskatchewan, through the BioLesna JV with Dunkley Lumber, backed by $10M from Natural Resources Canada.

name: BCHAR
tech_note: BCHAR designs and sells automated, turn-key industrial-scale pyrolysis systems that convert agricultural waste into biochar, bundled with proprietary MRV software for carbon-credit generation.
description: <cite index="3-1,3-4">BCHAR is a Zurich-based developer of biochar carbon removal technologies that transforms bio-waste into biochar, and offers services for project setup, technology delivery, MRV, and carbon credit sales.</cite> <cite index="2-5,2-6,2-7">The company launched its first biochar system in Thailand using coconut husks as feedstock as a pilot project, with insights being incorporated into an upcoming full-scale system.</cite> <cite index="6-6,3-11">Founded in 2023 and based in Zurich, Switzerland, BCHAR has raised $743K from VC investors including Riceberg Ventures, BlueLion Incubator, SICTIC, Rockstart, and Founderful Campus.</cite>

name: BIOCHAR GmbH
tech_note: Pyrolytic carbonization of wood chips into biochar at an industrial plant near Leipzig, with syngas-driven process energy recovery.
description: BIOCHAR GmbH & Co. KG is a German biochar producer part of the CONVORIS Unternehmensgruppe, operating a pyrolysis facility at the Reuden/Draschwitz industrial park near Leipzig. They produce biochar from natural wood feedstocks (softwood chips from German forestry) using BEHORE Technology pyrolysis plants, with syngas recovered as process heat and power. Primary market is agriculture (feed additive, soil amendment) and they are listed as a Puro.earth registered producer.

name: BLOCK
tech_note: Operates a Carbo-FORCE partial-oxidation pyrolysis plant converting regional hedgerow cuttings, waste wood and agricultural residues into biochar for soil application and permanent carbon storage.
description: BLOCK Pflanzenkohle (BLOCK Bio Innovationen GmbH & Co. KG) is a family-run German biochar producer in Osterrade, Dithmarschen, Schleswig-Holstein, founded by brothers Mathis and Steffen Block. Their facility is designed to produce roughly 550 tonnes of biochar per year from ~2,000 tonnes of regional biomass, with waste heat feeding a local district heating network. Carbon removal credits from the project are distributed via Klimate.co.

name: Bakz4ever
tech_note: Cryogenic + membrane-separation DAC coupled with long-duration energy storage, producing solid CO2 intended for ocean storage.
description: <cite index="2-1">Founded in 2021, Bakz4ever is an early-stage Indian climate-tech startup</cite> (OPC Pvt Ltd) developing cryogenic direct air capture integrated with long-duration energy storage. <cite index="2-3">The business model has two revenue streams: energy-storage-as-a-service for renewable grid operators, and carbon removal certificates generated by capturing CO2 in solid state and placing it in the ocean for permanent storage</cite>. The company appears to be at the concept/prototype stage with ~2 employees, no registry-issued credits, and minimal recent public activity.

name: Banyu Carbon
tech_note: Uses sunlight-activated reversible photoacids to release CO2 from seawater, enabling the ocean to reabsorb atmospheric CO2.
description: <cite index="7-7,7-8">Banyu Carbon is a Seattle-based company founded in 2022 by Alex Gagnon and Julian Sachs, former University of Washington professors of chemical oceanography, developing a sunlight-driven process to strip CO2 from seawater.</cite> <cite index="6-4">The company has raised a $6.5 million seed round from investors including the Grantham Foundation, Propeller, United Airlines Ventures, Carbon Removal Partners and ReGen Ventures.</cite> It is an Ocean CDR supplier physically removing CO2 via photochemical reactions.

name: Basic Dust
tech_note: ERW
description: Basic Dust applies finely pulverized alkaline rock powder to water and land to mineralize carbon dioxide into bicarbonates, utilizing enhanced rock weathering for carbon removal.

name: Basna
tech_note: Basna produces biochar via pyrolysis of wooden biomass at its Čačak, Serbia facility, holding European Biochar Certificate (EBC) for soil amendment and animal-feed applications.
description: Basna d.o.o. is a Swiss-owned company founded in 2010 and headquartered in Čačak, Serbia, producing biochar and heat energy from wooden biomass using pyrolysis. The company sells EBC-certified biochar for agriculture, animal husbandry, and industrial applications, and is listed as a Puro.earth-registered biochar producer. It remains a small operation (~2 employees on LinkedIn) with limited recent public signals specifically about CDR credit sales.

name: Belfast Health and Social Care Trust
Bella Biochar Corp
tech_note: Biochar
description: Bella Biochar Corp is a Canadian company that manufactures certified organic biochar from landfilled waste wood using a thermal conversion unit. This biochar is used as a soil amendment for carbon dioxide removal and to improve agricultural productivity.

name: Beston Group
tech_note: Beston Group manufactures industrial-scale biomass pyrolysis/carbonization equipment (e.g. BST-50S, BST-06 Max) that converts forestry and agricultural waste into biochar for durable carbon sequestration.
description: <cite index="1-1,3-2">Beston Group Co., Ltd., based in Zhengzhou, China, specializes in waste-to-resource pyrolysis solutions covering oil sludge, plastics, rubber, and biomass.</cite> On the biochar side, they supply the pyrolysis equipment used by CDR project developers; <cite index="8-1">Beston Group is an official technology provider for Puro.earth and is the first biochar equipment partner of Isometric.</cite> <cite index="8-3,8-4,8-5">Their BST-50 units power Exomad Green's biochar production, with Phase 2 bringing a total of 15 industrial-grade systems online.</cite>

name: Beyond Captur
tech_note: Beyond Captur develops battery-based electrochemical direct air capture technology that operates entirely on electricity, avoiding thermal regeneration steps.
description: <cite index="2-1">Beyond Captur is a South Korea-based Direct Air Capture (DAC) company leveraging battery-based carbon capture technology that operates entirely on electricity, eliminating the need for thermal processes.</cite> <cite index="11-4">The company signed an MoU with Great Carbon Valley to launch Kenya's first electrochemical Direct Air Capture pilot project</cite>, followed by a Definitive Agreement to advance that collaboration. It is a technology supplier building removal hardware rather than a buyer or ecosystem actor.

name: Bhumi Sewa Networks
tech_note: Converts agricultural residues into biochar via farmer-cooperative projects in Nepal, bundled with agroforestry and sold as verified carbon credits.
description: Bhumi Sewa Networks is a Nepal-based (Pokhara) for-purpose company that partners with farmer cooperatives to convert agricultural residues into biochar, generating verified carbon removals while promoting regenerative agriculture. They provide end-to-end biochar project development, from feasibility to implementation, and sell carbon credits to corporate buyers.

name: Bio Graphene Solutions
tech_note: Bio-materials
description: Bio Graphene Solutions manufactures and supplies graphene from non-graphite based, organic renewable resources, focusing on improving environmental impact in concrete and asphalt markets. While they mention "sustainable solutions" and "green graphene," the search results do not explicitly state that their method is a direct CDR technology like BiCRS.

name: Bio-Logical
tech_note: Biochar
description: Bio-Logical is a Kenyan company that removes carbon by producing biochar from agricultural waste, which is then used to create a biochar-based fertilizer called Asili. They aim to sequester 1Mt of CO2 annually by 2030 and support smallholder farmers.

name: Bio-Restorative Ideas
tech_note: Pyrolyzes bamboo residues into biochar in Puerto Rico using a half-mobile 5-train pyrolysis reactor (installed by ARTi in 2023), generating Puro.earth CORCs.
description: Bio-Restorative Ideas (BRi) is a Puerto Rico-based biochar producer that converts bamboo residues and post-hurricane biomass waste into biochar using a mobile pyrolysis unit installed at the Eureka hacienda site. The project is registered on Puro.earth and managed by carbon developer GECA Environnement, targeting roughly 3,000 mtons of biochar annually from 13,000 mtons of bamboo feedstock. Biochar is applied in soils, building materials, and other sequestration end-uses locally.

name: BioC
tech_note: Biochar
description: No search results specifically refer to the company 'BioC' as a Carbon Dioxide Removal company. The term 'BioC' in the search results refers to 'biochar' as a product or method, not a company.

name: BioCarb Solution
tech_note: BECCS
description: BioCarb Solution provides carbon dioxide removal (CDR) credits from the storage of biogenic CO2, helping companies achieve their sustainability goals.

name: BioCarbon
tech_note: Proprietary pyrolysis technology converts woody agricultural waste into biochar and co-products (wood vinegar, bio-oil, syngas) primarily for use as renewable charge carbon in EAF steelmaking.
description: BioCarbon is an Australian climate-tech company using proprietary pyrolysis technology to convert woody agricultural waste into biochar ("GreenChar"), bio-oil, wood vinegar, and syngas. Their primary application is replacing metallurgical coke in Electric Arc Furnace steelmaking, with a first commercial-scale plant under development at Bulahdelah, NSW. They also pursue ACCU-verified carbon credits from the biochar production process.

name: BioCirc
tech_note: BioCirc operates eight biogas plants in Denmark and is installing CO2 liquefaction/capture at five of them, with captured biogenic CO2 to be permanently stored subsea via Project Greensand.
description: <cite index="2-15,2-16">BioCirc Group, founded in Denmark in 2021, is one of the largest biomethane producers globally, operating eight biogas plants.</cite> <cite index="4-3,4-4">A Nordic Investment Bank loan is financing infrastructure to clean and liquefy captured CO2 for delivery to Project Greensand, which will store the CO2 underground in the Danish part of the North Sea.</cite> <cite index="1-1,1-2">CCS implementation is underway across five biogas plants, with operations ramping from 2026 to 2032, aiming to capture and store up to 1 million tonnes of CO2.</cite>

name: BioFlux
tech_note: Whether you're decarbonizing a ... regional CDR platform, we design the infrastructure that delivers verified carbon removal. ... We help projects unlock funding and off-take by bridging devel...
description: BioFlux is a consultancy firm that designs, certifies, and deploys biochar projects, providing end-to-end expertise in biomass carbon removal to connect biochar production to carbon markets.

name: Biocarbon Tech Asia
tech_note: Biocarbon Tech Asia is a Malaysian biochar producer listed on the Puro.earth registry pursuing CORC 100+ carbon removal certificates.
description: Biocarbon Tech Asia is listed as a biochar supplier on Puro.earth with a production facility in Malaysia, targeting CORC 100+ durability credits. According to the Puro listing, the project appears to be in early development stage with 0 CORCs in stock and feasibility/implementation work ongoing. There is limited independent public information about the company beyond its Puro supplier page.

name: Biocare
tech_note: Biocare develops, finances, and delivers biochar CDR projects globally, converting waste biomass (almond shells, forestry residues, fire-damaged timber) into biochar via pyrolysis with third-party-verified removal credits.
description: <cite index="1-1">Biocare is an engineering-focused developer of biochar carbon removal projects, bringing deep technical expertise and project delivery capability across Asia, Australia, North America and South America.</cite> <cite index="1-9">They are developing 10+ projects, representing more than 300,000 tonnes of annual CO2e removal.</cite> The company is a registered supplier on Puro.earth with the Kangaroo Island Biochar Project.

name: Biochar Byte
tech_note: Produces biochar via industrial-scale pyrolysis (and Kon Tiki kilns) of agricultural biomass/crop residues in Maharashtra, India, for soil amendment and carbon sequestration.
description: <cite index="5-1,5-2">Biochar Byte is an unfunded company based in Pune, India, founded in 2024 by Udaykumar Mathapati and Vinayak Patil, operating as a provider of industrial-scale biochar production and carbon credit generation.</cite> <cite index="6-10,6-11,6-12">The startup transforms agricultural biomass into carbon-rich material through pyrolysis, integrating geospatial imaging and technology-driven logistics to collect crop residues and prevent open-field burning.</cite>

name: Biochar Earth
tech_note: Produces biochar via controlled pyrolysis of coconut shell waste sourced from smallholder farmers in the Philippines, selling durable Biochar Carbon Removal (BCR) credits.
description: <cite index="2-1,2-2">Biochar Earth sells premium carbon dioxide removal at $199 per metric tonne of CO2 removed, grounded in controlled pyrolysis and conversion into durable biochar designed for long-term storage, representing CO2 taken from the atmosphere and stored as a material.</cite> <cite index="5-2">The company's BCR operations are currently centered in the Philippines, using coconut biochar to also support the local economy in the Global South.</cite> They also offer separately-priced avoided-emissions credits tied to diverting coconut waste from open burning.

name: Biochar Life
tech_note: Distributed smallholder-farmer biochar production via flame-curtain/Kon-Tiki and improved Aom kilns, certified under the EBC Global Artisan C-Sink standard with dMRV.
description: Biochar Life is a Delaware Public Benefit Corporation and impact venture of nonprofit Warm Heart Worldwide that trains smallholder farmers in Thailand and Africa to convert crop waste into biochar using low-tech kilns (including the new Aom Kiln). The company issues carbon-sink credits under the Global Artisan C-Sink / EBC Tropical Farmer standard and has generated over 21,000 tonnes of verified carbon removals since founding.

name: Biochar Now
tech_note: Biochar
description: Biochar Now is a pioneer and current manufacturing leader in the biochar industry, focused on making and selling high-quality biochar on a very large scale for various applications including crop production, composting, and odor control.

name: Biochar Production and Carbon Removal Company
tech_note: Develops low-capex on-farm pyrolysis kilns that convert wood chips into biochar for soil application, plus a chain-of-custody software platform for issuing Biochar Carbon Units.
description: CapChar is a UK-based biochar startup (founded 2021) offering on-farm pyrolysis kiln technology and a software platform for tracking and verifying Biochar Carbon Units (BCUs). They have operational plants in Cornwall and North Wales and developed their own Biochar Carbon Code for UK biochar quantification.

name: Biochar Rendsburg
tech_note: Operates a commercial Carbo-FORCE partial-oxidation pyrolysis plant that carbonizes organic residues into biochar for soil and material applications.
description: Biochar Rendsburg GmbH is a German company based in Borgstedt (Schleswig-Holstein) that operates the first commercial Carbo-FORCE pyrolysis plant on the site of the AWR waste-disposal region. The facility converts organic residues into biochar via partial oxidation, producing a durable carbon material and removing CO2 from the atmosphere. It is affiliated with the Carbo-FORCE technology brand (Bauer group ecosystem) and listed on the biochar-zero marketplace.

name: Biochar: a scalable carbon sink solution
tech_note: Pyrolysis of forest biomass residues (via Airex Energy CarbonFX torrefaction) and sewage sludge (via PYREG Pyrolis S2B) into stable biochar used for soil amendment and carbon sequestration credits.
description: SUEZ is a global water and waste management company that operates a dedicated biochar carbon-removal business line through joint ventures. It co-owns Carbonity, Canada's largest biochar plant in Port-Cartier (Québec), with Airex Energy and Groupe Rémabec, and partners with PYREG to produce biochar from sewage sludge. SUEZ targets 350,000 tonnes of biochar production per year by 2035.

name: Bioenergie Frauenfeld
tech_note: Operates a SYNCRAFT wood-fired CHP plant in Frauenfeld, Switzerland that pyrolyzes regional residual wood into EBC-certified biochar while co-producing renewable electricity and district heat.
description: <cite index="2-1,2-2,2-3">Bioenergie Frauenfeld AG, a joint venture between Energie 360° AG and Schweizer Zucker AG, operates a climate-positive wood-fired power plant in Frauenfeld that has been in operation since spring 2022, converting regional residual wood via pyrolysis into durable carbon (biochar).</cite> <cite index="3-15,3-16">The carbon-negative plant removes 9,000 metric tons of CO2 annually and was built in collaboration with IWK Integrierte Wärme Kraft AG and SYNCRAFT.</cite> <cite index="7-2">Carbonfuture has signed a partnership with Bioenergie Frauenfeld to enable large-scale carbon removal deliveries.</cite>

name: Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Sequestration (BECCS)
tech_note: Babcock & Wilcox supplies BECCS technology — SolveBright™ post-combustion amine capture and OxyBright™ oxy-combustion capture systems — to operators converting coal plants to biomass with CCS (e.g., 550,000 tpy Filer City, MI project with NorthStar Clean Energy; Project Cyclus with Fidelis New Energy).
description: Babcock & Wilcox Enterprises (NYSE: BW) is an Akron, Ohio-based power and industrial technology firm whose ClimateBright™ suite includes BECCS carbon capture technologies. B&W serves as a technology supplier and EPC partner for biomass-to-energy plants with carbon capture, with active projects including the Filer City, Michigan BECCS conversion (up to 550,000 tons CO2/yr) and Fidelis New Energy's Project Cyclus in Louisiana.

name: Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Storage (BECCS)
tech_note: Drax operates the UK's largest biomass power station and is developing post-combustion carbon capture on its biomass units to generate permanent geological CO2 storage (BECCS).
description: <cite index="1-8,1-9">Drax's BECCS program captures and permanently stores CO2 generated during electricity production from sustainable biomass, with the captured CO2 stored in saline aquifers.</cite> <cite index="2-10,2-11">Drax planned two full-scale BECCS units by the end of the decade, with planning permission granted in January 2024.</cite> However, <cite index="2-2,2-3">the company has recently scaled back its CCS funding, pledging around £1m in H1 2025 versus £2m the prior year</cite>, and its US arm operates under the Elimini brand.

name: Biofine
tech_note: Biochar
description: Biofine, also known as Biofine Developments Northeast (BDNE Inc.), utilizes patented technology to produce carbon-negative biofuels, renewable chemicals, and biochar from waste lignocellulosic feeds, with plans for a biorefinery to produce biochar as a soil amender.

name: Biokol
tech_note: Aggregates small-scale Swedish producers using Brachio pyrolysis boilers to convert FSC-certified forestry residues and crop residues into EBC-certified biochar, with heat byproduct fed into local heating networks.
description: Biokol.se is a Swedish biochar company founded in 2018 that builds pyrolysis boilers (via sister firm Brachio AB) and aggregates small-scale producers who convert forestry residues into high-carbon biochar. In September 2025 the project became the first to have biochar credits validated under the Rainbow Standard for a 1,000-year permanence horizon, with roughly 2.6 tCO2e sequestered per tonne of biochar produced. In early 2026 Biokol.se announced a scale-up partnership with ZeroMission to distribute Swedish biochar carbon credits.

name: Bioman
tech_note: Bioman captures biogenic CO2 from its biogas production plants and sends it to permanent geological storage, under an 8-year Danish NECCS contract.
description: <cite index="14-1,14-2">Bioman ApS is a Bigadan-owned Danish biogas company that bid to capture and store 25,000 tonnes of CO2 annually at a support price of DKK 1,175.5 per tonne</cite> under the Danish Energy Agency's NECCS fund. <cite index="18-1,18-2">As of August 19, 2025, Bioman merged into its parent group and now operates legally as Bigadan Sourcing & Commodities</cite>, covering the full value chain from biomass and biogas to CO2 storage.

name: Biomass Projects
tech_note: Biochar
description: Biomass Projects transforms Weeds of National Significance and Invasive Species into high-grade biochar at an industrial scale for Biomass Carbon Removal.

name: Biopower Tana
tech_note: Pyrolysis of local residual biomass (wood waste, agricultural, and animal-processing residues) to produce biochar used in fertilizer pellets and animal feed, with carbon credits issued via Puro.earth.
description: Biopower Tana AS is a Norwegian biochar company, founded in 2020 and based in Austertana, Finnmark, that plans to convert residual biomass (from forestry, dairy, slaughterhouses, and fish farms) into biochar for animal feed and agricultural fertilizer. The company is listed on Puro.earth as an early-development supplier with 0 CORCs in stock, and its first plant was planned for commissioning in 2025 following a feasibility study.

name: Biorecro
tech_note: Biorecro is a global BECCS project developer that integrates bioenergy-with-carbon-capture systems at existing biomass power, CHP, pulp/paper, ethanol, and biogas facilities, commercializing the resulting Puro.earth-certified CORC removal credits.
description: <cite index="13-3,13-4,13-5">Biorecro is a global project developer with over 15 years of experience focusing on BECCS, integrating BECCS operations into existing industrial facilities such as biomass power, CHP, pulp and paper, and bioenergy facilities including ethanol and biogas, to bring carbon removal to market at scale.</cite> <cite index="14-1">In September 2025 Gevo's subsidiary Net-Zero Richardton signed a carbon removal sales agreement that strengthens Biorecro's BECCS project portfolio with an in-operation project.</cite> <cite index="16-9,16-10">In November 2025, Gevo announced its first delivery of Puro.earth-certified CORCs to Biorecro North America, fulfilling a multi-year agreement expected to generate approximately $26 million in revenues over five years.</cite>

name: Biosorra
tech_note: Biosorra operates a patented pyrolysis system that converts tropical agricultural crop residues into biochar ("Biochar Bora") applied to farmland in Kenya, sequestering carbon while improving soil.
description: <cite index="1-22">Biosorra is a female-led Kenyan biochar producer aiming to remove at least one megaton of CO2 per year by 2030 via deployment of 150+ reactors.</cite> It runs what it describes as the largest industrial biochar facility in East Africa at Thika/Murang'a and supplies Kenya Nut Company and smallholder farmers. <cite index="3-1">In October 2025 the company secured $3.5 million in seed funding to scale its biochar operations in Kenya.</cite>

name: Black Bull Biochar
tech_note: Biochar
description: Black Bull Biochar is a UK-based company that scales greenhouse gas removal technologies by integrating industry and agriculture through a pioneering platform that utilizes biochar to restore the environment and remove carbon.

name: Bloomineral
tech_note: OAE
description: Bloomineral is a climate tech company that uses biomineralization to convert atmospheric CO2 into stable stone, creating carbon-negative materials and permanent carbon storage solutions.

name: Blue Carbon
tech_note: Upwelling
description: No search results specifically refer to the company 'Blue Carbon' (https://bluecarbon.cc/) that uses ocean fertilization for marine CDR. All results refer to the general concept of 'blue carbon' or other CDR methods.

name: Blue Flint Ethanol
tech_note: Corn ethanol biorefinery capturing biogenic fermentation CO2 and permanently sequestering it in an on-site Class VI injection well in the Broom Creek formation.
description: <cite index="15-3,15-4">Blue Flint Ethanol is a wholly owned subsidiary of Harvestone Low Carbon Partners (HLCP) located near Underwood, North Dakota, that generates, captures, and sequesters biogenic CO2, and was the first CCS entity to commence carbon capture operations following the August 2022 passage of the Inflation Reduction Act.</cite> <cite index="9-16,9-17">Using CCS, Blue Flint captures 100% of its CO2 emissions from fermentation, injecting approximately 600 metric tons of CO2 per day permanently stored about one mile below the surface in the Broom Creek formation.</cite> As a CDR-tech operating subsidiary of HLCP, it qualifies as a "division" supplier for the directory.

name: Blue Planet
tech_note: Building materials
description: Blue Planet uses patented mineralization technology to capture CO2 from industrial sources and convert it into synthetic limestone aggregates, which can be used in concrete to make it carbon-negative.

name: Blue Sky Biochar
tech_note: Biochar
description: Blue Sky Biochar is a BiCRS company that produces and distributes biochar as a soil amendment to create regenerative soil, enhance nutrient density, and improve plant immunity.

name: BlueGreen
tech_note: BlueGreen applies proprietary Lake Guard® algaecide formulations to remediate harmful algal blooms in lakes and reservoirs; they claim the killed algal biomass sinks to sediment, locking away sequestered carbon, and they sell verified Net Blue™ credits under the SOCIALCARBON® methodology.
description: BlueGreen Water Technologies (netbluezero.com / bluegreenwatertech.com) is a US-headquartered (R&D in Israel) water-restoration company that treats harmful algal blooms and monetizes the resulting carbon sequestration as Net Blue™ credits. In April 2024 the Social Carbon Foundation issued 12,913 tCO2e of credits from their Mantua Reservoir (Utah) project at $100/credit, and in November 2025 the company announced a peer-reviewed study in Phycology validating the approach. They raised a Series B2 round led by TAU Capital with OurCrowd in 2024 to scale the CDR business unit.

name: BlueShift
tech_note: Uses a membrane-free electrochemical process to extract CO2 from seawater (as limestone via mineralization with calcium/magnesium from industrial waste) while co-producing critical minerals and rare earths from mine tailings and coal fly ash.
description: BlueShift is a Boston/Cambridge-based startup founded in 2024 developing membrane-free electrochemical direct ocean removal (DOR) co-located with coal plants and desalination facilities. The company exited stealth in March 2025 with $2.1M pre-seed funding from ConocoPhillips, Ridgeline, and MassCEC, and is building a Boston Harbor pilot. It is an independent supplier, not a division of a larger firm.

name: Bluefield Renewable Energy
tech_note: Biochar
description: Bluefield Renewable Energy is a Singapore-based company that drives decarbonization efforts by transforming biomass waste into biochar, generating carbon removal credits, and producing biochar concrete.

name: Blusink
tech_note: Deploys engineered "Blusinky" substrates on the seabed that increase local alkalinity and act as attachment surfaces for calcifying rhodolith (coralline algae) beds, sequestering carbon via biogenic carbonate formation.
description: Blusink is a UK-based marine CDR startup pioneering seabed-deployed substrates that restore rhodolith (coralline algae) beds while enhancing local ocean alkalinity. Their dual approach combines materials engineering, chemistry and biology, with MRV based on total alkalinity measurements and calcification rates validated through a mesocosm experiment with Plymouth Marine Laboratory. Early deployments have been conducted off the coast of Colombia.

name: Boomitra
tech_note: TSB
description: Boomitra develops large-scale carbon removal projects, primarily focusing on soil carbon projects and pioneering Biomass Carbon Removal and Storage (BiCRS) initiatives.

name: Brimstone
tech_note: Brimstone's patented Rock Refinery process replaces limestone with calcium silicate rock to co-produce ordinary portland cement and alumina, with magnesium byproducts that absorb atmospheric CO2 via mineralization.
description: <cite index="5-2,5-3">Brimstone is a U.S. industrial innovator whose patented Rock Refinery produces portland cement, smelter-grade alumina, and supplementary cementitious materials, with a roadmap to co-produce steel, aluminum, magnesium, titanium, and other critical minerals from abundant silicate rocks.</cite> <cite index="9-4,9-5">Chemically extracting calcium oxide from silicate avoids CO2 release, and the process yields a magnesium byproduct that absorbs CO2 from the atmosphere.</cite> <cite index="5-15,5-18">Amazon signed a commercial agreement in August 2025 to reserve annual volumes from Brimstone's forthcoming plant, which is being engineered near Reno, Nevada.</cite>

name: Brineworks
tech_note: Electrochemical DAC electrolyzer designed for intermittent operation on cheap renewable energy. Green hydrogen as co-product to improve economics. Targeting sub-$100/tonne by 2035.
description: Amsterdam-based DAC startup (~15 employees) using electrochemical electrolyzers that run on intermittent renewables, with green hydrogen as a co-product to offset costs.

name: Brodie Biomass
tech_note: Produces biochar via pyrolysis of locally sourced woody biomass on a Surrey farm using a Woodtek Bibi C1000 unit; sells biochar and biochar-compost blends and registers carbon credits under Puro.earth.
description: Brodie Biomass is a UK-based (Brockham, Surrey) biochar producer that launched its production facility in 2024 and holds European Biochar Certificate (EBC) Animal Feed Plus grade status. It sells biochar and biochar composts for agriculture and gardens, and registers the associated carbon removal credits under Puro.earth. In March 2025 it acquired the SoilFixer brand, expanding its soil-improvement product range.

name: Bureau of Economic Geology
tech_note: State geological survey and university research institute conducting science on geological CO2 storage, subsurface characterization, MRV, and CCS/CDR policy.
description: The Bureau of Economic Geology (BEG) is the State Geological Survey of Texas, a research unit within the University of Texas at Austin's Jackson School of Geosciences. Its Gulf Coast Carbon Center (GCCC) has been a global leader since 1999 in geological CO2 storage research, monitoring, site characterization, and CCS/CDR science. BEG is a research institution that supports the CDR/CCS ecosystem rather than a commercial supplier of removals.

name: Bussme Biochar
tech_note: Pyrolysis of biomass to produce EBC-certified biochar for agricultural soil amendment, certified under Puro.earth's Biochar methodology.
description: Bussme Biochar AB is a Swedish family-run biochar producer based in Svedala, Skåne, operating since 2020 and producing EBC-certified biochar primarily for agriculture and soil applications. The company is registered on Puro.earth (project Bussme-01-Svedala) with 2,332 CORCs issued and 1,811 retired under the Biochar 2022 methodology, with a crediting period running through 31 Aug 2025. Its sister company Bussme Energy divested district-heating plants to Solör Bioenergi in 2020 and 2024, but the Biochar AB entity remains a distinct operating biochar producer.

name: Bygen
tech_note: Bygen uses a proprietary low-temperature activation (LTA) pyrolysis process to convert nut shells and sustainable forestry residues into activated carbon, with the durable carbonized product functioning as a biochar-like carbon sink.
description: <cite index="5-1,5-2">Founded in 2018 and headquartered in Melbourne, Australia, Bygen produces sustainable activated carbon from renewable agricultural and forestry by-products.</cite> <cite index="2-16,2-17">Their novel 'low-temperature activation' (LTA) technology converts carbon-rich materials like nut shells and wood into activated carbon, optimising pyrolysis and activation to improve energy efficiency and reduce emissions.</cite> <cite index="5-14">At a North American production plant, Bygen's technology was independently validated as carbon-negative via a Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) in accordance with ISO 14040, 14044, and 14067 standards.</cite>

name: C-Crete
tech_note: C-Crete produces cement-free concrete using pulverized non-carbonate rocks (granite, basalt, zeolite) as binders, which avoids Portland cement emissions and absorbs atmospheric CO2 during and after curing via mineralization.
description: C-Crete Technologies is a California-based materials science company commercializing Portland-cement-free concrete in which pulverized natural rocks like granite, basalt and zeolite replace cement. Their binder emits no CO2 during manufacturing and the cured concrete absorbs CO2 from the air over time, resulting in a carbon-negative building material.
