The company has poured thousands of tonnes across commercial, government and residential projects and received over $10M in grants from the US DOE and California Energy Commission.

name: C-Fix
tech_note: Solid sorbent DAC
description: C-Fix is a Direct Air Capture (DAC) company founded in 2022 that uses solar-powered alkaline metal sorbents and electrolysis to remove CO2.

name: C2X/SunGas Renewables
tech_note: BECCS
description: C2X/SunGas Renewables is active in BiCRS, specifically BECCS, by converting woody biomass into green methanol and capturing surplus biogenic CO2 for permanent geological storage. They have secured a significant CDR offtake agreement with Microsoft.

name: CHAR Technologies
tech_note: Uses proprietary high-temperature pyrolysis (HTP) to convert woody biomass and organic waste into biocarbon (biochar, CleanFyre biocoal) and renewable gases (RNG, green hydrogen, syngas).
description: CHAR Technologies Ltd. (TSXV:YES) is a Toronto-based cleantech company operating high-temperature pyrolysis facilities that transform woody biomass and organic waste into biochar/biocarbon products and renewable energy. Its biochar qualifies for CORC carbon removal credits, and the company also supplies biocoal to replace pulverized coal in steel blast furnaces via a partnership with ArcelorMittal. Recent activity includes the Thorold Renewable Energy Facility commissioning and a Québec biocarbon pellet facility acquisition with a 62,500-tonne offtake agreement.

name: CO2 Sink
tech_note: Purported biochar producer; no verifiable public information found about operations, products, or customers.
description: CO2 Sink (co2sink.co) is listed as a US-based biochar company, but web research returned no substantive information about the firm — no press, no projects, no registry listings, and no distinguishing operational footprint. LinkedIn shows only 4 employees and the entity appears to have minimal public presence. Note: co2sink.org is an unrelated defunct EU geological storage research project completed in 2010.

name: CO280
tech_note: CO280 develops, finances, and operates BECCS retrofit projects at pulp and paper mills, installing modular post-combustion liquid amine capture units (via partner SLB Capturi) on recovery boilers to capture biogenic CO2 and permanently store it in geologic formations.
description: <cite index="1-10,1-11">Vancouver-based CO280 develops biomass carbon removal and storage projects in the pulp and paper industry, including financing, developing, owning and operating large-scale CDR projects in partnership with pulp and paper companies, and is currently developing more than 10 projects including 5 high-priority projects anticipated to be active by 2030.</cite> <cite index="1-7">Microsoft signed one of the largest-ever engineered CDR purchase deals, agreeing to offtake nearly 3.7 million tonnes of carbon removal over 12 years from a CO280 project at a U.S. Gulf Coast pulp and paper mill.</cite>

name: CO2CO
tech_note: Grows microalgae at scale and pyrolyses the biomass into biochar for soil, afforestation, or construction aggregate applications.
description: <cite index="11-3,11-4,11-5">CO2CO is a UK carbon-removal start-up that has developed a process of growing microalgae and converting the biomass into biochar, used for agricultural or afforestation purposes to embed carbon into the soil carbon reservoir, with the aim of delivering the process at scale.</cite> The company is a spin-out involving <cite index="11-6">founders from the energy and infrastructure sectors and academics from Imperial College London</cite>, and has received an Innovate UK feasibility grant to develop microalgal biomass as a bitumen alternative.

name: CO2CirculAir
tech_note: CO2CirculAir develops SMART-DAC, a membrane-based direct air capture system using wind-driven membrane gas absorption with KOH solution and membrane electrolysis/electrodialysis for regeneration.
description: <cite index="2-1">CO2CirculAir is a Dutch R&D and innovation start-up formed by a group of membrane technology experts</cite> developing a direct air capture system. <cite index="8-5,8-6">Funded under the UK DESNZ Greenhouse Gas Removal Programme, SMART-DAC is a passive wind-driven DAC system using a two-step process with KOH-based absorption and membrane electrolysis/electrodialysis regeneration.</cite> <cite index="8-4">The pilot first captured CO2 in September 2023 and operated at over 80% uptime through April 2025.</cite>

name: CO2Rail
tech_note: Develops specialized railcars that capture CO2 from ambient air using regenerative braking energy from trains in regular service, eliminating the need for fans via the train's slipstream.
description: <cite index="11-2,19-15,19-16,19-17">CO2Rail Company is a Houston, Texas-based climate tech company whose main service is a proprietary rail-based system that captures carbon dioxide from ambient air and diesel locomotive emissions using energy generated by train regenerative braking.</cite> <cite index="2-11,2-12">Its purpose-built rail cars capture energy from regenerative braking to charge onboard batteries while leveraging the slipstream of the moving train in a ramjet-type process to avoid the need for fans, directing air into a cylindrical CO2 collection chamber.</cite> The company remains pre-commercial, with no deployed railcars or registry-issued credits; it is still fundraising from venture capital as of recent LinkedIn activity.

name: CO2Zero
tech_note: Modular, tech-agnostic DAC integrator that combines third-party capture technologies with power-to-heat and clean water co-production to reduce energy demand and cost per ton.
description: CO2Zero is a Rotterdam, Netherlands-based Direct Air Capture startup that was incubated through the YES!Delft accelerator program. The company describes its approach as a tech-agnostic modular integrator that combines multiple DAC technologies with power-to-heat and water co-production, targeting capture costs below €150/ton. They are an independent startup (not a division of a parent company — YES!Delft is an incubator, not a parent).

name: CORMETECH
tech_note: Designs and manufactures honeycomb-structured, amine-based sorbent adsorbers/contactors that serve as the core capture component of third-party DAC systems, and also develops point-source capture monoliths.
description: CORMETECH is a North Carolina-based emissions-control manufacturer (SCR catalysts) that has extended its ceramic-extrusion and honeycomb-substrate expertise into CO2 capture, producing custom-designed amine adsorbers for DAC developers and point-source capture systems under its PATHWAY product line. They collaborate with leading DAC developers, supplying the adsorber hardware at the core of those systems, and have received multiple DOE/NETL awards to advance their DAC contactor and NGCC point-source capture technology.

name: CREW Carbon
tech_note: Doses municipal wastewater with finely crushed limestone/alkaline minerals during biological treatment, converting biogenic CO2 into dissolved bicarbonate that is discharged to the ocean for long-term storage.
description: CREW Carbon is a US-based CDR supplier that adds alkaline minerals like limestone to municipal wastewater treatment streams, converting CO2 into stable bicarbonate ions that are eventually discharged to the ocean. <cite index="6-13">In 2025 the company delivered the first-ever Wastewater Alkalinity Enhancement credits under its $32.1M offtake agreement with Frontier for 71,878 tonnes between 2025-2030.</cite> <cite index="5-8">In early 2026 CREW also secured a $2.35M award from the Colorado Energy Office to deploy at a Colorado wastewater facility.</cite>

name: CTRL + Z
tech_note: Pyrolyzes agricultural waste into graphene derivatives, aiming for carbon-negative conversion of biomass into durable carbon-rich materials.
description: CTRL Z is an India-based early-stage startup converting agricultural waste into graphene derivatives through a process they describe as carbon-negative. The company positions itself as a biochar-to-graphene carbon removal supplier and was selected for the remove accelerator Phase 2. With only ~3 employees and limited recent public signals, operational status is uncertain.

name: CUR8
tech_note: Intelligence, due diligence, portfolio construction, and offtake financing platform that aggregates third-party CDR credits for corporate buyers.
description: CUR8 is a UK-based carbon removal intelligence and portfolio platform that helps corporate buyers procure, finance, and manage CDR credits across pathways including DAC, enhanced weathering, and biochar. They act as a market-maker/broker rather than a removal supplier, providing due diligence, portfolio construction, and offtake financing for clients such as British Airways, Standard Chartered, and Coca-Cola HBC.

name: Caligenia
tech_note: Caligenia pyrolyzes organic waste (including chicken manure) into BACTERCHAR, a biochar-based biofertilizer combined with plant-growth-promoting microorganisms applied to degraded agricultural soils.
description: <cite index="7-1">Caligenia is an Argentine biotechnology startup that leverages scientific knowledge in biochar, microorganisms, and soil management practices to restore degraded soils and remove CO2 from the atmosphere.</cite> <cite index="1-6">The company is building the first biochar production plant in Argentina, located in Luján.</cite> <cite index="10-1,10-4">The Argentina-based firm transforms chicken manure into "bacterchar" to turn degraded soils into farmable land, and is seeking to relocate/expand to Tulsa and test in U.S. fields.</cite>

name: Cap Clean
tech_note: Develops biofuel/bioenergy facilities (SAF, renewable diesel) using oxy-fuel biomass combustion with CO2 capture routed to geologic storage, structured as BECCS with CCS-as-a-service.
description: Cap Clean Energy Corp. is a Calgary, Alberta-based clean energy development company (subsidiary of Aether Catalyst) developing biofuel and bioenergy facilities with carbon capture and geologic storage. It signed a 2023 MOU with Raven SR to co-develop BECCS-style SAF and renewable diesel projects in Canada, and in May 2025 announced a proposed facility in Beaver County, Alberta near existing carbon capture infrastructure. Their published technology covers oxy-fuel CO2 capture from biomass combustion with permanent geologic storage.

name: Capital Link
tech_note: Capital Link Green (CLG) produces biochar via controlled pyrolysis of organic waste biomass and issues carbon removal credits verified through Isometric.
description: <cite index="12-3">Capital Link Green (CLG) transforms waste into premium biochar, while removing carbon, restoring ecosystems, and generating credits backed by science and measurable results.</cite> <cite index="12-5">Verified Carbon Credits are issued via Isometric, backed by peer-reviewed methodology.</cite> <cite index="12-13">Credits are insurable against reversal through Oka, via Lloyd's of London.</cite>

name: Captur Tower
tech_note: Develops Direct Air Capture units designed to retrofit existing industrial cooling towers, using their airflow and waste heat to lower DAC capital and operating costs.
description: <cite index="11-8,11-9,11-10">Captur Tower was founded in 2023, is headquartered in Madrid, Spain, and has 5 total employees.</cite> <cite index="2-1">The company's system integrates direct air capture (DAC) units with existing cooling towers, leveraging waste heat for efficient CO2 removal directly from the atmosphere.</cite> It is an early-stage supplier building DAC removal technology rather than a broker or buyer.

name: Captura
tech_note: Uses proprietary bipolar-membrane electrodialysis to strip CO2 from seawater for permanent storage or reuse, restoring the ocean's capacity to absorb atmospheric CO2.
description: Captura is a Pasadena, California-based Direct Ocean Capture company spun out of Caltech in 2021 that uses high-performance bipolar-membrane electrodialysis to extract CO2 from seawater, allowing the ocean to reabsorb additional atmospheric CO2. The company operates a 1,000 t/yr pilot in Kona, Hawaii (with Equinor) and is designing its first 30,000–50,000 t/yr commercial facility, with a 30,000-credit offtake signed by MOL.

name: Capture6
tech_note: Capture6 pairs direct air capture with water treatment facilities, using an electrochemical process to convert waste brine into a sodium hydroxide solvent that binds atmospheric CO2 into solid mineralized carbonates while producing freshwater as a co-product.
description: Capture6 is a US-based DAC supplier that integrates carbon removal with desalination and water treatment infrastructure, turning waste brine into a CO2-capturing solvent while recovering freshwater. Active projects include Project Wallaby in Western Australia (with Pilot Energy), Project Monarch in Los Angeles County (with Palmdale Water District), and a partnership with K-Water in South Korea.

name: CapturePoint
tech_note: BECCS
description: CapturePoint specializes in carbon capture, transport, utilization, and permanent underground storage. They partner with other companies to manage CO2 from industrial emitters and DAC facilities, focusing on environmental services.

name: CarStorCon
tech_note: CarStorCon produces a biochar-based additive (Clim@Add®) from pyrolyzed woody biogenic residues that is incorporated into concrete and asphalt, permanently embedding biochar carbon in building materials and generating CO2-sink certificates.
description: CarStorCon Technologies GmbH, founded in 2022 in Marienhafe, Germany, develops the Clim@Add® additive — a modified technical carbon derived from biochar pyrolysis — that turns concrete and asphalt into permanent carbon sinks. The company classifies its approach as Biochar Carbon Removal (BCR) and works with construction-industry partners across the DACH region and Europe. As of 2025 it reports over 5,000–6,500 m³ of climate concrete realized and participates in EU-funded biochar research consortia.

name: Carba
tech_note: Autothermal low-temperature pyrolysis of waste biomass into biocarbon, followed by anoxic burial in landfills for permanent CO2 storage.
description: Carba is a Minneapolis-based CDR supplier that converts waste biomass into stable biocarbon via a patented autothermal low-temperature pyrolysis process and sequesters it through anoxic burial in landfills for 1,000+ year durability. The company has a 44,000-ton offtake with Microsoft, a $7M DOE Carbon Negative Shot grant, and recently raised $6M led by Rusheen Capital and Canopy Generations Fund. Its first project in Burnsville, MN is commissioning with Isometric-certified deliveries starting Q1 2026.

name: Carbex
tech_note: Biochar
description: Carbex GmbH is a German manufacturing company that produces biochar and biochar-based products for various applications, utilizing biochar as a carbon dioxide removal method.

name: Carbfix
tech_note: Injects CO2 dissolved in water into basaltic bedrock where it reacts with divalent cations to form stable carbonate minerals, providing permanent in-situ mineral storage.
description: Carbfix is an Icelandic company that permanently stores CO2 by dissolving it in water and injecting it into basaltic rock formations, where it mineralizes into stable carbonate minerals within approximately two years. It operates point-source mineralization at the Hellisheiði and Nesjavellir geothermal plants and partners with DAC providers like Climeworks (Orca/Mammoth) for storage. It is developing the Coda Terminal, a large-scale transport-and-mineralization hub.

name: CarbiCrete
tech_note: Mineralizes CO2 into cement-free concrete blocks/pavers made with steel slag binder, replacing Portland cement and locking CO2 in the product via carbonation curing.
description: CarbiCrete is a Montreal-based carbon removal technology company that licenses a patented process for producing cement-free concrete by replacing cement with steel slag and mineralizing CO2 into the concrete for permanent storage. They license their technology to block and paver manufacturers in Canada, the northeastern US, and (from 2026) France via Saint-Gobain's POINT.P brand.

name: Carbo Culture
tech_note: Uses patented Carbolysis™ pyrolysis reactors to convert waste biomass into stable biochar while generating renewable energy.
description: <cite index="1-3,1-4,1-5">Carbo Culture is a Finland-based climate technology company that uses patented Carbolysis™ reactors to take waste biomass and convert it into stable biochar, locking carbon away for centuries while generating renewable energy.</cite> <cite index="2-2,2-3,2-4">In 2025 the company announced ARC Middenmeer, a new biochar plant at the ECW Energy site in Middenmeer, North Holland, expected to remove more than 20,000 tonnes of CO2 annually while producing 40,000 m³ of biochar and 16 MW of sustainable energy.</cite> The company produces premium biochar for carbon removal, horticulture, and industrial decarbonization.

name: Carbo-FORCE
tech_note: Biochar
description: Carbo-FORCE is a German company that specializes in carbon dioxide removal by converting organic residues into biochar using its Carbo-CAP-TEC pyrolysis technology, which also produces energy.

name: CarboHeroes
tech_note: Biochar
description: CarboHeroes is a Climate Technology Product Manufacturing company that scales biochar to remove 500 million tons of CO2 from the atmosphere by 2050, aiming for a circular economy.

name: CarboVerte
tech_note: CarboVerte operates a pyrolysis plant in Eibenstock, Germany to produce biochar from biomass, selling plant-charcoal and biochar-based soil amendments and feed additives for agriculture, livestock and horticulture.
description: <cite index="14-1,14-2">CarboVerte is a German company specialized in producing biochar and biochar-based products using a modern pyrolysis plant.</cite> <cite index="13-1,13-2">Based in Eibenstock, its focus is the agricultural and livestock industry as well as urban green spaces.</cite> Products are sold via their own store and Amazon, marketed as permanent atmospheric CO2 sinks for soil, composting and animal feed applications.

name: Carbofex Oy
tech_note: Biochar
description: Carbofex Oy produces biochar through the thermochemical conversion (pyrolysis) of biomass, which serves as a carbon dioxide removal method. Their biochar product is used for soil amendment, water filtering, and as a compost additive.

name: Carbogenics
tech_note: Pyrolyzes difficult-to-recycle organic waste and secondary biomass into CreChar® biochar, primarily sold as an additive to anaerobic digestion and wastewater treatment plants, with carbon sequestration as a co-benefit.
description: Carbogenics is an Edinburgh-based University of Edinburgh spinout (2016) producing CreChar®, an engineered biochar made from paper waste and secondary biomass via pyrolysis. Its primary market is enhancing biogas yields in anaerobic digestion plants, with the stable carbon in the biochar providing durable CDR. The company is expanding into the US (New Mexico) following a $3M funding round in early 2026.

name: Carboliva
tech_note: Biochar
description: Carboliva produces and commercializes sustainable biochar and vegetable charcoal from olive biomass (pits and pulp) through pyrolysis, which also generates clean thermal energy. This process fixes carbon absorbed by olive trees into a solid structure, preventing its release into the atmosphere.

name: Carbon 1.5
tech_note: France-based Direct Air Capture startup developing solid-sorbent DAC technology aimed at low-energy-consumption CO2 removal from ambient air.
description: Carbon 1.5 is a French direct air capture company focused on developing sorbent-based DAC systems with significantly lower energy consumption than incumbents. Public information on the company is limited, and independent corroboration of recent milestones, funding, or deployments was not found in search results.

name: Carbon America
tech_note: BECCS
description: Carbon America develops carbon capture and sequestration projects, delivering the entire CO₂ capture-transport-storage value chain, and is actively hiring for various roles.

name: Carbon Bank
tech_note: Carbon Bank operates an enhanced rock weathering project in Northumberland, UK, spreading finely crushed basalt rock dust from local quarries onto arable farmland, with planned afforestation projects under the Woodland Carbon Code.
description: Carbon Bank is a UK-based CDR project developer and part of the Green Britain Group (sister company to Ecotricity). They run an enhanced rock weathering project in Northumberland using basalt from Breedon quarries spread on local farmland, and plan afforestation/nature recovery projects aligned with BSI Flex 701 and the Woodland Carbon Code.

name: Carbon Blade DAC
tech_note: Develops a distributed, containerized Direct Air Capture system using a rotating blade contactor, alkaline absorption solvent, and electrodialysis bipolar membrane (EDBM) regeneration powered by onboard solar/wind.
description: <cite index="6-3">Carbon Blade is a California-based climate technology company that develops hardware solutions to capture CO2 directly from the air as a climate mitigation strategy.</cite> <cite index="6-1">The company acquired foundational DAC IP from RoCo® in 2023.</cite> <cite index="10-12">It is currently collaborating with UC San Diego to construct a pilot carbon capture plant on campus capable of both capturing and storing CO2.</cite>

name: Carbon Capital
tech_note: Produces certified biochar from invasive encroacher bush (Acacia spp.) using retort kiln pyrolysis at Farm Gai Kaisa 159 in the Grootfontein/Otjozondjupa region of Namibia, with carbon removal credits issued via Puro.earth.
description: Carbon Capital is a Namibian biochar producer operating Farm Gai Kaisa 159, reportedly the largest industrial biochar project in Africa, developed in partnership with biochar developer Planboo. The project has produced over 16,000 tonnes of certified biochar, issued 19,500+ CORCs on Puro.earth, and earned a Sylvera A rating, with buyers including Boeing.

name: Carbon Capture & Commercialization
tech_note: Solid sorbent DAC
description: Carbon Capture & Commercialization (CC&C) is a US-based company that develops Direct Air Carbon Capture (DACC) adsorbers using a patented low-power, no-solvent solid sorbent technology.

name: Carbon Cell
tech_note: Carbon Cell combines pyrolysis-derived biochar with natural bio-based polymers to make an expandable, moldable rigid foam that replaces EPS/EPP/PUR/PIR in packaging and building insulation, locking biochar carbon into durable products (and ultimately soil at end-of-life).
description: <cite index="8-2,8-3">Carbon Cell, founded by Imperial College alumni Elizabeth Lee, Ori Blich, Eden Harrison and Juan Ignacio Rion, produces a patent-pending, plastic-free foam with a low or negative carbon footprint that replaces conventional plastic foams in packaging and insulation.</cite> <cite index="9-3">The company estimates nearly a kilogram of CO2 is removed per kilogram of foam produced.</cite> <cite index="9-9">At end of life the natural polymer composts away, leaving biochar that keeps carbon sequestered for generations while enriching soil.</cite>

name: Carbon Centric
tech_note: Develops, owns and operates amine-based carbon capture plants on biogenic flue gas from waste-to-energy and bioenergy sites in Norway, liquefying and sending CO2 to permanent geological storage.
description: <cite index="4-16,4-17">Carbon Centric, established in 2021, develops, builds and operates carbon capture plants for industry and the energy sector, aiming to make carbon capture scalable for small and medium-sized emission sources in Norway and the Nordic region.</cite> Its Rakkestad plant at Østfold Energi's waste-to-energy facility began operations in September 2025 as a CCU demonstrator, while its flagship BECCS project at Kirkenær with Solør Bioenergi targets ~32,000 t/yr of biogenic CO2 removal and <cite index="7-1">has completed the Puro.earth Preliminary Assessment</cite>, backed by a long-term offtake agreement with DNV.

name: Carbon Collect
tech_note: Carbon Collect develops the MechanicalTree™, a passive direct air capture (PDAC) system using vertically stacked sorbent disks and low-temperature vacuum-steam regeneration (~85°C), based on Klaus Lackner's ASU research.
description: <cite index="10-3,10-4,10-5,10-6,10-7">Carbon Collect, formerly Silicon Kingdom Holdings Limited, specializes in carbon capture technology and offers the MechanicalTree, a passive, scalable system designed to capture CO₂ from ambient air without energy-intensive processes; it was founded in 2018 and is based in Dublin, Ireland.</cite> <cite index="2-8,2-9">In 2025, Carbon Collect installed its Gen-II MechanicalTree™, which doubles CO₂ capture per cycle and uses lightweight, non-metallic, recyclable materials.</cite>

name: Carbon Containment Lab
tech_note: A 501(c)(3) research nonprofit that designs, tests, and supports pilots of novel carbon containment methods (BiCRS, mineralization, refrigerant abatement, methane measurement) but does not itself develop credit projects or operate removal facilities.
description: <cite index="6-3,6-4,6-5,6-6,6-7">Carbon Containment Lab is a 501(c)(3) climate nonprofit supporting the design, testing, and implementation of novel and neglected climate solutions, working to bring research from laboratories into pilot and commercialization across anthropogenic, biologic, and geologic emissions pathways including BiCRS, carbon mineralization, fluorocarbon recovery, and low-concentration methane measurement.</cite> <cite index="1-1,1-2,1-3">CC Lab is explicitly not a carbon credit registry, validator, verifier, or project developer, engaging market stakeholders only as an independent nonprofit without financial interest.</cite> <cite index="6-9">It spun out of the Yale School of the Environment in early 2024 to operate as an independent nonprofit.</cite>

name: Carbon Corp
tech_note: Liquid solvent DAC
description: Carbon Corp is a DAC company that uses a proprietary liquid solvent technology involving high-yield electrolysis in molten carbonate to transform CO2 into valuable carbon nanotubes.

name: Carbon Cycle
tech_note: Pyrolysis of locally-sourced untreated wood chips into biochar (Pflanzenkohle) for soil amendment, animal feed, and concrete additive applications.
description: Carbon Cycle GmbH & Co. KG is a German biochar producer based in Rieden, Bavaria, producing Pflanzenkohle from PEFC-certified untreated wood chips via pyrolysis for agricultural soil improvement and animal feed applications. The company is EBC-certified and Puro.earth-listed (CORC 100+), with biochar production starting in 2019 and a larger second production system commissioned in 2023. They export to Norway and Switzerland and are exploring biochar-in-concrete pilots and district heating networks.

name: Carbon Direct
tech_note: Science-led carbon management advisory and software platform providing supplier due diligence, procurement, portfolio construction, and emissions accounting for corporate and government buyers of carbon removals.
description: Carbon Direct is a US-based carbon management firm combining a science advisory team with software to help large buyers procure, verify, and monitor high-quality carbon removal and reduction credits. It does not physically remove CO2 itself but sits in the CDR ecosystem as a broker/advisor/diligence provider, working with Fortune 500 clients including Microsoft, Shopify, and Alaska Airlines. A sister firm, Carbon Direct Capital, invests growth equity in carbon management technologies.

name: Carbon Drawdown Initiative
tech_note: Philanthropic funder and research operator running enhanced rock weathering (basalt/dunite on agricultural fields) field experiments and investing in early-stage CDR startups.
description: Carbon Drawdown Initiative is a German (GmbH), philanthropically-funded organization founded in 2019 by Dirk Paessler that supports the emerging CDR industry through early-stage investments in 30+ CDR startups, scientific research partnerships, and policy work. They also run "Project Carbdown," a field research program on enhanced rock weathering in partnership with universities and institutes across Europe. Their primary role is as a CDR ecosystem funder/research organization rather than a commercial removal supplier.

name: Carbon Energy
tech_note: N/A DAC tech
description: No information found about Carbon Energy, a DAC company from South Korea.

name: Carbon Engineering/Occidental Petroleum
tech_note: Liquid solvent DAC
description: Carbon Engineering, now a subsidiary of Occidental Petroleum, develops and deploys Direct Air Capture (DAC) technology using a liquid solvent method to capture CO2 from the atmosphere, which can then be used for clean transportation fuels or stored.

name: Carbon Gap
tech_note: Carbon Gap is a UK-registered non-profit advocacy and research NGO focused on advancing EU policy to scale carbon dioxide removal; it produces policy analysis, a CDR Policy Tracker, and country readiness assessments.
description: <cite index="4-19">Carbon Gap is Europe's leading carbon dioxide removal (CDR) advocacy and research NGO</cite>, based in the UK and focused on shaping EU policy frameworks to enable the scale-up of permanent carbon removal. <cite index="2-11">Carbon Gap LTD is a registered charity (charity number 1200562) and a private company limited by guarantee, registered in England and Wales.</cite> It does not itself remove CO2 — it produces policy briefs, a Policy Tracker, the CARE Calculator, and country readiness assessments to guide European decision-makers.

name: Carbon Gold
tech_note: Produces biochar via pyrolysis and sells enriched biochar-based composts, fertilisers, soil improvers and tree care products for agricultural and horticultural applications.
description: <cite index="10-3">Carbon Gold was founded in 2007 by Craig Sams, founder of Green & Blacks Chocolate, and Dan Morrell, founder of the Carbon Neutral Company.</cite> The UK-based B Corp produces enriched biochar products (composts, fertilisers, soil improvers, tree care) that sequester carbon in soil while improving plant health. <cite index="8-1">Retail products have moved to Marshalls Garden</cite>, while the company continues trade sales directly.

name: Carbon Hill
tech_note: Biochar
description: Carbon Hill is a family-run company based in mid-Wales, UK, that produces biochar from locally sourced, underutilized biomass using proprietary low-emission pyrolysis systems. They are expanding their operations through a joint venture, Biodynamic Carbon Ltd, to create the UK's largest biochar facility.

name: Carbon Iceland
tech_note: DAC project developer
description: Carbon Iceland captures CO2 from industrial emissions, particularly aluminum smelters, to produce renewable fuels like sustainable methanol for long-range transportation.

name: Carbon Impact
tech_note: Carbon Impact is a French CDR project developer that retrofits biomass and biomethane plants with CO2 capture, liquefaction, and offshore geological sequestration (partnering with South Pole and Airfix) to generate BECCS carbon removal credits.
description: <cite index="2-18,2-19">Carbon Impact is a French carbon removal project developer, cofounded by energy experts, that leads the implementation of CO2 capture infrastructure in partnership with local biomethane unit owners.</cite> <cite index="3-6">Together with South Pole and Airfix, the company is launching France's first biogas-based BECCS project near Nancy,</cite> with captured CO2 liquefied on-site and transported to Norway for subsea storage under the North Sea.

name: Carbon Instead
tech_note: Produces pyrolysis-derived biochar from biogenic waste and functionalizes it as an additive/replacement for cement and sand in concrete and mortar, creating durable carbon storage in the built environment.
description: Carbon Instead is a Berlin-based startup (founded 2020) that produces a biochar-based additive for construction materials like concrete and mortar, made via pyrolysis of biogenic waste streams. The biochar partially replaces cement and sand, turning building materials into long-term carbon stores. They operate across the value chain from biomass sourcing to carbonization technology to application.

name: Carbon Kapture
tech_note: Biochar
description: Carbon Kapture is a UK-based BiCRS company that grows seaweed to remove carbon from the sea. The harvested seaweed is then converted into biochar, a stable form of carbon used to enrich soil.

name: Carbon Lockdown
tech_note: Carbon Lockdown buries sustainably-sourced coarse woody biomass in engineered underground "Wood Vaults" capped with low-permeability clay to create anoxic conditions that prevent decomposition for 1,000+ years.
description: Carbon Lockdown Project is a US public benefit corporation spun out of University of Maryland research by Dr. Ning Zeng, developing wood-vault biomass burial for durable carbon removal. Its flagship 5,000 tCO2e Potomac Project is considered the world's first commercial-scale wood vault, with CORC credits issued under the Puro.earth Terrestrial Storage of Biomass methodology, and the company has delivered tonnes to buyers including Kinnevik via Climate Vault.

name: Carbon Neutral Initiative
tech_note: CNI deploys olivine/silicate-enriched substrates in urban green (sedum) roofs to drive Enhanced Rock Weathering, producing durable CO2 removal via bicarbonate formation.
description: <cite index="7-15,7-16">Carbon Neutral Initiative develops green roofs that remove CO2 through the addition of olivine, expecting net removal of 1,804 tonnes of CO2 over 25 years from its flagship project.</cite> <cite index="3-2,3-9">The Netherlands-based company runs the Carbon Green Roof project as part of its bio-enhanced silicate weathering programme and collaborates with TNO, Utrecht University, Hasselt University, and Spanish universities.</cite> <cite index="7-2">It is also initiating similar Enhanced Weathering projects in Suriname and Spain using other suitable rock types beyond olivine.</cite>

name: Carbon Plus
tech_note: Malaysian industrial biochar facility for carbon removal and sustainable agriculture.
description: Carbon Plus is a Malaysian company that develops and implements industrial-scale biochar facilities, converting biomass into biochar for carbon sequestration and producing biochar, pyroligneous acid, and renewable energy.

name: Carbon Reform
tech_note: Decentralized direct air capture via HVAC-retrofit "Carbon Capsule" units that remove CO2 from indoor air in commercial buildings and mineralize it on-site into limestone for reuse in construction materials.
description: Carbon Reform is a Philadelphia/Wilmington-based climate tech startup (founded 2020) that retrofits commercial building HVAC systems with modular hardware that captures indoor CO2 and contaminants while lowering ventilation energy use. Captured CO2 is mineralized on-site into limestone byproduct for use in concrete and paint. The company raised a $5.5M seed-plus round in January 2025 (bringing total to ~$9M) and has active customer deployments with utilities such as Baltimore Gas & Electric and New Jersey Natural Gas.

name: Carbon Removal AS/Nordic DAC Group
tech_note: Project developer deploying Phlair's electrochemical pH-swing liquid-solvent DAC technology at Kollsnes, Norway, with captured CO2 piped to Northern Lights for offshore geological storage.
description: Carbon Removal AS is a Norwegian project development company developing a large-scale Direct Air Capture facility at Kollsnes in Øygarden, adjacent to the Northern Lights CO2 storage terminal. In July 2025, via subsidiary NorDAC Kollsnes AS, it signed an agreement with German DAC technology provider Phlair to deploy an electrochemical liquid-solvent DAC plant targeting 60,000 tpa initially and scaling to 500,000 tpa. Nordic DAC Group AB is a Swedish affiliate/minority shareholder that sells the resulting removal certificates.

name: Carbon Removal Startup InPlanet Raises €1.2m In Pre
Carbon Remove
tech_note: Produces biochar via pyrolysis of biomass for soil application and carbon removal credit generation in Brazil.
description: Carbon Remove is a small Brazilian biochar producer based in Anhembi, São Paulo state, founded and led by Thomas Britze. The company produces biochar from biomass via pyrolysis to generate carbon removal credits while providing soil fertility benefits for Brazilian agriculture.

name: Carbon Sequestration Inc
tech_note: TSB
description: Carbon Sequestration Inc. offers carbon dioxide removal through methods including wood vaulting, biochar production, and carbon farming, integrating waste management and soil improvement.

name: Carbon Square
tech_note: Liquid solvent DAC
description: Carbon Square specializes in effective carbon removal and reuse strategies, aiming to sequester carbon permanently or repurpose it for beneficial applications. Their website indicates they use DAC (Liquid Solvent) as their method.

name: Carbon Time
tech_note: Carbon Time develops Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement (OAE) approaches — primarily olivine-based rock weathering and electrochemical alkalinization — to increase seawater alkalinity and sequester atmospheric CO2 as dissolved inorganic carbon.
description: <cite index="2-1,2-2">Carbon Time is a Paris, France–based company founded in 2021 that operates as a developer of ocean alkalinity enhancement for carbon dioxide removal.</cite> <cite index="1-5,1-6,1-8">Its initial focus is alkalinization via rock weathering using olivine, alongside electrochemical approaches compatible with coastal industries like desalination or water treatment.</cite> <cite index="1-12,1-13">The company was financed by the Team for the Planet citizen-investor movement.</cite>

name: Carbon To Stone
tech_note: Reactive crystallization process that combines CO2 (from air or point-source) with alkaline industrial residues (steel slag, fly ash, mine tailings) to form solid carbonates while recovering energy-critical metals.
description: Carbon To Stone is a Cornell University spinout developing a low-energy carbon mineralization technology that couples CO2 capture with reactive crystallization using alkaline industrial waste streams. The process produces solid carbonates for construction use and recovers valuable metals (Li, Co, Ni, Mg, etc.) as co-products, targeting hard-to-abate sectors like iron and steel.

name: Carbon Universe
tech_note: Building materials
description: Carbon Universe is a Polish tech company focused on carbon reduction in concrete prefabrication, leveraging advanced technologies to combat climate change through mineralization (Other).

name: Carbon Utility
tech_note: Liquid solvent DAC
description: Carbon Utility synthesizes PAN precursors from captured CO2 and green H2 to create CO2-derived carbon fiber, offering a high-performance material with a cleaner input stream. They also provide zero-carbon food-grade CO2 and green H2 for power generation and HFC vehicles.

name: Carbon removal through enhanced rock weathering: InPlanet closes €1.2 million to scale its vision
tech_note: InPlanet applies finely crushed basalt/silicate rock powder to tropical farmland in Brazil to accelerate natural weathering, permanently sequestering CO2 as bicarbonate while improving soil fertility.
description: <cite index="4-21,8-1">Founded in 2022, InPlanet is a Brazil- and Germany-based AgTech startup pioneering Enhanced Rock Weathering (ERW) as a scientifically rigorous pathway for durable carbon removal and regenerative agriculture.</cite> <cite index="3-10,3-11">In December 2024 InPlanet and Isometric announced the world's first delivery of verified carbon credits through Enhanced Rock Weathering, verified under Isometric's Enhanced Weathering Protocol.</cite> <cite index="4-8">In December 2025 InPlanet signed an agreement with Microsoft to remove more than 28,500 tonnes of CO₂ between 2026 and 2028.</cite>

name: Carbon to Sea Initiative
tech_note: Non-profit philanthropic funder and convener supporting scientific research, field trials, MRV development, and policy advocacy for ocean alkalinity enhancement (OAE).
description: Carbon to Sea Initiative is a non-profit philanthropic program (a project of the Windward Fund) dedicated to advancing ocean alkalinity enhancement (OAE) research through grant-making, field research network-building, policy advocacy, and convening. It is the largest philanthropic funder in the OAE space but does not itself remove CO2 or sell credits. It sits squarely in the CDR ecosystem as a funder, field-builder, and policy advocate.

name: Carbon180
tech_note: Nonprofit policy advocacy think tank focused on advancing U.S. federal policies, funding, and environmental justice frameworks for carbon dioxide removal across DAC, soil carbon, and other pathways.
description: <cite index="2-1,2-2">Carbon180 is a nonprofit environmental organization headquartered in Washington, D.C., co-founded in 2015 by Giana Amador and Noah Deich at UC Berkeley</cite> (formerly known as Center for Carbon Removal). <cite index="2-4,2-5">Its main activities include federal policy advocacy, the New Carbon Economy Consortium, and the Leading with Soil Initiative, and it publishes fact sheets and deep dives on various carbon removal approaches.</cite> CDR is its entire mission, making it part of the CDR ecosystem rather than a physical supplier.

name: Carbon2H
tech_note: Biochar
description: Carbon2H is a German company that uses mobile biomass gasification systems to convert organic residues into renewable energy and biochar, which sequesters CO2 for centuries and improves soil fertility.

name: CarbonAir Energy
tech_note: Solid sorbent DAC
description: CarbonAir Energy is a Brazilian company that provides CO2 capturing services using modular, 100% national Direct Air Capture (DAC) technology with solid sorbents, and offers decarbonization consulting.

name: CarbonBlue
tech_note: DOR
description: CarbonBlue develops a Direct Ocean Removal method that draws excess carbon dioxide out of water, restoring its capacity to absorb more from the atmosphere. Their technology can turn various water sources into efficient CDR assets.

name: CarbonCapture Inc.
tech_note: CarbonCapture Inc. develops modular solid-sorbent Direct Air Capture systems (Leo Series) that filter CO2 from the atmosphere for permanent underground storage.
description: <cite index="5-2,5-3">CarbonCapture's DAC systems use solid sorbents that soak up atmospheric CO2 when cooled and release it when heated, capturing CO2 from the air and permanently storing it underground.</cite> Through its Canadian subsidiary True North Carbon, the company is deploying <cite index="1-3">Project Tamarack at Deep Sky Alpha in Alberta, designed to remove up to 2,000 tonnes of CO2 annually</cite>, which <cite index="3-1">achieved "First Capture" on October 22, 2025</cite>.

name: CarbonChip
tech_note: Operates a Tigercat 6050 mobile pyrolysis unit that converts eucalyptus and pine forestry residues into biochar in situ at Queensland plantations, generating Puro.earth-certified carbon removal credits.
description: <cite index="15-1,15-2,15-3">Carbonchip is a Brisbane-based biochar manufacturer established in 2020 that processes sustainable forestry residue through a mobile pyrolysis machine to produce biochar for Queensland farms and larger national projects.</cite> <cite index="14-3,14-4,14-5,14-6">The Carbonchip Mobile Carboniser Project uses a Tigercat 6050 mobile pyrolysis unit to process eucalyptus and pine residues from Queensland plantations in situ under Puro.earth's Biochar Methodology.</cite> <cite index="13-7">As one of Biocare's earliest issued CDR projects (2023), Carbonchip has issued 579 carbon removal credits.</cite>

name: CarbonCure
tech_note: Injects captured CO2 into fresh concrete and reclaimed wash water where it reacts with calcium to form permanently embedded calcium carbonate minerals, with a Verra-approved methodology; supports both industrial-sourced CCU and atmospheric (DAC-sourced) permanent CO2 storage.
description: CarbonCure Technologies, headquartered in Halifax, Canada, licenses carbon mineralization systems that inject CO2 into ready-mix concrete, precast concrete, and reclaimed wash water at concrete plants. While primarily marketed as a carbon utilization solution, the company partners with DAC providers like Heirloom to deliver verified atmospheric CO2 removal via permanent mineralization, and has a Verra-verified methodology generating carbon credits.

name: CarbonFields
tech_note: Biochar
description: CarbonFields transforms biomass waste into biochar and sustainable bioproducts, offering carbon-negative solutions for agriculture and industry.

name: CarbonMeld
tech_note: Automated LLM-based pipeline that scores carbon credit projects across registries and marketplaces on integrity, transparency, claim safety, and documentation quality.
description: <cite index="1-1,1-2">CarbonMeld provides quality scores for 650+ carbon credit projects across 9 marketplaces, with daily updates on integrity, transparency, and claim safety.</cite> <cite index="2-12,2-13,2-14">It applies a standardized evaluation pipeline to public documents from registries such as Verra, Gold Standard, CDM, and CORSIA, using an LLM-based system to evaluate four dimensions: registry integrity, transparency, claim safety, and documentation quality.</cite> <cite index="2-6,2-7">CarbonMeld is not a marketplace but an independent analysis tool used before negotiation to screen projects.</cite>

name: CarbonRun
tech_note: Adds powdered limestone to acidified rivers (River Alkalinity Enhancement), converting CO2 into bicarbonate that is transported to the ocean for long-term storage.
description: CarbonRun is a Nova Scotia-based CDR supplier that deploys River Alkalinity Enhancement (RAE), adding finely ground limestone to rivers to reduce acidity, restore fish habitat, and permanently sequester CO2 as bicarbonate delivered to the ocean. In January 2026 the company issued the world's first Isometric-certified RAE credits (76 tonnes from its Kvina River project in Norway), delivered under a $25.4M Frontier offtake covering ~55,442 tonnes between 2025-2029.

name: CarbonZero
tech_note: Pyrolysis of almond shell agricultural waste into biochar, applied to farmland soils for long-term carbon storage and soil improvement.
description: CarbonZero.Eco is a Silicon Valley-based biochar startup founded by Harper Moss that converts California almond shells into biochar via pyrolysis, partnering with almond growers in Colusa and Yolo Counties. In December 2025 it commissioned its first commercial biochar facility in Colusa County and announced a carbon removal credit purchase agreement with Climeworks. The company is registered as a biochar supplier on the Puro.earth registry.

name: CarbonZero.Eco Opens First Biochar Plant in California, Secures Major Carbon Credit Deal With Climeworks
tech_note: Pyrolyzes almond shell agricultural waste from California Central Valley farms into biochar for long-term carbon storage and soil amendment.
description: <cite index="1-2,1-3">CarbonZero.Eco is a Silicon Valley–based, venture-backed climate technology startup pioneering regenerative agriculture and carbon removal through biochar, which completed its first commercial biochar production facility in Colusa County, California in December 2025 and announced a landmark carbon credit purchase agreement with Climeworks.</cite> <cite index="5-27,5-28">At full capacity, the kilns can produce 30,000 tons of biochar per year, and the biochar will be mixed into compost and used by partner farms to enrich soils.</cite> <cite index="7-23">The company was founded in 2024 by Harper Moss and raised about $3.5 million in early 2025 from investors including leaders at Google, Meta and Amazon.</cite>

name: Carbonaide
tech_note: Carbonaide mineralizes biogenic/captured CO₂ into precast concrete via ex-situ carbonation curing, permanently storing ~100 kg CO₂ per m³ of concrete.
description: <cite index="6-3">Carbonaide is a Finnish spin-out from VTT Technical Research Centre that enables manufacturing of carbon-negative concrete.</cite> <cite index="1-8,1-9,1-10">It uses ex-situ mineralization based on carbonation, where calcium ions from cement react with biogenic CO₂ during curing to form stable carbonate minerals for permanent storage.</cite> <cite index="1-32">Carbon removals are certified by Isometric, enabling verified durable carbon removal credits.</cite>

name: Carbonapp
tech_note: Carbonapp is a French mission-driven carbon project developer/mandataire that helps third-party project owners (biochar producers, foresters, farmers, construction firms) structure and certify credits under Label Bas-Carbone, Puro.earth, Riverse and CSI standards.
description: Carbonapp is a France-based multi-sectoral carbon project developer and offset platform founded in 2020, operating as a mandated developer (mandataire) that sources projects and shepherds them through certification under standards such as Label Bas-Carbone, Puro.earth, Riverse and CSI. It does not itself produce biochar or physically remove CO2; its sister company DEMIO produces biochar, while Carbonapp structures and markets the resulting credits to corporate buyers. It sits in the CDR ecosystem as a developer/intermediary rather than a supplier of removals.

name: Carbonaught
tech_note: Applies finely crushed basalt (often sourced from quarry waste) to agricultural soils to accelerate silicate weathering, delivering permanent CO2 removal alongside soil-health benefits for farmers.
description: <cite index="9-3,9-4">Carbonaught is a Brisbane-based startup founded by former mining professionals Andrew Pedley, James Lyons and Rhys Heffernan to turn mining waste into a farm input that delivers measurable carbon removal.</cite> <cite index="1-10,1-11">Its enhanced rock weathering technology is deployed in trials across Queensland, New South Wales, Western Australia and California, with initial focus on sugarcane and expansion into horticulture, grains, cotton, beef, dairy and rice.</cite> <cite index="9-14,9-15">The company is also developing a digital platform connecting quarry operators, farmers and carbon credit buyers, with GPS-based application tracking and carbon-removal verification.</cite>

name: Carbonauten
tech_note: Biochar
description: Carbonauten is a German company that develops and produces technical biocarbons, pyrolysis oils, and renewable energy from woody biomass residues through proprietary pyrolysis technology. They use biochar as a CO2 sink, locking it into innovative products like CO2-negative materials for durable seat shells.

name: Carbondrop
tech_note: Applies micronized basalt in hydrogel pellets to agricultural soils to accelerate silicate weathering and sequester CO2 as bicarbonate/carbonate.
description: Carbondrop is a Vienna, Austria-based climate-tech startup developing enhanced rock weathering (ERW) for carbon removal. They produce a carbon-removing fertilizer made of micronized basalt in hydrogel-based pellets that can be spread on cropland with standard farm equipment, providing soil nutrients and pH buffering alongside CO2 sequestration. The company is very small (≈2 employees) and early-stage, with no registry-issued credits yet, but the website is live and technically detailed.

name: Carboneers
tech_note: Carboneers develops decentralized biochar projects with smallholder farmers in the Global South, converting agricultural biomass waste (rice, cotton, maize, cocoa residues) into biochar via small-scale pyrolysis kilns.
description: <cite index="5-1,5-2">Carboneers works with farming communities across the Global South to develop biochar and carbon sequestration projects, with a mission to remove 1 million tons of CO2 by 2028.</cite> The company (originally Dutch Carboneers) operates projects in India and Ghana, and is <cite index="9-7,9-8">listed as a supplier on Isometric with a buffer pool for reversal protection</cite>, partnering with Terrafront Ventures and Together for Restoration.

name: Carboneyes
tech_note: Carbonises waste sugarcane bagasse via pyrolysis into biochar, which is donated to smallholder sugarcane farmers for soil application, generating durable carbon removal credits.
description: Carboneyes is a UK-based biochar carbon removal project developer that converts waste bagasse from sugarcane processing into biochar and donates it to smallholder sugarcane farmers, generating carbon credits from the resulting soil carbon storage. The company states it aims to remove over 500,000 tonnes of CO2 and donate over 200,000 tonnes of biochar by 2030.

name: Carbonfuture
tech_note: Carbonfuture operates a digital MRV+ platform and marketplace that connects durable CDR suppliers (biochar, BECCS, DAC, mineralization) with corporate buyers, handling certification, tracking, and credit sales.
description: <cite index="2-1,2-2">Carbonfuture is the Trust Infrastructure for durable carbon removal, centered on Carbonfuture MRV+, a fully integrated, end-to-end solution for monitoring, reporting, and verification of carbon removal projects.</cite> They operate as a marketplace/broker rather than a physical remover, aggregating supply from <cite index="1-6">biochar, BECCS, DACCS, and mineralization projects</cite> across five continents. Clients include Microsoft, Swiss Re, Boeing, and the WEF First Movers Coalition.

name: Carboniferous
tech_note: Biomass sinking
description: Carboniferous, Inc. focuses on Marine Anoxic Carbon Storage (MACS), a method for large-scale carbon dioxide removal by sequestering organic carbon in restricted, anoxic, deep ocean basins.

name: Carbonified
tech_note: Small Canadian carbon project developer focused on biochar, regenerative agriculture, and afforestation/reforestation/revegetation (ARR) carbon removal projects.
description: <cite index="2-1,2-3">Carbonified is a Canadian company providing high-integrity carbon solutions aimed at reversing climate change with measurable impact.</cite> <cite index="11-2,11-3">They focus on biochar, regenerative agriculture, and ARR as scalable carbon sequestration solutions.</cite> They are a small (~3 employees) project developer listed in Carbon Removal Canada's directory.

name: Carbonis
tech_note: Carbonis operates two PYREG P500 pyrolysis plants to produce certified biochar from regional hardwood/softwood forest chips for animal feed, biogas, soil improvement, and industrial applications.
description: Carbonis GmbH & Co. KG is a German biochar producer based in Garrel, Lower Saxony, founded in 2016 as part of the Voßmann agricultural group. The company produces GMP+ certified biochar via dry pyrolysis and sells it across agricultural, livestock, biogas, and industrial segments, with the agricultural application delivering durable carbon storage.

name: Carbonity
tech_note: Biochar
description: Carbonity is a Canadian company that produces premium biochar from FSC-certified woody residues using advanced technology, making it one of the largest industrial-scale biochar plants in North America.

name: Carbonloop
tech_note: Deploys on-site modular biomass thermolysis (HYNOCA, Haffner Energy) to co-produce renewable hydrogen/syngas and biochar, with the biochar serving as the permanent carbon sink.
description: Carbonloop is a French startup (launched 2021, part of the Kouros Group) that offers industrial customers turnkey on-site biomass pyrolysis units producing renewable hydrogen/syngas and biochar, using Haffner Energy's HYNOCA technology. The biochar co-product is sold to the agricultural sector and generates carbon removal credits, while the renewable gas/hydrogen substitutes for fossil fuels in industry and heavy mobility.

name: Carbono Capital
tech_note: Chilean company producing biochar from biomass pyrolysis for soil amendment, compost, and durable carbon removal credits.
description: <cite index="3-1">Carbono Capital SpA is a Chile-based biochar producer whose website emphasizes soil enrichment, carbon sequestration, and promoting healthier ecosystems through biochar</cite>. The company operates as a CDR supplier producing biochar-based compost and carbon credits, though public activity signals and news coverage are limited.

name: Carbons Finland
tech_note: Biochar
description: Carbons Finland Oy is a smartup company founded in 2014 that develops and sells biochar-based products made from Finnish wood, focusing on solutions for stormwater treatment, landscaping, and organic agriculture.

name: Carbonsate
tech_note: Carbonsate selectively harvests encroaching bush biomass and stores it in engineered oxygen-limited dry underground pits to prevent decomposition, issuing Puro.earth-certified CORCs under the Terrestrial Storage of Biomass methodology.
description: Berlin-based Carbonsate (founded 2023) is a carbon removal supplier operating biomass storage projects in Namibia, Cameroon, Colombia, and Bulgaria. Its flagship Otjiwarongo Project in Namibia harvests invasive bush biomass and stores it in engineered oxygen-free pits, and the company issued its first 799 Puro.earth-certified credits in January 2026 as the 100th certified facility on the Puro Registry.

name: Carbonway
tech_note: Building materials
description: Carbonway decarbonizes industry through CO2 mineralization, providing additional revenue to biomethane plants and recyclers for sustainably sequestering carbon dioxide in construction materials.

name: Carbony
tech_note: Carbony deploys Enhanced Rock Weathering by spreading finely ground silicate rock on managed forest land in Central and Eastern Europe to accelerate natural mineral weathering and sequester CO2.
description: Carbony is an Austria-based CDR project developer focused on Enhanced Rock Weathering, uniquely targeting managed forests in Central and Eastern Europe rather than cropland. The company is a member of the Enhanced Weathering Alliance and has corporate partnerships (e.g., Refurbed). Live website and active LinkedIn presence confirm operational status.

name: Carborganic
tech_note: Bio-materials
description: Carborganic produces biocarbon compounding concentrates to defossilize polymers. They offer solutions for compounders and 3D printing applications.

name: Carborok
tech_note: Carborok develops industrial reactors that mineralize biogenic CO2 into recycled concrete, ashes, and alkaline industrial wastes for permanent sequestration.
description: Carborok is a Nantes-based French startup, a spin-off of engineering firm Voltigital, founded in 2021. It designs, builds and operates CO2 mineralization units that sequester biogenic CO2 in recycled concrete and alkaline industrial wastes, and also sells reactors and licenses. The company runs a pilot reactor at Chauvé (Ocaapi project) backed by France2030 and GRDF's bioCO2 sequestration call.

name: Carbuna
tech_note: Biochar
description: Carbuna is a German company that develops, produces, and markets biochar and biochar-based products, transforming raw biochar into readily accessible products that bind CO2 from the atmosphere and store it permanently within soil and materials.

name: Carbyon

description: Carbyon is a Dutch deep-tech startup (TNO spin-off, founded 2019) developing a "fast swing" direct air capture technology that uses thin-film sorbents to capture CO2 in seconds rather than hours. The company unveiled its Carbyon GO outdoor demonstrator at High Tech Campus Eindhoven in September 2025 and raised a €15.3M Series A in 2025, positioning itself as a modular DAC equipment supplier targeting ~€100/tonne.

name: Cardinal Ethanol
tech_note: BECCS
description: Cardinal Ethanol produces high-grade fuel ethanol from corn and is involved in BECCS, with a permit issued for One Carbon Partnership to inject and store CO2 underground at their facility.

name: CarpeCarbon
tech_note: Develops a proprietary energy-efficient Direct Air Capture system that avoids the high energy demands and critical-raw-material dependencies of traditional DAC, targeting permanent geologic storage or utilization of captured CO2.
description: CarpeCarbon is a Turin-based Italian climate-tech startup founded in 2022 that is developing a proprietary, energy-efficient Direct Air Capture (DAC) technology, positioned as the first Italian DAC company. They raised a €1.75M pre-seed round in 2023 from Tech4Planet (CDP Venture Capital), 360 Capital, Club degli Investitori and PiemonteNext to design Italy's first domestically-developed DAC plant in Piedmont.

name: Cascade Climate
tech_note: Nonprofit research organization advancing carbon dioxide removal through geochemical approaches.
description: Cascade Climate is a philanthropically-funded global nonprofit that accelerates progress in open-system carbon dioxide removal (CDR), particularly focusing on enhanced rock weathering (ERW) through platforms, grants, and research.

name: Catch 23
tech_note: Nordic broker/retailer that sells Carbon Removal Certificates (CRCs) from Stockholm Exergi's planned BECCS facility in Värtan, Stockholm.
description: <cite index="3-1,3-2">Catch 23 was founded in 2020 as a Nordic retailer of captured carbon dioxide, working on the brokerage of captured carbon dioxide and communication about the benefits of carbon capture.</cite> <cite index="2-1,2-2">The company sells CRC (Carbon Removal Certificate) credits for negative emissions from Stockholm Exergi's planned BECCS facility in Värtan, Stockholm, targeting Nordic corporate customers.</cite> They do not physically remove CO2 themselves but operate as a sales channel for Stockholm Exergi's removals.

name: Ceal
tech_note: OAE
description: Ceal is an Israeli company focused on Carbon Dioxide Removal (CDR) using the Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement method. Their website indicates they are committed to providing accessible services.

name: Ceezer
tech_note: The CEEZER Carbon Coalition provides start-ups in the voluntary carbon market with the tools needed to bridge the gap between ideation and commercialization, and we are thrilled to announce the sec...
description: Ceezer is a digital platform and marketplace that provides enterprises with access to high-quality carbon removal projects, including biochar, direct air capture, and enhanced rock weathering, enabling them to screen, purchase, and manage negative emissions.

name: Cella Mineral Storage
tech_note: In-situ carbon mineralization via CO2 injection into basalt formations in Kenya's Rift Valley, paired with DAC partners and powered by geothermal/solar.
description: Cella Mineral Storage is a New York-based startup operating carbon mineralization storage in Kenya's Rift Valley, injecting captured CO2 into basaltic volcanic rocks for permanent sequestration. They partner with multiple DAC companies (Octavia, Sirona, RepAir, Greenlyte, Carbon Atlantis) to provide storage services and have sold credits to Frontier (Stripe/Shopify).

name: Charm Industrial
tech_note: Bio-oil
description: Charm Industrial is a carbon sequestration company that converts agricultural waste and biomass into carbon-dense bio-oil and biochar, which is then permanently sequestered underground.

name: Charolina
tech_note: Bio-materials
description: Charolina is a BiCRS company that uses a waste-based material to capture carbon dioxide during direct air capture.

name: Chestnut Carbon
tech_note: Afforestation and improved forest management (IFM) developer planting native, biodiverse forests on marginal crop/pasture lands in the Southeastern U.S. to generate Gold Standard-verified removal credits.
description: <cite index="2-7,2-8,2-9">Chestnut Carbon is a U.S. developer of nature-based carbon removal credits, founded in 2022 with support from asset manager Kimmeridge, that develops forest carbon projects on family-owned forestland and marginal crop and pastureland.</cite> <cite index="5-4,5-5,5-6">The company has planted over 17 million trees across 30,000+ acres of marginal land in the Southeastern U.S., spanning states like Arkansas, Mississippi, Alabama, Louisiana, Texas and Oklahoma, and operates the largest U.S.-based afforestation project listed on the Gold Standard.</cite> It also signed a 25-year, 7 million-ton offtake with Microsoft and closed a $210M non-recourse project finance facility led by J.P. Morgan in 2025.

name: Chevron
tech_note: BECCS
description: Chevron is an energy company involved in developing a bioenergy with carbon capture and sequestration (BECCS) project in California and has invested in other carbon capture technologies.

name: China Energy Engineering Corporation
tech_note: A CEEC subsidiary (CEEC Shanghai System Engineering) co-developed "CarbonBox" with Shanghai Jiao Tong University — a containerized sorbent-based direct air capture module producing 99% pure CO2 with ~100 tpa per module and 600 tpa total pilot capacity.
description: China Energy Engineering Corporation (CEEC / Energy China) is a Chinese state-owned power and infrastructure EPC conglomerate (~RMB 453B revenue in 2025, 115,000+ employees) whose core business is engineering, procurement and construction for power, renewables, grid and infrastructure projects. A CEEC subsidiary, together with Shanghai Jiao Tong University, developed CarbonBox, described as Asia's largest DAC module, which passed reliability testing in July 2024 with intended applications in green methanol, green aviation fuel and carbon trading. CarbonBox remains a pilot-scale R&D effort inside a much larger non-CDR parent, and the envisioned uses lean toward CCU rather than permanent removal.

name: Chooose AS
tech_note: Climate action platform helping airlines and travel companies integrate carbon removal into their services.
description: Chooose AS is a CDR platform/marketplace that provides software solutions for integrating climate action, automating emissions calculations, and offering access to high-quality carbon removal credits. They also focus on accelerating sustainable aviation fuel programs.

name: Circonomy
tech_note: Circonomy develops industrial and artisanal biochar carbon removal projects in the Global South, converting agricultural residues into biochar via pyrolysis and tracking removals with a proprietary digital MRV system.
description: <cite index="15-5,15-6">Circonomy is a biochar carbon removal project developer that partners with agricultural firms to convert biomass into high-quality biochar.</cite> <cite index="4-7,4-9">Since 2022, the company has developed a digital MRV tool and biochar technologies, and is growing into a network across 10 countries in Asia, Africa and Latin America.</cite> <cite index="13-16">Credits are verified and issued under frameworks like Puro.earth and Carbon Standards International.</cite>

name: Circular Carbon
tech_note: Designs, builds, and operates industrial-scale pyrolysis plants ("CarbonHubs") that convert biomass residues (e.g. cocoa shells) into biochar plus renewable process steam for host industrial partners.
description: Circular Carbon is a Hamburg-based company founded in 2018 that operates a first-of-its-kind industrial biochar plant on the Peute site in Hamburg-Veddel, carbonizing cocoa shells from a neighbouring cocoa producer and feeding the co-produced steam back into the partner's factory. The facility is designed to deliver roughly 5,800 tCO2e/yr of carbon removal alongside ~5,000 t/yr of fossil-gas displacement, and the company generates CDR credits from its CarbonHubs while selling certified biochar for soil, animal feed, and industrial uses.

name: Circular Carbon Pathways
tech_note: Biochar production from agricultural residues in Zambia, intended to generate Biochar Carbon Removal (BCR) credits.
description: Circular Carbon Pathways (CCP) is a Zambia-based company that aims to produce Biochar Carbon Removal (BCR) certificates through nature-based decarbonization. The website is minimal with just a tagline, and no recent press, funding, or registry-listed issuances were found. With only 1 employee on LinkedIn and no public signals of operational activity, the company appears to be very early-stage or stalled.

name: Circularity2
tech_note: Biochar
description: Circularity2 is a company focused on industrial-scale biochar production and deployment, developing facilities to produce biocarbon for carbon dioxide removal.

name: City of Scientific Research and Technological Applications
Clairity Technology

description: Clairity Technology is a climate tech startup that develops low-cost, scalable Direct Air Capture (DAC) technology using a solid sorbent approach with alkali carbonate sorbent coated on a ceramic honeycomb substrate to capture CO2, which is then mineralized on-site.

name: Clargreen
tech_note: Pyrolyzes agricultural waste (palm kernel shells, insect frass) into biochar, blended into a branded soil amendment/bio-fertilizer (CO₂ Savior™) for smallholder farmers in Nigeria.
description: Clargreen Technologies is a Nigeria-based climate-smart agribusiness that converts palm kernel shells and insect frass into biochar-based organic fertilizer sold to smallholder farmers. The company aims to monetize carbon removal via Verra and Puro.earth standards, and the founder is a 2025 Founder Institute alumnus actively engaging with the CDR community (e.g., AirMiners).

name: Clean Air Tech
tech_note: Building materials
description: Clean Air Tech focuses on carbon capture and permanent sequestration through mineralization, specifically converting basic oxygen steel (BOS) slag and CO2 into CaCO3 and producing solid carbonates like carbonated recycled concrete aggregate (C-RCA).

name: Clean Energy Systems
tech_note: CES develops proprietary oxy-fuel combustion technology (derived from rocket engine principles) that enables zero-emission power plants with full CO2 capture, deployed for BECCS (Mendota project using agricultural waste biomass) and oxy-fuel CCS for steel, oil & gas, and offshore power.
description: Clean Energy Systems (CES) is an independent California-based technology developer that commercializes oxy-fuel combustion systems for carbon-negative power and industrial decarbonization. It leads the Mendota BECCS project (converting agricultural waste biomass into syngas with ~99% CO2 capture for geologic storage) and has partnerships with PETRONAS/MISC/Aker Solutions (ZEUS offshore demo) and Metal One (green steel).

name: Clean Maine Carbon
tech_note: Operates a rotary-kiln pyrolysis facility in Greenville, Maine, converting low-value Northeastern hardwood biomass into biochar for agriculture, concrete, and remediation applications.
description: <cite index="1-1,1-2,1-3">Clean Maine Carbon purchased the Greenville Steam Biomass facility in Maine in 2017 and started its first biochar facility in July 2023, transforming low-value discarded woody biomass into biochar.</cite> <cite index="6-1,6-2">The company transforms locally sourced woody biomass into premium biochar, repurposing waste and sequestering carbon.</cite> It has issued biochar CORCs on the Puro.earth registry via Flowcarbon as carbon developer.

name: CleanCapture Tech
tech_note: Solid-sorbent direct air capture with a novel plate/heat-exchanger reactor design targeting low-temperature, fully-electric regeneration.
description: CleanCapture Tech is an early-stage U.S. DAC startup founded in 2021 by MIT engineers, developing a solid-sorbent gas/solid reactor for low-cost, mass-producible atmospheric CO2 capture. The company has demonstrated a first-generation design at lab scale with DOE support and is seeking investors/partners to scale up to a commercial unit module.

name: Cler-Verts
tech_note: Cler Verts operates multi-filière organic waste valorization platforms in Occitanie, France, producing biochar via wood pyrolysis alongside compost, biomass fuel, and biogas via methanization.
description: <cite index="9-14">Cler Verts is a French group established in Occitanie since 2003 that collects, treats and valorizes organic matter for communities and professionals, with activities including wood recycling, biomass fuels for boilers, green waste composting, biodéchets valorization, methanization/renewable energy, and biochar and organic soil amendment production.</cite> <cite index="9-10">The company claims to produce the first CE-certified biochar in France.</cite> <cite index="3-11">A new pyrolyzer installation was planned for August 2024.</cite>

name: Climate Impact Partners
tech_note: Voluntary carbon market retailer, broker, and project developer that creates and manages portfolios of carbon credits (both avoidance and removals) and energy attribute certificates for corporate buyers.
description: Climate Impact Partners is a UK/US-based voluntary carbon market specialist formed from the merger of Natural Capital Partners and ClimateCare, offering carbon credit sourcing, portfolio development, MRV support and project origination across 600+ projects in 56 countries. They are a carbon market intermediary rather than a physical CDR supplier — their business is trading and developing credits from third-party projects, including nature-based removals.

name: Climate Vault Solutions
tech_note: Curates a portfolio of third-party CDR projects via an expert-led RFP and sells those credits (alongside compliance-market allowance retirements) to corporates through its software platform.
description: Climate Vault Solutions is a Chicago-based CDR ecosystem company (spun out of a University of Chicago nonprofit) that combines compliance-market carbon allowance vaulting with a curated portfolio of carbon removal credits sourced via its Tech Chamber RFP program (chaired by former U.S. Energy Secretary Ernest Moniz). It resells CDR credits from vetted suppliers (e.g., Octavia Carbon, Carbon Lockdown) through its sales channel and Climate Solutions Platform software to corporate clients. It does not itself remove CO2; it is a curator/broker/platform.

name: ClimateCarbon

KG is part of the ForestFinance Group and is building a carbonization facility in Eberswalde, Germany, with carbonauten GmbH as technology partner responsible for constructing the production plant and marketing the biochar.</cite> <cite index="11-19,11-20">The plant uses three modules each with two carbonization retorts and is designed to produce 4,800 tonnes of biochar per year.</cite> The company is a genuine biochar CDR supplier funded through limited-partner investor participation.

name: ClimatePartner Impact
tech_note: Biochar
description: ClimatePartner Impact drives high-integrity solutions aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), including removal technologies like afforestation, reforestation, and revegetation, and improved cookstoves.

name: ClimeFi
tech_note: Leading portfolio manager for durable carbon removals; provides intelligence and asset management tools for CDR purchasing across all pathways (DAC, BiCRS, mineralization); facilitated CHF 10M+ in CDR purchases; structured first ITMO CDR transfer between Switzerland and Norway under Paris Agreement Article 6.2
description: ClimeFi is a Zurich-based CDR portfolio manager and carbon removal intelligence platform. It helps corporate buyers contract, purchase, and manage CDR across all durable removal pathways (DAC, BiCRS, mineralization). Notably, it structured the first Article 6.2 ITMO CDR transfer between Switzerland and Norway in 2025, and has facilitated over CHF 10 million in CDR purchases.

name: ClimeRock
tech_note: Spreads finely ground basalt from nearby quarries onto French agricultural fields to accelerate silicate weathering, converting atmospheric CO2 into stable bicarbonate.
description: ClimeRock is a French ERW (Enhanced Rock Weathering) startup founded in 2023 and based near Paris, with operations in the Massif Central. It spreads finely ground basalt on agricultural fields to sequester CO2 as bicarbonate while improving soil health, selling removal credits to corporate buyers.

name: Climeworks
tech_note: Solid-sorbent Direct Air Capture using modular collectors paired with geologic mineralization storage via Carbfix in Iceland; also curates multi-pathway removal portfolios.
description: Climeworks is a Swiss-based pioneer in Direct Air Capture, operating the Orca (4,000 tCO2/yr) and Mammoth (36,000 tCO2/yr) DAC plants in Iceland with solid sorbent technology. The company also offers blended carbon removal portfolios combining DAC with nature-based and other engineered solutions for corporate buyers.

name: Climitra
tech_note: Biochar
description: Climitra is an Indian company that provides biomass pyrolysis systems to convert agricultural biomass into high-performance biochar, which serves as a sustainable alternative for coal in industries like steel and for carbon credits.

name: Co-reactive
tech_note: Ex-situ CO2 mineralization of silicate minerals and steel slags into supplementary cementitious materials that permanently sequester CO2 as stable carbonates.
description: Co-reactive is a Düsseldorf-based climate-tech startup, spun out of RWTH Aachen University in 2024, that converts CO2 with silicate minerals (olivine) or metallurgical slags into CO2-negative supplementary cementitious materials (CO-SCMs) via a continuous mineralization process. In January 2026 the company closed a €6.5M seed round led by HTGF to scale from pilot to a 1,000-ton/year demonstration plant in Q2 2026, with industrial-scale plants planned from 2027. CO2 is permanently bound as stable carbonates within the SCM product.

name: Coal Products Limited (CPL)
tech_note: Biochar
description: Coal Products Limited (CPL) has expertise in dealing with and analyzing the potential uses of various biomass char. They currently produce and sell biomass-derived solid products, and previously manufactured activated carbon.

Cotierra

name: Cowboy Clean Fuels

description: Cowboy Clean Fuels (CCF), founded in 2020 and spun out of the University of Wyoming's Center for Biogenic Natural Gas Research, commercializes a patented Biomass Carbon Removal and Storage plus Renewable Natural Gas (BiCRS+RNG) process. Its Triangle Unit project in the Powder River Basin uses agricultural residues injected into deep coal seams to produce RNG while permanently sequestering CO2, and CCF sells durable CDR credits alongside renewable gas.

name: Cquesta

description: Cquesta specializes in harnessing the power of deep-rooted crops, often through gene editing, to enhance soil carbon sequestration and provide farmers with new revenue streams and resilient crops.

name: Cquestr8
tech_note: Reactor-based accelerated carbonation of magnesium-rich silicate minerals to convert CO2 into solid carbonates and stable ocean bicarbonate for permanent storage.
description: Cquestr8 is a UK-based startup (Durham) developing a reactor-based accelerated mineral carbonation process using magnesium-rich silicates to sequester CO2 from industrial sources (biogas, fermentation, cement, lime, steel) as stable carbonates and ocean bicarbonate. Founded in 2020, it raised $300K seed from Counteract in 2021 and was a 2023 SOSV Climate Tech Summit finalist. No significant public news or follow-on funding since 2023, though the UK entity remains registered as Active.

name: Ctrl-S
