It plans to license this archive (including "negative learnings") to remaining DAC developers, large energy firms, and AI-driven materials discovery companies via subscriptions, licensing fees, and royalties. It does not physically remove CO2 itself.

name: Cula
tech_note: Digital MRV platform that automates sensor/machine data capture from CDR projects (mainly biochar pyrolysis) and pushes verified data to crediting registries.
description: Cula Technologies is a digital MRV (Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification) software platform for carbon removal projects, founded in 2023 by Hasso-Plattner-Institut and HHL Leipzig alumni. The company integrates machine, IoT, and sensor data from CDR producers (primarily biochar) and transfers it via API directly into registries like Puro.earth and Carbon Standards International. Cula does not physically remove CO2 — it is an enabling-tech/ecosystem player whose entire business depends on the CDR market.

name: Cultivo
tech_note: Cultivo is a nature-based carbon project developer using an AI/geospatial platform to originate, finance, and operate large-scale land restoration projects (primarily U.S. grasslands soil carbon, plus afforestation, agroforestry, improved forest management, mangrove restoration, and biochar) that generate removal credits.
description: <cite index="6-8,6-9,6-10,6-11">Cultivo is a platform for developing and operating natural assets, partnering with institutional investors and multinational corporations, with a model that generates returns through payments for services, primarily carbon removal, unlocked by land regeneration activities.</cite> They focus heavily on U.S. grasslands but also cover afforestation/reforestation, agroforestry, improved forest management, mangrove restoration, and biochar. <cite index="8-13,8-14,8-15,8-16">Cultivo acquired Kateri, a U.S.-based carbon grasslands project developer, effective December 1, 2025, strengthening its vertically integrated model; combined projects aim to remove over 9 million tonnes CO₂e over 30 years.</cite>

name: DAC Labs

It launched out of stealth in September 2025 with a $3M seed round and its first commercial "Kelvin" product line aimed at e-fuels and CO2 sequestration markets.

name: DACMA GmbH

description: DACMA GmbH is a German company that manufactures and provides high-quality, modular Direct Air Capture (DAC) systems based on solid sorbent technology, offering gigatonne capacities and carbon credits.

name: DACworx

description: <cite index="1-2,1-5,1-6">DACworx is a European DAC technology developer offering cost-efficient, scalable carbon capture for project developers, contractors, and operators aiming for permanent CO₂ removal or production of sustainable chemicals and fuels, via modular standardized designs.</cite> <cite index="1-7,1-8,1-9">The process uses ambient operating conditions and readily available CO₂ filter materials, backed by in-house manufacturing and partnerships across Europe and the U.S.</cite>

name: Dair Capture
tech_note: Early-stage U.S. direct air capture developer claiming a solid-sorbent-style DAC system with a novel regeneration method that produces clean water as a byproduct, targeting both sequestration and CO2 utilization in industries like cement, healthcare, and beverages.
description: Dair Capture is a U.S.-based direct air capture startup developing a DAC technology it claims is roughly 10x cheaper than incumbents, marketed for both carbon sequestration and supply of clean CO2 to industrial users. The company's public footprint is minimal — website only, 0 employees reported on LinkedIn, no registry listings, no funding announcements, and no evidence of deployed hardware or delivered tonnes.

name: Dark Earth Carbon
tech_note: Biochar
description: Dark Earth Carbon specializes in transforming agricultural and forestry waste into biochar through advanced pyrolysis technology, effectively sequestering carbon and enhancing soil.

name: Decarbon

name: Desired Future Conditions

name: Diacarbon Energy

There is no public evidence of recent CDR credit issuances or carbon-removal offtake deals.

name: Direct air capture technology licensed to Knoxville

In late 2024 it signed a record $100/ton, $10M removal deal with Google and demonstrated a ~10 t/yr pilot. In April 2025 Holocene was acquired by Occidental Petroleum's Oxy Low Carbon Ventures, joining Carbon Engineering in Oxy's DAC portfolio.

name: Dotz Nano
tech_note: Dotz Nano develops proprietary amine-modified polymer (AMP) and carbon-based solid sorbents for Direct Air Capture and low-concentration flue-gas CO2 capture, supplying sorbent material to DAC system developers.
description: Dotz Nano (ASX-listed, operating via its Dotz Earth/DOTZearth carbon capture division) is a materials company engineering solid sorbents — including its AMP polymer sorbent — tailored for DAC and point-source CO2 capture. They do not operate DAC plants themselves but supply the core removal-enabling material to DAC developers such as CarbonCapture Inc. Activity remains strong with a first commercial order and new sorbent generation announced in late 2025.

name: Douglas County Forest Products
tech_note: Oregon sawmill that pyrolyzes waste wood chips and sawdust into biochar and sells the resulting carbon removal credits via Puro.earth.
description: Douglas County Forest Products is an independently owned sawmill in Roseburg, Oregon that produces biochar from its wood residues (chips, sawdust) as a side stream. It sells CDR credits on the voluntary market and was listed among the top North American biochar CDR sellers as of early 2025.

name: Dowmann
tech_note: Biochar
description: Dowmann builds and operates factories that remove carbon from the atmosphere by converting biomass waste into biochar through pyrolysis, which is then stored in the soil. They also produce bio-oil and useful bio-chemicals.

name: Drax
tech_note: Drax operates the UK's largest biomass power station and is developing Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Storage (BECCS) projects at Selby (UK) and in the US South via its Elimini carbon removals subsidiary.
description: Drax Group is a UK-listed energy company that generates electricity from wood pellets and is developing BECCS projects to deliver engineered carbon removals. Its Elimini business markets CDRs from planned BECCS plants, though the flagship UK Selby BECCS project has been scaled back amid regulatory and cost uncertainty, and Drax announced staff cuts to its carbon capture division in late 2025.

name: Drax/Elimini
tech_note: BECCS
description: Elimini, a US-based business launched by Drax, is dedicated to permanently removing carbon from the atmosphere by developing a portfolio of Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Storage (BECCS) projects.

name: E-quester
tech_note: Liquid solvent DAC
description: E-quester is a Canadian company that removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere using Direct Air Capture (DAC) with a liquid solvent and an electrochemical regeneration system.

name: EAD
tech_note: EAD operates a pyrolysis/carbonization plant in Darmstadt-Kranichstein that converts urban green-waste biomass into EBC-certified biochar used on municipal green spaces.
description: EAD (Eigenbetrieb für kommunale Aufgaben und Dienstleistungen) is the 100% city-owned municipal services utility of Darmstadt, Germany, responsible for waste management, street cleaning, and composting. As a division of the municipality, it runs a biochar carbonization plant producing EBC-certified biochar products from urban green-space biomass. The biochar activity is a small CDR-relevant operation within a much larger municipal utility.

name: EDAC Labs
tech_note: Liquid solvent DAC
description: EDAC Labs develops an electrosynthesizer device that creates acid and base at half the energy of conventional processes. This system can be used for direct air capture (DAC) using liquid solvent chemistry, as well as other decarbonization activities.

name: EGoS
tech_note: Biochar
description: EGoS GmbH produces biochar-based products, including biochar, feed carbon, and TerraPreta, which are bio-certified and approved for organic farming. They utilize innovative plant technology to generate CO2-negative electricity from synthesis gases produced during the manufacturing process.

name: EM-Süd
tech_note: Biochar
description: EM-Süd is a German family business that produces biochar and other products using Effective Microorganisms (EM) for soil improvement and plant strengthening, contributing to carbon dioxide removal through biochar application.

name: Earth Foundries
tech_note: Biochar
description: Earth Foundries processes woody forest waste into biochar, heat, and energy, addressing wildfire threats and developing biochar markets for soil enhancement, filtration, and stormwater mitigation.

name: Earthcare Solutions
tech_note: Patented thermal gasification of high-ash organic feedstocks (biosolids, manure, MSW digestate) to produce stable biochar while destroying PFAS and microplastics.
description: Earthcare Solutions is a U.S.-based circular waste management company that operates patented thermal gasification systems to convert biosolids, manure, and other organic wastes into biochar (marketed as Ecochar). The company is registered on Puro.earth and sells its biochar for agronomic, remediation, filtration, and animal-bedding uses while also destroying PFAS and microplastics during processing.

name: Earthly
tech_note: Earthly is a UK-based marketplace and platform that curates and resells high-integrity nature-based carbon and biodiversity credits (reforestation, mangroves, regenerative agriculture) to corporate buyers.
description: Earthly is a nature-based carbon credit marketplace that helps businesses invest in vetted reforestation, mangrove, and biodiversity projects via instant purchases, subscriptions, or bespoke portfolios. They assess projects using 106 data points and partnerships with BeZero and Google Earth Engine, acting as a broker/curator rather than a project developer.

name: Earthly Biochar
tech_note: Produces biochar from waste wood via pyrolysis and sells it as a soil amendment, plus manufactures smokeless biochar kilns for gardeners to make their own biochar.
description: Earthly Biochar is a small UK-based biochar producer (incorporated 2018, Salisbury) that makes organic biochar from waste wood and sells it, along with purpose-built smokeless biochar kilns, to gardeners, horticulturists, and land managers. A related entity, Earthly Biochar Industries Ltd (2023), appears aimed at scaling production. The company positions biochar as a negative-emission technology and soil amendment.

name: Earthshot Labs
tech_note: Nature-based carbon credit platform using satellite monitoring and AI for ecosystem restoration verification.
description: Earthshot Labs is a platform that develops and finances nature-based carbon projects, utilizing AI and remote sensing for ecological monitoring and decentralized verification to streamline the compliance process for land stewards and project developers.

name: Ebb Carbon
tech_note: Electrochemical ocean alkalinity enhancement using bipolar membrane electrodialysis integrated with desalination plant brine streams to generate NaOH returned to seawater.
description: Ebb Carbon is a US-based marine CDR supplier using electrochemical ocean alkalinity enhancement (bipolar membrane electrodialysis) to convert desalination brine into alkaline seawater that draws down atmospheric CO2 as stable bicarbonate. The company operates Project Macoma in Port Angeles, WA and runs a demonstration system at PNNL-Sequim. Recent commercial traction includes a 350,000-tonne Microsoft offtake, a 3,500-tonne Google prepurchase (Dec 2025), and a partnership with the Saudi Water Authority.

name: Echo Tech Carbon Corporation
tech_note: Develops biochar production projects via pyrolysis (and gasification) of crop waste, primarily in equatorial regions like Senegal and Uganda, selling durable biochar CDR credits.
description: Echo Tech Carbon Corporation is a Vancouver, Canada-based biochar project developer operating primarily in Africa, converting agricultural residues into biochar for soil amendment and construction materials while generating permanent carbon removal credits. The company is certified/listed via Puro.Earth and Carbonfuture and has inaugurated multiple biochar plants, including a Senegal partnership with rice farmers.

name: EcoAct
tech_note: Climate consultancy and nature-based carbon project developer (afforestation, reforestation, mangrove restoration) supporting corporate net-zero strategies.
description: EcoAct is an international climate and sustainability consultancy and carbon project developer, founded in France in 2006, acquired by Atos in 2020 and then by Schneider Electric in 2023. As of 2025 it has been rebranded as SE Advisory Services, Schneider Electric's global consulting branch, focused on net-zero strategy, carbon accounting, reporting, and nature-based carbon project development (e.g., mangrove restoration, reforestation). They are a consultancy/project-developer in the CDR ecosystem rather than a removal technology supplier.

name: EcoChar
tech_note: Biochar
description: EcoChar develops innovative projects in agroforestry and regenerative agriculture, producing biochar (an agricultural bio-stimulant) or green charcoal briquettes from waste materials.

name: EcoFix
tech_note: Pyrolysis of nut-processing agricultural waste into biochar for carbon sequestration and soil amendment, with the facility developed under Terraton's full-stack biochar platform.
description: EcoFix is a nut processor in Kenya whose agricultural waste is being converted to biochar through a partnership with Terraton Biochar Platform. The "EcoFix Kenya Biochar" facility is listed as a future supplier on Puro.earth and is under review by Isometric, and is expected (together with a Ghana cocoa project) to deliver over 20,000 tonnes of annual CO₂ removal. The biochar project carries the EcoFix name and the host is the operational site for CDR.

name: Ecoera
tech_note: Ecoera pyrolyzes pelletized agricultural residues into biochar at the Skånefrö/Hammenhög facility in southern Sweden, selling Puro.earth-verified CO2 Removal Certificates (CORCs).
description: <cite index="1-1,14-9">Ecoera is a Swedish biochar CDR company founded at Chalmers Ventures in collaboration with Skånefrö AB, and started Sweden's first large-scale biochar carbon removal work in 2009.</cite> <cite index="3-15,3-16">Biochar is produced in Hammenhög, South Sweden, at one of the largest biochar production facilities in the EU using PYREG P500 and P1500 carbonization systems.</cite> <cite index="3-5,3-7">Output is third-party verified under the European Biochar Certificate and the Puro.earth Biochar methodology, and sold as CORC removal credits on carbon marketplaces.</cite>

name: Ecomerit Technologies
tech_note: Uses wind energy to electrolyze sea salt into alkaline constituents that precipitate atmospheric CO2 as mineral carbonates, which sink to ocean depth, combining ocean alkalinity enhancement with mineralization.
description: <cite index="5-3">Ecomerit Technologies is a Santa Barbara-based marine-renewable product design studio and laboratory founded in 2010 by Jim and Brent Dehlsen</cite>, developing the Precipitor CDR system alongside Aquantis marine current turbines, Anacapa wave energy generators, and SeaWell desalination buoys. <cite index="15-9">The CO2 Precipitor project pursues atmospheric CDR via mineralization and OAE with durable carbon sequestration at ocean depth</cite>, mounting systems on offshore wind turbines, ships, and platforms. They are a CDR technology developer (supplier) operating at early/R&D scale.

name: Econew
tech_note: Continuous slow-pyrolysis of certified eucalyptus forestry residues producing high-fixed-carbon biochar for carbon removal credits.
description: Econew is a Brazilian clean bioenergy company based in northern Minas Gerais that produces biochar via continuous pyrolysis of FSC®/PEFC-certified eucalyptus residues. <cite index="11-1,11-2">Their continuous pyrolysis process converts FSC®/PEFC-certified eucalyptus residues into biochar with a high fixed-carbon content, with each ton of confirmed CO₂ removal corresponding to one carbon credit available in the voluntary market.</cite> They align with Puro.earth standards for permanent carbon removal credits.

name: Ecotree
tech_note: Sustainable forestry company allowing individuals and businesses to invest in European forests for carbon offsetting.
description: EcoTree specializes in Afforestation/Reforestation (A/R) by managing forests across Europe, offering nature-based solutions for carbon sequestration and biodiversity restoration, and providing high-quality, third-party verified carbon credits.

name: Eion
tech_note: Eion applies pulverized olivine to US farmland as a replacement for agricultural lime, using a patented direct soil-sampling MRV method to measure CO2 removed via enhanced rock weathering.
description: Eion is a US-based enhanced rock weathering supplier that deploys olivine (sourced from Sibelco's Norwegian quarry) across farmland in the US Midwest and South via partnerships with ag cooperatives like Growmark. The company has delivered credits to Stripe and signed offtakes with Microsoft and a $33M Frontier agreement covering 78,707 tons between 2027-2030. It holds a patent on direct soil-sampling MRV for ERW.

name: Eion Carbon
tech_note: Applied pelletized olivine to cropland to accelerate silicate weathering, with patented soil-based tracer MRV to quantify CO2 removal as bicarbonate.
description: Eion was a U.S.-based enhanced rock weathering (ERW) carbon removal company that applied crushed olivine on agricultural fields to permanently sequester atmospheric CO2 while improving soil pH. It pioneered olivine-based deployments and a patented soil-tracer MRV approach, delivering ERW credits to Stripe and contracting removal with Microsoft. In February 2026, Terradot acquired Eion's assets, contracts (100,000+ tons), IP, and team, effectively ending Eion as a standalone entity.

name: Ekovilla
tech_note: The environmental impact of Ekovilla’s work goes well beyond avoided emissions. The company has started to modernized its production equipment, cutting electricity use per kilogram of product from ...
description: Ekovilla manufactures wooden building elements, specifically insulation products made from recycled wood fiber, which remove carbon from the atmosphere and offer durable carbon capture and storage.

name: Eleryc
tech_note: Liquid solvent DAC
description: No information about Eleryc's operations or specific CDR method was found in the search results, beyond the initial prompt.

name: Enable Earth
tech_note: Biochar
description: Enable Earth is a pioneering biochar initiative based in Thailand that develops industrial biochar carbon removal projects from agricultural wastes to tackle pollution and improve soil.

name: EnergieWerk Ilg GmbH
tech_note: Operates wood-fired SYNCRAFT gasifier CHP plants in Dornbirn, Austria producing biochar and green heat/power, with a newly commissioned Bright Renewables CO2 capture & liquefaction system (BECCS) added in 2025.
description: EnergieWerk Ilg GmbH is a family-owned regional energy company in Dornbirn, Vorarlberg, Austria that runs wood-chip gasification CHP plants producing biochar alongside renewable electricity and district heat. In 2025 it commissioned a Bright Renewables carbon capture and liquefaction unit on its gasifier, moving it from pure biochar production into BECCS-style biogenic CO2 capture.

name: Energnist CaptureCo
tech_note: Post-combustion carbon capture on a municipal waste-to-energy (incineration) plant in Esbjerg, Denmark; the biogenic fraction of the flue gas yields negative emissions when permanently stored.
description: <cite index="19-20,19-21">Energnist is West Denmark's largest waste-to-energy company, owned by 16 municipalities and operating waste-energy plants in Esbjerg and Kolding.</cite> Energnist CaptureCo A/S is its dedicated carbon-capture subsidiary developing a CCS facility at the Esbjerg plant to capture over 200,000 tonnes of CO2 per year, with transport via pipeline to an Esbjerg Harbour CO2 terminal for liquefaction and permanent storage. <cite index="16-1,16-5,16-6">It is one of 10 companies prequalified by the Danish Energy Agency to compete for DKK 28.7 billion in CCS funding</cite>, and <cite index="11-1,11-2">signed a letter of intent with Carbon Circle in April 2026 to jointly develop the capture project using Carbon Circle's CaCiMod modular system.</cite>

name: Energy Farmers
tech_note: Biochar
description: Energy Farmers Australia upcycles organic waste to produce bioenergy and biochar using their own pyrolysis technology. They supply biochar and biochar-based products to Australian farmers and industry.

name: Energy Ocean
tech_note: Biochar
description: Energy Ocean GmbH, also known as Swiss Biochar, produces high-quality biochar from natural wood sourced from the Luthern region of Switzerland.

name: Engrow
tech_note: Operates zero-emission continuous carbonization/pyrolysis units in South India that convert fast-growing hardwood energy-plantation biomass into enriched biochar (used as soil amendment) plus co-products such as bio-furnace oil and briquettes.
description: <cite index="20-3,20-5">Engrow Carbon Energy Private Limited is an India-based biochar producer incorporated in May 2019 and registered in Erode, Tamil Nadu.</cite> <cite index="11-11,11-13">The company converts biomass residues into energy and soil amendments via pyrolysis and gasification, and its thermochemical plant generates carbon reduction credits by producing bio-furnace oil and biochar.</cite> <cite index="13-1">It is named by the International Biochar Initiative among biochar producers actively scaling projects in India.</cite>

name: Enhanced rock weathering start
tech_note: Applied olivine (optimized for fast weathering) to agricultural land and used a patented direct-measurement MRV approach based on immobile trace elements in soil samples to quantify CO2 removal.
description: <cite index="8-2">Eion was a U.S.-based enhanced rock weathering (ERW) company known for pioneering olivine-based deployments and an early track record of technical innovation, including some of the first issued ERW credits.</cite> <cite index="9-3,9-5">In February 2026, ERW firm Terradot acquired Eion, including its commitment to deliver 8,000 tons of carbon removal credits to Microsoft under a deal signed in 2024.</cite> Eion's assets, IP, team, and contracts are now integrated into Terradot.

name: Enhanced rock weathering startup Eion predicts dramatic growth as DOE pumps $35m into CO2 removal
tech_note: Eion applies crushed olivine (sourced from Sibelco in Norway) on US farmland as a replacement for ag lime, using a patented direct soil-measurement MRV method to quantify CO2 removed via enhanced rock weathering.
description: Eion is a US-based enhanced rock weathering CDR supplier founded in 2020 that deploys olivine on Midwest and Southeast farmland and sold credits to Stripe, Frontier, and Microsoft. In February 2026 Eion was acquired by Terradot to form a combined global ERW platform, with Eion's operations, team, and 100,000+ tonnes of contracts folded into Terradot.

name: Enhanced rock weathering startup Eion secures $33m carbon removal offtake deal with Frontier
tech_note: Eion applies pulverized olivine to U.S. farmland as a substitute for ag lime, accelerating natural silicate weathering to permanently sequester CO2 as bicarbonate, with a patented soil-sample-based direct measurement MRV approach.
description: Eion is a U.S.-based enhanced rock weathering (ERW) carbon removal supplier that spreads crushed olivine on farmland across the Midwest, South, and Mid-Atlantic. It has delivered ERW credits to Stripe and signed offtakes with Microsoft and Frontier (78,707 tons, ~$33M). In February 2026, Eion was acquired by Terradot to form a combined global ERW platform, making it a division of Terradot.

name: Enhanced rock weathering startup Eion strikes carbon removal deal with Microsoft, raises $3m series A extension
tech_note: Eion applies pulverized olivine (sourced from Sibelco) to US farmland as a replacement for ag lime, using a patented direct soil-sampling measurement approach to quantify CO2 removed via enhanced rock weathering.
description: Eion is a US-based enhanced rock weathering carbon removal company that pioneered olivine-based deployments on Mid-Atlantic and Midwest farmland, delivering early ERW credits to Stripe, Frontier ($33M offtake), and Microsoft (8,000 tons). In February 2026, Eion was acquired by Terradot to form a combined global ERW platform with over 400,000 tonnes of contracted carbon removal; Eion's operations, contracts, and team were folded into Terradot.

name: Enrzi
tech_note: Biochar
description: Enrzi is a company committed to revolutionizing the energy sector with innovative biomass pyrolysis solutions, sharing expert opinions about sustainability through their blog.

name: EnviraPAC
tech_note: Biochar
description: EnviraPAC Monticello LLC manufactures renewable carbon materials for industrial applications and biochar for agricultural applications using high-temperature pyrolysis.

name: Envisgas
tech_note: Biochar
description: Envigas builds, owns, and operates high-precision, large-scale pyrolysis plants to convert organic residuals into premium quality BioCarbon and energy. They produce and sell high-quality fossil-free products from a specially developed pyrolysis process using biomass such as forest residues as raw material.

name: Ephemeral
tech_note: Accelerates natural silicate rock weathering by grinding alkaline minerals and deploying them in shallow coastal ocean waters, increasing ocean alkalinity and converting CO2 into stable bicarbonates/carbonates.
description: <cite index="13-2,13-3">Ephemeral Carbon is an unfunded company based in Santa Clara, United States, founded in 2023 by Josh Perfetto, operating as a provider of carbon removal solutions.</cite> <cite index="15-2,15-3">The company specializes in the permanent removal of CO2 through Oceanic Enhanced Weathering, grinding alkaline rock into sand which is then deployed in ocean waters to neutralize acidity and restore marine ecosystems.</cite> It is a pre-revenue, early-stage OAE supplier focused on field trials and community engagement.

name: Equatic
tech_note: Equatic uses a patented seawater electrolysis process combined with direct air contacting to permanently sequester CO2 as dissolved bicarbonate and solid carbonate minerals, while co-producing carbon-negative hydrogen.
description: <cite index="8-3">Founded in 2021, California-based Equatic has developed an electrolytic process for atmospheric carbon removal that accelerates the ocean's ability to absorb and permanently store massive amounts of carbon, while producing carbon negative hydrogen as a co-product.</cite> The company is a UCLA spin-out operating pilot plants in Los Angeles and Singapore, and is building the Equatic-1 demonstration plant in Singapore plus a planned commercial facility in Quebec with Deep Sky. <cite index="8-2">In August 2025 Equatic raised $11.6 million in a Series A funding round</cite> led by Temasek Trust's C3H and Kibo Invest.

name: Equilibrium
tech_note: Operates biochar pyro-gasification facilities using invasive biomass and crop residues, plus agroforestry, regenerative agriculture, and mangrove restoration projects with proprietary dMRV.
description: Equilibrium (operating entity Climeverse Pvt. Ltd.) is an India-based full-stack carbon removal project developer running biochar, agroforestry, regenerative agriculture, and mangrove restoration projects across nine Indian states. It operates a Puro.earth-listed biochar facility (Mundargi/Murudagiri) that pyro-gasifies invasive Prosopis juliflora and corn cobs, and raised $3M seed funding in September 2025 from Kalaari Capital, Peak XV Partners, and Avaana Capital.

name: Equinor/Rolls Royce
tech_note: Liquid-solvent (amine-based, water-based absorbent) Direct Air Capture system originally developed by Rolls-Royce with CSIRO, whose IP and assets Equinor acquired in April 2024; Rolls-Royce continues as test operator at the Derby Test Bed 52 demonstrator.
description: Equinor is a Norwegian energy major that in April 2024 acquired Rolls-Royce's liquid-solvent DAC technology IP and novated the UK DESNZ-funded Project ENCORE contract, taking ownership of a demonstrator plant that has captured over 100 tonnes CO2/year at Rolls-Royce's Derby campus. The program is now an internal DAC development effort within Equinor, targeting a capture cost below USD 200/t, and sits alongside Equinor's other CDR/CCS activities (Northern Lights, RepAir, Captura).

name: Euthenia Energy Group
tech_note: Produces biochar via Beston BST-30 pyrolysis of olive-grove agricultural residues in Andalusia, Spain, issuing Puro-certified CORC credits.
description: Euthenia Energy Group operates a biochar production facility in Lucena, Andalusia (Spain), converting olive orchard agricultural waste into biochar via Beston BST-30 pyrolysis technology. The company is registered on Puro.earth, has issued CORCs under the Biochar methodology, and co-hosted the 2025 European Biochar CDR Conference in Málaga in October 2025.

name: Everest Carbon
tech_note: Everest Carbon develops a patent-pending in-field alkalinity sensor with IoT connectivity that directly measures carbonate alkalinity efflux to provide real-time MRV for Enhanced Rock Weathering projects.
description: <cite index="7-1,7-2">Everest Carbon was founded in late 2022 as an ERW project developer, but at the end of 2023 its co-founders pivoted the company to commercialize its proprietary sensor.</cite> The company now sells hardware and software that enables ERW project developers to measure carbon removal in the field, <cite index="9-26">aiming to reduce MRV costs by over 90%.</cite> They are a technology supplier building core removal-enabling infrastructure for the ERW pathway.

name: Evero Energy
tech_note: Evero retrofits its waste-wood biomass power plants (Ince BioPower and Mersey Bioenergy) with MHI amine-solvent carbon capture, storing biogenic CO₂ in depleted Irish Sea gas fields via the HyNet cluster.
description: <cite index="3-10">Evero Energy Group Limited (previously known as Bioenergy Infrastructure Group) is a UK low-carbon waste-to-energy company partnering with Mitsubishi Heavy Industries to deliver its InBECCS (Ince Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Storage) project.</cite> <cite index="2-7,2-8,2-9">The company is retrofitting CCS onto its existing Ince Biopower and Mersey Bioenergy plants, which already process over 300,000 tonnes of waste wood into renewable electricity, with the addition generating up to 400,000 tons of CDRs per annum.</cite> <cite index="5-2,5-4,5-5">Its InBECCS project was listed on Puro.earth's Future Facility program in December 2025, making it the first and only UK BECCS project included in that program.</cite>

name: Evident
tech_note: Evident operates C-Capsule, a carbon removal registry and standard for durable CDR credits (Carbon Removal Units), building on its global environmental certificate registry expertise (I-RECs).
description: <cite index="3-1,3-2">Evident is a global sustainability certification firm with over two decades of expertise in establishing trusted renewable energy markets</cite>. <cite index="3-10,3-11,3-12">Its C-Capsule product is a standard and registry for durable Carbon Dioxide Removal that certifies only carbon that has been permanently removed from the atmosphere</cite>. <cite index="1-6,1-7">The C-Capsule registry issues CDR credits through partnerships such as with Cowboy Clean Fuels and Absolute Climate, aimed at meeting quality, traceability, and verification expectations</cite>.

name: Exomad Green
tech_note: Industrial pyrolysis (~600°C, Beston BST-50 units) of hardwood sawmill residues into high-carbon biochar (86% organic C, H:C 0.24) donated to indigenous farmers, generating Puro.earth CORCs.
description: Exomad Green is the biochar/CDR division of Exomad, Bolivia's largest wood exporter. It converts hardwood forestry residues from ABT-certified sawmills into biochar via pyrolysis at Riberalta and Concepción facilities, with credits certified under Puro.earth. It is among the largest biochar CDR suppliers globally, notably signing a 1.24M-tonne 10-year offtake with Microsoft in May 2025.

name: Explocom
tech_note: Produces biochar and wood vinegar via patented pyrolysis of wood waste at an industrial facility in Harghita County, Romania, with EBC certification and Puro.earth CORC listing.
description: <cite index="15-12,15-13">Explocom GK SRL is a production company of biochar-based products located in Lupeni Jud-Harghita, Romania, and its products are EBC certified.</cite> <cite index="10-5,10-6,10-7">The firm is a manufacturer of organic chemicals and a producer of charcoal and bulk char, which added wood waste to its production in 2007, and through Innovation Norway financing developed biochar, wood vinegar, wood oil and cellulosic alcohol products.</cite> The company is listed as a biochar supplier on the Puro.earth registry.

name: Exterra
tech_note: Ex-situ accelerated mineral carbonation that converts asbestos mine tailings into reactive magnesium oxides (LOW process) then reacts them with CO2 to form stable carbonate minerals (ROC process), while co-producing nickel and silica byproducts.
description: Exterra Carbon Solutions is a Quebec-based cleantech company that transforms legacy asbestos mine tailings into low-carbon critical minerals (magnesium oxide, nickel concentrate, amorphous silica) while permanently mineralizing CO2. The company raised a CAD $20M Series A in May 2025 and is developing Hub I, scheduled to begin construction in 2027, which it claims will become the world's largest asbestos mitigation plant. Exterra partners with BASF, Énergir, WSP and Winsome Resources to deploy its LOW and ROC processes at industrial scale.

name: ExxonMobil
tech_note: ExxonMobil Low Carbon Solutions is running an in-house solid-sorbent Direct Air Capture pilot at its Baytown, Texas facility, alongside a broader CCS business built on the Denbury pipeline network.
description: ExxonMobil is a major integrated oil and gas company whose Low Carbon Solutions division operates a proprietary DAC pilot (started February 2024 in Baytown, TX) after ending its partnership with Global Thermostat. The division also runs large-scale point-source CCS operations leveraging Denbury's CO2 pipeline infrastructure, with CEO Darren Woods calling DAC the "holy grail" of emissions technologies while targeting a 50% cost reduction from the current $600-$1,000/ton range.

name: FETZER Rohstoffe + Recycling
tech_note: Operates three pyrolysis plants producing ~1,500 m³/year of biochar from wood chips and spelt husks under the "Moola" brand, with waste heat reused in the adjacent recycling facility.
description: FETZER Rohstoffe + Recycling GmbH is a German recycling company based in Eislingen that has been producing biochar from wood waste for over a decade under its Moola brand. EBC-certified since 2013, its three pyrolysis plants produce around 1,500 m³ of biochar per year, which is primarily sold as a soil amendment. Biochar credits are offered via marketplaces such as Klimate.

name: FS
tech_note: FS captures fermentation CO2 from its corn-ethanol biorefinery in Lucas do Rio Verde (Mato Grosso, Brazil) and injects it ~800m+ underground into the Diamantino formation for permanent geological storage.
description: <cite index="5-3">FS Agrisolutions Indústria de Biocombustíveis Ltda is a joint venture between Summit Brazil Renewables (a subsidiary of Summit Agricultural Group) and Tapajós Participações</cite> and is Brazil's largest corn-based ethanol producer. <cite index="6-5">The BECCS project will prevent the release of approximately 423,000 tons of CO2 into the atmosphere per year from operations in Lucas do Rio Verde</cite>, with <cite index="7-7">construction expected to start once licensing approvals are granted and CO2 injection operations targeted to begin by July 2026</cite>. <cite index="7-4,7-12">FS has signed forward credit sale agreements with Pinheiro Neto Advogados, SLB, and Rubicon Carbon & YvY Capital, with the credits classified as removal credits under the Gold Standard methodology</cite>.

name: FabricNano/Veolia
tech_note: Immobilizes carbonic anhydrase enzyme onto large-particle basalt/silicate rock to catalytically accelerate enhanced rock weathering on agricultural land.
description: FabricNano is a London-based biotechnology startup that develops enzyme-immobilization technology, most notably applying the carbonic anhydrase enzyme to basalt rock fines to accelerate enhanced rock weathering. In partnership with Veolia UK, the company ran a world-first field trial near Bicester (UK) spreading enzyme-coated basalt on farmland to accelerate CO2 sequestration from decades to a few years. The firm also applies its enzyme platform to non-CDR applications (bio-manufacturing with Ginkgo/Sumitomo, PFAS research), so CDR is one of multiple product lines.

name: Fasera Holdings
tech_note: Fasera pyrolyzes spent eucalyptus biomass (left over from steam distillation of eucalyptus oil from mallee plantations) to produce biochar and wood vinegar, generating CORCs under Puro.earth and ACCUs from associated plantings.
description: Fasera Holdings is an Australian company that operates oil mallee plantations in Western Australia, producing eucalyptus oil, biochar, and wood vinegar. Its biochar is listed as a Puro.earth supplier (Fasera Biochar Plant 1) and it also generates Australian Carbon Credit Units from its plantations. CDR is a core integrated product line alongside eucalyptus oil, qualifying it as a supplier.

name: Fidelis
tech_note: BECCS
description: Fidelis, through its portfolio company AtmosClear, is developing a Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Storage (BECCS) project in Louisiana to provide durable carbon removal.

name: Fiora Mara
tech_note: Biomass sinking
description: Fiora Mara is a marine carbon dioxide removal (CDR) startup that leverages seaweed farming in the open ocean to sequester atmospheric carbon and revitalize oceans.

name: First Climate
tech_note: Carbon project developer, financier, and credit marketer specialising in biochar and nature-based removal credits — they do not operate removal hardware themselves but certify and offtake credits from partner pyrolysis and forestry projects.
description: First Climate is a 25-year-old German/Swiss carbon management services firm that develops, finances, sources, certifies, and markets verified emission reduction and carbon removal credits (especially biochar) from partner projects worldwide, alongside climate strategy consulting and green energy procurement. They do not operate removal technology themselves — e.g., the CARBONITY biochar plant in Canada uses Airex Energy pyrolysis technology, with First Climate acting as the offtake/certification/marketing partner. CDR project development is a core part of their business, placing them in the CDR ecosystem as a developer/broker rather than a technology supplier.

name: Flux
tech_note: Flux crushes silicate (basalt) rock and spreads it on smallholder farmland in Kenya (and, via partnership, Cameroon) to accelerate weathering, remove atmospheric CO2, and boost crop yields, selling verified ERW removal credits.
description: <cite index="5-4,5-5">Flux is a Nairobi-based climate startup that has sold Africa's first carbon dioxide removal credits based on the practice of using crushed basalt to absorb CO2, pre-selling credits for 540 tons of CO2 removal via enhanced rock weathering.</cite> <cite index="6-13,6-14">Flux is working to unlock the potential of ERW across Africa, aiming to sequester hundreds of millions of tonnes of CO2 while improving soils and yields for millions of farmers across the continent.</cite> <cite index="10-13">The company has also signed on to work with African Food Security on a 205,000-hectare maize farming project in Cameroon.</cite>

name: Fondation pour l’innovation en Cadiométabolisme et Nutrition
Forge Minerals
tech_note: Building materials
description: Forge Minerals utilizes advanced mineralization techniques to efficiently and permanently store carbon dioxide from biogenic emissions as mineral solids.

name: Forward
tech_note: Svante manufactures solid-sorbent nanoengineered filters (using metal-organic frameworks/CALF-20) and rotary adsorption machines (RAM) for post-combustion point-source carbon capture and direct air capture, and is developing BECCS projects via its Carbon Alpha acquisition.
description: Svante Inc. (website tagline "Forward-Thinking Carbon Capture") is a Vancouver/Burnaby-based carbon capture technology company that builds solid-sorbent filters and rotary contactor machines for industrial point-source CCS, BECCS and DAC. In May 2025 it commissioned its Redwood gigafactory in Burnaby and acquired Carbon Alpha, adding the North Star BECCS project which signed a 626,000-tonne CDR offtake with Microsoft. It also supplies filters to Climeworks and is partnering with Nikkiso on Canada's first DAC facility.

name: Freres Lumber
tech_note: Freres operates a 100% biomass-fired cogeneration boiler at its Lyons, Oregon wood-products mill; biochar is recovered as a byproduct and sold as Puro.earth-certified CORCs.
description: Freres Lumber (Freres Engineered Wood) is a family-owned Oregon manufacturer of plywood, veneer, and Mass Ply engineered wood products whose biomass cogeneration facility produces biochar as a byproduct. The biochar project is registered on Puro.earth and has supplied CORCs to Microsoft via ACT Group. Biochar is a secondary revenue line to the core lumber business, but the firm is a bona fide supplier of durable carbon removal credits.

name: Freshean
tech_note: Develops a nano-engineered solid sorbent ("Nano-in-Nano" platform) for Direct Air Capture, with an HVAC-integrated DAC + chemical filter product aimed at semiconductor fabs and office buildings.
description: Freshean is a Phoenix, Arizona nanotechnology startup founded in 2017 by Dr. Xiwang Qi, developing a nano-engineered solid sorbent for Direct Air Capture alongside indoor air pollution solutions. The company claims a proprietary "Nano-in-Nano" platform for improved CO2 capture efficiency and cost, and participated in the Venture for ClimateTech Cohort 4 in mid-2024 and presented at SEMICON West 2024. Per Tracxn (March 2026), Freshean remains unfunded, with minimal LinkedIn footprint (1 employee), suggesting it is an early-stage R&D/licensing outfit rather than an operating removal supplier.

name: Frontier Infrastructure Holdings
tech_note: Captures biogenic CO2 from ethanol refineries, transports via rail (Union Pacific), and permanently sequesters it in a Class VI well at the Sweetwater Carbon Storage Hub in Wyoming.
description: Frontier Infrastructure Holdings is a Tailwater Capital-backed developer of low-carbon infrastructure across the US Mountain West and Texas, specializing in BECCS by capturing biogenic CO2 from ethanol refineries and transporting it via rail to its Sweetwater Carbon Storage Hub in Wyoming for permanent geologic sequestration. The company has signed offtake deals (e.g. 120,000 tonnes with Wild Assets) and partnerships with Baker Hughes, Gevo/Verity, and Union Pacific.

name: Funga
tech_note: Funga inoculates tree seedlings and forest soils with native mycorrhizal fungal communities (identified via DNA sequencing and ML) to accelerate tree growth and carbon sequestration in working forests, primarily loblolly pine in the southeastern US.
description: <cite index="9-1">Funga is a public benefit corporation focused on restoring the power of fungal biodiversity to working forests, thereby accelerating tree growth and carbon drawdown.</cite> They operate forest microbiome restoration projects in the southeastern US loblolly pine belt and sell nature-based carbon removal credits to corporate buyers. <cite index="3-1">In November 2024 Funga secured its first major deal to deliver more than 500,000 tons of carbon removal to a major corporate buyer.</cite>

name: Förvaltnings AB Helje
tech_note: Biochar
description: Förvaltnings AB Helje is a real estate company that owns facilities, including biochar production at Essunga Plantskola AB, and sells the produced biochar.

name: GE Vernova
tech_note: Solid sorbent direct air capture using temperature/pressure/concentration swing desorption, developed at GE Vernova's Advanced Research Centers.
description: GE Vernova is a publicly traded global energy company (NYSE: GEV) whose DAC program, run out of its Advanced Research Centers in Niskayuna, NY and Bengaluru, India, is developing proprietary solid-sorbent direct air capture technology. The company commissioned a 10-ton/year DAC test facility in New York and in September 2025 announced a partnership with Deep Sky to deploy a 1,500 tonne/year DAC unit at Deep Sky Alpha in Innisfail, Alberta, with operations scheduled to begin in late 2026.

name: Gaia
tech_note: BECCS
description: Gaia is a BiCRS company based in Denmark that utilizes Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Storage (BECCS) to convert municipal waste into energy and remove CO2 from the atmosphere.

name: Gaia Refinery
tech_note: Gaia Refinery is developing a hybrid Bio-DAC system combining liquid-solvent direct air capture with biomass carbon removal (BiCRS), using biogenic acetic acid and fuel cells to capture CO2 at low energy demand for industrial integration.
description: <cite index="2-4">Halifax-based Gaia Refinery was founded in 2020 by Dr. Tammy Cai and Genny Shaw to scale up carbon removal systems</cite>. <cite index="4-1,4-2">The company has developed a dual-capture process that combines biomass carbon removal (BiCRS) with direct air capture (DAC) to remove CO2 from the atmosphere and biogenic sources, designed for integration into industrial operations</cite>. They are a Canadian CDR technology developer (supplier), backed by accelerators including Brinc, Hatcher+, Kiloton Fund, and CICE's Women in Climate Tech program.

name: Gary Climate Solutions
tech_note: BECCS
description: Gary Climate Solutions is a Carbon Capture and Storage developer that partners with industrial emitters to provide a turnkey solution for capturing, transporting, and permanently sequestering carbon dioxide.

name: Geolocked
tech_note: Geolocked sequesters carbon by burying biomass and landfill waste underground for permanent storage.
description: <cite index="11-1,11-2,11-3,11-4">Geolocked operates in carbon sequestration, focusing on the removal of carbon by utilizing biomass and landfill waste, which it stores underground. It is based in Houston, Texas.</cite> The company applied to Frontier's 2025 Summer prepurchase round, indicating active participation in the CDR supplier market.

name: Gevo (Red Trail Energy)
tech_note: BECCS
description: Gevo (formerly Red Trail Energy) operates an ethanol production facility in North Dakota that captures and sequesters CO2 underground, generating carbon removal credits through BECCS.

name: GigaDAC/Victory Over Carbon
tech_note: Spray-based liquid-solvent DAC contactor designed around aerospace airflow engineering to reduce build and operating costs at gigaton scale.
description: GigaDAC (legal name Victory Over Carbon Inc.) is a Houston-based DAC startup spun out of Rice Alliance and resident at Greentown Labs, developing a spray-and-aerodynamic-separator contactor to replace filter/cooling-tower designs. The company has received NSF SBIR funding and was building a commercial-scale pilot targeted for early 2025, with plans to sell removal credits and claim 45Q. Small team (~4 employees) in early R&D stage.

name: Gigablue
tech_note: Deploys engineered particles (nutrient shell + gravity-controlling core) in the ocean to stimulate phytoplankton growth and sink the resulting biomass to the deep sea for long-term carbon storage.
description: Gigablue is an ocean-based CDR startup (founded in Israel, headquartered in New York) that uses geo-specific engineered particles to grow phytoplankton and sink captured carbon to the deep ocean. It has completed multiple trials off New Zealand, signed a 200,000-ton offtake with SkiesFifty, and is pursuing a Puro.earth methodology, though its approach has drawn scientific scrutiny over parallels to iron fertilization.

name: Gigafex
tech_note: Gigafex operates proprietary pyrolysis reactors that convert palm oil mill empty fruit bunch (EFB) biomass into biochar for permanent carbon removal and soil application.
description: <cite index="4-1,4-2">Gigafex helps palm oil mills turn EFB biomass into biochar and verifiable carbon removal credits using proprietary, patent-pending pyrolysis reactors purpose-built for EFB biomass that integrate into existing mill operations at industrial scale.</cite> The company markets the resulting biochar as both a stable carbon removal pathway and a soil amendment that reduces reliance on chemical fertilizers.

name: Giner
tech_note: Develops an electrochemical DAC system using KOH capture solution coupled with a hydrogen-assisted carbonate electrolyzer to regenerate purified CO2 at low voltage.
description: Giner, Inc. is a Newton, Massachusetts-based electrochemical R&D firm founded in 1973 with a broad portfolio spanning fuel cells, electrolyzers, batteries, biomedical devices, and aerospace technologies. Within that portfolio they are developing a lab-scale Direct Air Capture system that uses a concentrated KOH air contactor paired with a hydrogen-assisted carbonate electrolyzer to capture and regenerate purified CO2, a project funded through DOE's DAC Pre-Commercial Technology Prize. DAC is one of several research lines rather than the company's principal business, but Giner is building the removal technology itself rather than buying credits.

name: Glanris
tech_note: Glanris pyrolyzes rice husks into Biocarbon® biochar that functions as a dual-function water filtration medium (removing metals and organics) while sequestering carbon durably.
description: <cite index="12-9,12-10,12-11,12-12">Glanris specializes in the production of biocarbon biochar, with offerings including biochar for water filtration and soil enhancement, as well as an additive in cement and concrete, all derived from processed agricultural waste such as rice husks. It was founded in 2018 and is based in Olive Branch, Mississippi.</cite> <cite index="11-2,11-3">Its Biocarbon filtration biochar was declared net CO2 negative via a Life Cycle Assessment with Accend, a Puro.Earth partner, and was added to the Puro.Earth CORC exchange.</cite>

name: GoBiochar
tech_note: Bulk biochar supply, consulting, and distribution for agricultural and soil regeneration applications, sourcing customer-specific biochar across multiple feedstocks.
description: GoBiochar LLC is a Salt Lake City, Utah-based biochar supply and consulting company that sources and distributes bulk biochar to agriculture, climate tech, and heavy industry clients across North America. Founded and led by John Webster (also Development Director for Biochar On Site and former Communications Director at US Biochar Initiative), the firm produces customer-specific biochar across a range of feedstocks and supports projects from concept to delivery. Their focus is primarily agricultural/soil amendment with carbon sequestration co-benefits rather than explicit CDR credit issuance.

name: Goal 300
tech_note: Applies finely crushed basalt to agricultural soils to accelerate silicate weathering, capturing CO₂ as stable bicarbonates while improving soil pH and fertility.
description: Goal 300 is a US-based (Oregon/Pacific Northwest) Enhanced Rock Weathering supplier that partners with landowners to apply crushed basalt to agricultural soils to sequester CO₂ and generate carbon credits. <cite index="16-1,16-2">The company is focused on removing legacy greenhouse gas emissions through Enhanced Rock Weathering in the Pacific Northwest USA and claims the largest active carbon removal project in Washington State.</cite> It is a very small operation (1 employee on Coresignal) with no public registry-listed credits yet.

name: Google taps direct air capture startup for latest carbon removal deal
Grain Ecosystem
tech_note: Digital platform providing project development software, financing tools, and equipment selection workflows for biochar/waste-to-value operators — not a physical biochar producer.
description: Grain Ecosystem was a Boston-based digital platform (founded 2022) providing software and workflows for biochar project developers, connecting operators, investors, and equipment manufacturers in the voluntary carbon market. It did not physically produce biochar itself — it offered financing tools, equipment selection software, and project development infrastructure. In April 2026, Mangrove Systems acquired select operating assets from Grain Ecosystem, folding its operator customer base onto Mangrove's MRV platform.

name: Graphyte
tech_note: TSB
description: Graphyte is a US-based BiCRS company that uses a novel 'Carbon Casting' technology to sequester CO2 by storing waste biomass underground in a durable form.

name: Grassroots Biochar
tech_note: Small-scale biochar producer on Öland, Sweden, using Kon-Tiki flame-curtain kilns to pyrolyze biomass into biochar sold as a soil amendment for agriculture and gardening.
description: <cite index="15-12,15-13,15-14,15-15">Grassroots Biochar AB is a small Swedish company based on Öland that manufactures, refines and innovates biochar products, offering charged and activated biochar for soil management, fertilizing, water holding, filtration and decontamination.</cite> The company uses the Kon-Tiki method and is focused on the agricultural/gardening market in Sweden, without any listed carbon-sink registry certifications.

name: Grassroots Carbon
tech_note: Partners with U.S. ranchers to implement regenerative grazing practices that sequester atmospheric carbon in grassland soils, measured via deep soil sampling and sold as certified soil carbon credits.
description: <cite index="6-9,6-10,6-11">Founded in 2021, Grassroots Carbon is a U.S. company dedicated to measuring, verifying, and rewarding ranchers for storing carbon on America's grasslands, now spanning 2 million acres across 22 states.</cite> They generate soil carbon removal credits through regenerative grazing practices and have delivered credits to buyers including Nestlé, Microsoft, Shopify, and Chevron.

name: Great Carbon Valley
tech_note: DAC project developer
description: Great Carbon Valley is a Kenyan systems integrator and project developer that partners with global DAC leaders to deploy direct air capture (DAC) technology and mineralization at scale in Kenya.

name: Green Carbon
tech_note: Green Carbon develops nature-based carbon credit projects, including industrial-scale biochar carbon removal projects in India and Thailand (converting agricultural and forestry residues into biochar), alongside rice paddy methane reduction, forest conservation, mangrove afforestation, and livestock projects across Japan and Southeast Asia.
description: Green Carbon Inc. is a Tokyo-based developer of nature-based carbon credits founded in 2019, operating in Japan, Southeast Asia, Australia, and South America. Its CDR-relevant activity centers on biochar projects — notably a partnership with Excellent Enfab in India targeting Isometric-certified biochar carbon removal (~18,000 t CO2/yr per plant) and an MOU with the Rubber Authority of Thailand for biochar from rubber trees. The company also develops agriculture/forestry J-Credits and operates the NCCX blockchain credit exchange.

name: Green Carbon Products
tech_note: Biochar
description: Green Carbon Products provides sustainable wood reduction and biochar supply services, focusing on amending soil and generating CDR credits through biochar carbon removal projects.

name: Green Carbon Solutions
tech_note: GCS operates a pyrolysis facility in Indiantown, Florida that converts eucalyptus wood into high-carbon biochar (~95% C), with secondary bio-oil sequestration in geologic formations and bio-energy co-products.
description: <cite index="3-2,3-3">Green Carbon Solutions is a renewable bio-carbon manufacturing company focused on large-scale production of sustainable engineered bio-carbon, bio-oil, and bio-energy, leveraging proprietary design-build-operate technology to decarbonize industrial supply chains and deliver CO₂ removal solutions.</cite> <cite index="12-1">Led by Martin Ellis in Indiantown, Florida, the company uses pyrolysis to transform eucalyptus wood into high-quality biochar and activated carbon.</cite> <cite index="14-1,14-2">A March 2025 tour highlighted its 110-foot retort processing eucalyptus wood into biochar for silicon chipmakers, with plans by 2029 to enrich soil, purify water, and generate electricity.</cite>

name: Green Charcoal International
tech_note: Biochar production from invasive bush biomass in Namibia. Operates Farm Gai Kaisa 159 project.
description: No information found about Green Charcoal International in the provided search results.

name: Green Man Char
tech_note: Continuous slow pyrolysis of local woody waste biomass via Earth Systems CharMaker CPP500 technology producing biochar and wood vinegar.
description: Green Man Char is an Australian biochar producer operating at the Yarra Ranges Council biochar facility in Lysterfield, Victoria, using Earth Systems' CharMaker continuous pyrolysis technology to convert local woody waste into biochar and wood vinegar. The facility was commissioned in 2023 and won the 2025 LGPro VIC Award for Environmental Sustainability. Biochar products are sold primarily as soil conditioners for horticulture and agriculture.

name: Green Sequest
tech_note: Crushes and thermoactivates antigorite serpentinite to accelerate ex-situ enhanced rock weathering, spreading it on agricultural soils to remove CO2 while serving as a magnesium fertilizer.
description: Green Sequest is a Polish startup (founded 2022, based in Nasławice) developing an Enhanced Rock Weathering technology based on antigorite serpentinite, a magnesium-rich rock that permanently mineralizes CO2. They also commercialize a serpentinite-based fertilizer ("Green Mag Balance") approved by the Polish Ministry of Agriculture, and have participated in accelerators such as Carbon Removal ClimAccelerator and Google Startups for Sustainable Development.

name: Green State Biochar
tech_note: Biochar
description: Green State Biochar produces high-quality biochar from biomass waste, primarily for agricultural applications like manure management and runoff control, and is committed to carbon dioxide removal through biochar production.

name: GreenCap Solutions
tech_note: Solid sorbent DAC
description: GreenCap Solutions is a Norwegian company that develops and offers Direct Air Capture (DAC) technology based on physical adsorption using solid sorbents to remove CO2 from the atmosphere.

name: GreenCarbonFactory
tech_note: Pyrolysis of clean woodchips into EBC-certified biochar plus co-produced green heat and electricity at small-scale on-site facilities.
description: GreenCarbonFactory is an Arnhem-based Dutch sustainable technology company founded by Jerom van Roosmalen and Harold Joanknecht that operates small-scale biochar and green-energy facilities at client sites. They convert certified clean (White Listed, PEFC/FSC) woodchips into biochar and heat/electricity via thermal pyrolysis, serving as a Managed Service Provider for site partners.

name: GreenChar Climate Solutions
tech_note: GreenChar develops biochar carbon removal projects in China by partnering with pyrolysis manufacturers that convert agricultural, food, forestry, and manure waste into biochar, and issues internationally certified biochar carbon removal credits with integrated MRV.
description: GreenChar Climate Solutions is a Singapore-headquartered biochar project developer operating across China that transforms organic waste into biochar and sells internationally verified biochar carbon removal credits under standards including Puro.Earth, Verra, Isometric, EBC, and CSI. The company was endorsed by Carbon Standards International as an Artisan C-Sink Manager in September 2025 and serves as the carbon accounting and certification partner for the Yangtze Delta Biochar-Based Zero-Carbon Countryside Collaborative Initiative.

name: GreenGlow
tech_note: Biochar
description: GreenGlow is a Southeast Asian BiCRS company that uses advanced pyrolysis technology to convert agricultural waste and forestry residues into biochar, a stable form of carbon for CO2 removal.

name: Greene
tech_note: Biochar
description: Greene is a Spanish company focused on innovation for non-hazardous solid waste management, including the valorization of biomass as an alternative to conventional combustion, and exploring the potential of biochar and pyrolysis.

name: Greenlyte Carbon Technologies
tech_note: Liquid solvent DAC
description: Greenlyte Carbon Technologies develops and markets a low-energy Direct Air Capture (DAC) process using a liquid-sorbent solution to capture CO2 from the atmosphere while co-producing hydrogen as a byproduct.

name: Groh Land Air & Water
tech_note: Applies biochar (along with microbes, biopolymers, and nanobubbles) to soils and water systems for agricultural improvement, water treatment, and ecosystem restoration.
description: Groh Land Air & Water is a Wisconsin-based environmental services company that uses biochar as one of several natural tools for sustainable agriculture, water treatment, and ecosystem restoration. <cite index="1-6">They describe biochar as a porous charcoal-like substance created through pyrolysis that sequesters carbon and improves soil health.</cite> They are a member of the US Biochar Initiative but there is no public evidence of CDR credit issuance or registry activity.

name: Ground Up
tech_note: Ground Up operates industrial biochar production hubs in India, using pyrolysis to convert agricultural crop residues into biochar-based fertilizers that sequester carbon in soil while improving farm productivity.
description: <cite index="3-3">Ground Up is a Mumbai-based startup founded in 2024 by Shanay Jhaveri, Rhea Dabriwala and Naveen Shivalingam</cite>, developing <cite index="4-6,4-7">industrial biochar production hubs that convert agricultural residues into high-quality biochar using advanced pyrolysis technology, aiming to eliminate open-field burning and produce a carbon-rich soil amendment</cite>. <cite index="3-11">Its latest funding round was a Seed round on May 21, 2025</cite>, and the company has joined the Carbon Business Council coalition of carbon management startups.

name: Groundwork BioAg
tech_note: Applies mycorrhizal fungi inoculants to croplands to accelerate permanent soil carbon sequestration via Mineral-Associated Organic Matter (MAOM) formation, generating Verra VM0042 soil-carbon removal credits.
description: Groundwork BioAg is an Israeli bioagriculture company producing mycorrhizal fungi inoculants (Rootella®) that, when applied to croplands, catalyze the formation of Mineral-Associated Organic Matter (MAOM) for durable soil carbon sequestration. Their Rootella Carbon® program generates Verra VM0042-verified CDR credits, with a September 2025 collaboration with Anew Climate to commercialize 500,000 tCO2e of mycorrhizal CDR credits over three years. They are an active CDR supplier, not a buyer.

name: Groupe Bordet
tech_note: French industrial producer of biochar, activated carbon, charcoal, and bio-oil via slow pyrolysis of wood from local sawmill residues, with Puro.earth-certified carbon removal credits.
description: <cite index="7-1,7-2">Groupe Bordet is a French industrial group transforming wood into charcoal, based in Leuglay, Burgundy since 1860, producing a locally-sourced plant-based charcoal with over 90% carbon content.</cite> <cite index="3-7">Its biochar production has been certified by Puro.earth with support from Carbonapp</cite>, and <cite index="10-5,10-6,10-7,10-8">the group is investing over €30M in a new plant in Decize (Nièvre), operational in Q1 2027, to add 15,000 tonnes of biochar capacity (from 4,200 t today) and develop bio-oil, aiming for 60,000 tonnes of biochar by 2030.</cite>

name: HEMPALTA
tech_note: Biochar
description: HEMPALTA is an agricultural technology company that produces biochar from hemp biomass for soil enhancement and carbon sequestration. The company is also focusing on generating carbon credits through its Hemp Carbon Standard program.

name: HP Biochar: The Leader in Biochar Production & Furnaces
Hafslund Celsio
tech_note: Hafslund Celsio is building a full-scale post-combustion amine-based carbon capture plant at its Klemetsrud waste-to-energy facility in Oslo, with liquefaction and ship transport to Northern Lights for permanent sub-seabed storage; ~60% of captured CO2 is biogenic, yielding BECCS removals.
description: Hafslund Celsio is Norway's largest district heating supplier and operator of the country's largest waste-to-energy plant at Klemetsrud, Oslo. It is a partly-owned subsidiary within the Hafslund/Infranode/HitecVision consortium developing a flagship BECCS project under Norway's Longship program, with FID reached in January 2025 and operations targeted for Q3 2029. The project has secured major CDR offtakes including a 10-year, 1.1 Mt deal with Microsoft and a Frontier prepay.

name: Hago Energetics
tech_note: Converts organic waste (cow manure, agricultural residues, landfill gas, wastewater byproducts) into fuel-cell-grade green hydrogen via biomethane pyrolysis, producing biochar as a carbon-sequestering co-product used as soil amendment.
description: Hago Energetics is a California-based startup (founded 2017) developing a carbon-negative hydrogen process that strips hydrogen from biomethane and deposits the carbon as biochar. EcoEngineers' third-party LCA validated strongly negative carbon intensity (as low as -492 gCO2e/MJ with biochar sequestration). The company was selected as a Qualified Hydrogen Supplier by First Public Hydrogen Authority in January 2026 and has won DOE, CEC, NASA and NYSERDA awards.

name: Haliburton Forest Biochar
tech_note: Pyrolysis of sustainably harvested hardwood sawmill residues to produce biochar for soil amendment and as a fossil-carbon-black substitute in advanced manufacturing.
description: Haliburton Forest Biochar is a joint venture/subsidiary of Haliburton Forest & Wild Life Reserve Ltd. in central Ontario, Canada, producing high-quality biochar from sustainably harvested hardwood sawmill residues via proprietary pyrolysis. Products serve soil amendment and advanced manufacturing applications (e.g., as a fossil carbon-black replacement). The company received a $4.6M Ontario provincial investment announced in 2025 to scale engineered biochar production.

name: Happy Ground
tech_note: Happy Ground converts Thai agricultural residues (rice, sugarcane, coconut, rubber) into biochar and biochar-enhanced fertilizers, deploying them with smallholder farmers and tracking carbon removal via an IoT/satellite traceability platform.
description: Happy Ground is a Thailand-based biochar CDR supplier working with smallholder farmers to turn agricultural residues into carbon removal, avoiding open-field burning and PM2.5 pollution. It is developing a large-scale project across 100,000 hectares with 10,000 farmers, is in certification with Carbon Standards International, and targets Puro.earth-aligned verification. The company also operates an insetting/traceability platform for corporate Scope 3 reporting.

name: Harvestone
tech_note: Operates three corn ethanol biorefineries and captures biogenic fermentation CO2 for permanent sequestration via Class VI injection wells (BECCS).
description: Harvestone Low Carbon Partners (HLCP), a portfolio company of Energy Capital Partners formed in 2022, owns three Midwest ethanol biorefineries (Blue Flint and Dakota Spirit in North Dakota; Iroquois Bio-Energy in Indiana) producing ~220 million gallons/year. Blue Flint began sequestering biogenic CO2 in October 2023 via an on-site Class VI injection well — the third U.S. biorefinery to do so and the first post-IRA — and HLCP is developing similar CCS at Dakota Spirit (including a trucking-based transport plan) under its Vision Carbon Zero initiative.

name: Heirloom
tech_note: Solid sorbent DAC
description: Heirloom develops a low-cost Direct Air Capture (DAC) technology that uses modified limestone (calcium carbonate/oxide) as a solid sorbent to remove CO2 directly from the atmosphere.

name: HerbaCarbo
tech_note: Pyrolytic carbonization of plant biomass (including herbal pomace from medicinal-plant extraction) into EBC-certified biochar sold as plant carbon and feed carbon.
description: <cite index="1-1,1-2">HerbaCarbo GbR is a production company of biochar-based products located in Andernach, Germany, with products sold under the HerbaCarbo brand.</cite> They produce EBC-certified biochar from biomass including herbal pomace and woodchips via pyrolysis at 500–700°C, marketed for Terra Preta soil applications and as a feed additive. The company is a small, family-run GbR that has been operating since ~2015.

name: High Hopes Labs
tech_note: Cryogenic DAC
description: High Hopes Labs is an Israeli startup that developed a unique High Altitude Carbon Capture (HACC) methodology using balloons to capture carbon dioxide from the upper atmosphere where it is colder, making separation easier.

name: Hjelmsäters Egendom
tech_note: Biochar
description: Hjelmsäters Egendom is a Swedish company that produces biochar from forestry residues using BIOMACON technology. The biochar is used for soil amendment in the agricultural sector and they sell CORCs (CO2 Removal Certificates) via Puro.earth.

name: Hokuetsu Corporation
tech_note: BECCS
description: Hokuetsu Corporation is a Japanese paper milling company that is involved in a BECCS (Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Storage) project in Niigata Prefecture, Japan, as part of a government-selected carbon capture initiative.

name: Holocene
tech_note: Liquid-based, low-temperature DAC using amino acids and guanidine-based organic compounds (licensed from ORNL) that precipitate captured CO2 as a solid for regeneration and permanent geological storage.
description: Holocene is a Knoxville, Tennessee-based direct air capture startup founded in 2022 by former Climeworks engineers, using a liquid-based, low-temperature thermochemical process with amino acids and guanidine compounds (licensed from Oak Ridge National Laboratory). In September 2024 it signed a landmark $100/ton, 100,000-ton carbon removal deal with Google, and in April 2025 it was acquired by Occidental Petroleum, which is integrating the technology with its Carbon Engineering/1PointFive DAC business.

name: Hovyu
tech_note: Develops the ZEUS liquid-solvent absorption/stripping process for DAC and point-source CO2 capture, designed to release CO2 at high pressure without requiring thermal regeneration.
description: Hovyu is a Netherlands-based carbon capture engineering firm developing the ZEUS (Zero-Emission Ultra-Stripping) liquid-solvent process for Direct Air Capture, flue gas capture, and biogas upgrading. <cite index="3-1,3-3,3-4">Their ZEUS technology is a flexible and scalable process to remove CO2 from industrial emissions or from air, with CO2 release proceeding at room temperature requiring no heat, which is an advantage where steam availability is constrained.</cite> <cite index="1-2">They have diversified international operations with projects in the Netherlands, Norway and Brazil.</cite>

name: Husk
tech_note: Biochar
description: Husk produces biochar from organic rice husks, which is used as a fertilizer to regenerate soils, improve yields, and increase long-term profitability for farmers.

name: Hydrogen Naturally
tech_note: Gasifies forestry waste fibre to produce hydrogen and a pure CO2 stream, which is compressed and geologically sequestered — a BECCS-with-hydrogen pathway, not biochar.
description: Hydrogen Naturally (H2N) is a Canadian startup developing "Bright Green Hydrogen" facilities that gasify forestry residuals to co-produce hydrogen and pure CO2 for permanent underground storage. It is backed by founding partners Peak Renewables and North West Capital, and is planning hubs in Alberta's Industrial Heartland and British Columbia. In April 2025 it received a $3M grant from Emissions Reduction Alberta to advance its negative-emission hydrogen project.

name: HyveGeo
tech_note: Biochar
description: HyveGeo is a BiCRS company that transforms biogenic residues into carbon-rich biochar, supercharged with microalgae, to remove carbon and regenerate degraded land, particularly in desert environments.

name: Húmica
tech_note: Húmica produces tailor-made biochar-based biofertilizers via pyrolysis and applies them to smallholder agricultural soils in Mexico, combined with regenerative agroforestry practices.
description: Húmica is a Mexican biotech startup founded in 2019–2020 that works with smallholder farmers (with a focus on women producers in Puebla, Veracruz, Tabasco, and Oaxaca) to sequester carbon through biochar production and regenerative agroforestry. The company diagnoses soils, formulates site-specific biochar recipes, and helps farmers access carbon credit markets while commercializing their crops.

name: IGAD Climate Prediction and Applications Center
IRCCS Azienda Ospedliero-Universitaria di Bologna Policlinico di Sant'Orsola
Ibero Massa Florestal
tech_note: Produces biochar via slow pyrolysis of forest and agricultural biomass at its Oliveira de Azeméis plant in Portugal, selling agricultural Ecochar and domestic Carvão Zero, with CDR credits sold via Carbonfuture under EBC/Global C-Sink certifications.
description: <cite index="10-3,10-4,10-5">Ibero Massa Florestal (IMF) is a Portuguese company focused on the production of biochar and bio-based sustainable solutions, based in Oliveira de Azeméis, transforming forest biomass through slow pyrolysis to produce Carvão Zero (a charcoal for household use) and Ecochar (a certified biochar for agriculture, forest restoration, and long-term carbon removal), with an installed capacity of 5,000 tonnes per year and certifications including EBC, GLOBAL C-SINK, FSC, and PEFC.</cite> The company sells biochar carbon removal credits through partners such as Carbonfuture.

name: InPlanet
tech_note: Applies finely crushed basalt silicate rock powder to tropical Brazilian farmland to accelerate natural weathering that converts atmospheric CO2 into stable bicarbonates.
description: InPlanet is a Brazil/Germany-based CDR supplier pioneering tropical Enhanced Rock Weathering, spreading finely crushed basalt on farmland to permanently sequester CO2 as bicarbonates while improving soil fertility. The company delivered the world's first independently verified ERW credits (via Isometric) and in December 2025 signed a deal with Microsoft for 28,500+ tonnes to be delivered 2026-2028.

name: Indian Institute of Science Education and Research Kolkata
Indigo
tech_note: Enrolls US farmers in regenerative agriculture practices (cover crops, reduced tillage) and issues registry-verified agricultural soil carbon removal credits through the Climate Action Reserve's Soil Enrichment Protocol.
description: Indigo Ag is a US-based sustainable agriculture company whose Carbon by Indigo program (operated by subsidiary Indigo Carbon PBC) develops and issues agricultural soil carbon credits. <cite index="6-11,6-12">Since 2018, Indigo Carbon has enrolled more than 8 million acres across 28 U.S. states and sequestered/abated approximately 2.1 million metric tons of CO₂e.</cite> <cite index="4-2">Under a 12-year agreement, Microsoft will purchase 2.85 million soil carbon removal credits from Indigo.</cite>

name: Industrielle Werke Basel
tech_note: Biochar
description: Industrielle Werke Basel is a Swiss energy, water, and telecommunications service provider that produces biochar from organic waste, such as sawdust, wood chips, and Christmas trees, to remove CO2 from the atmosphere.

name: Inherit
tech_note: Inherit captures biogenic CO2 from biogas production at wastewater/organic-waste facilities and sends it via Northern Lights to permanent geological storage below the North Sea seabed.
description: Inherit Carbon Solutions is a Norwegian BECCS project developer that captures biogenic CO2 from biogas plants processing wastewater and agricultural organic waste and permanently stores it under the North Sea. In March 2026 it entered operation with what it describes as the world's first carbon removal project from biogas, delivering Puro.earth-certified credits to buyers including Microsoft, DNV and Nordea.

name: Inkan Negro
tech_note: Peruvian company producing biochar soil amendments from agricultural and urban green waste biomass, with applications in soil remediation, agriculture, and mine reclamation.
description: <cite index="2-1,2-2">Inkan Negro is a Peruvian-owned company that manufactures and sells its own ecologically sustainable biochar soil amendment, based on over 10 years of scientific research conducted in Peru.</cite> <cite index="3-1,3-2">They produce biochar by converting urban green and agricultural wastes into an optimized soil amendment that improves soil structural properties and fertility.</cite> The company has engaged with Puro.earth through a Pre-CORC biochar project.

name: Inkoh
tech_note: Inkoh operates a Biomacon pyrolysis reactor in Maienfeld, Switzerland that converts untreated forest waste wood into biochar for soil amendment, animal feed additive, and climate concrete (KLARK), while also supplying heat and issuing CO2 certificates.
description: Inkoh AG is a Swiss biochar producer that has operated a pyrolysis plant in Maienfeld since May 2020, capable of producing approximately 450 tons of biochar per year from forest waste wood. The company sells biochar directly and as substrate mixtures (including tree-pit substrates for sponge-city applications) and issues carbon removal certificates via First Climate. Swiss Post is a notable partner investing in Inkoh biochar as part of its 2040 carbon-neutral strategy.

name: InnoSepra
tech_note: InnoSepra develops a solid-sorbent-based Direct Air Capture process using physical sorbents in structured form to reduce regeneration energy below 4 GJ/tonne, alongside related post-combustion CO2 capture and biogas upgrading technologies.
description: <cite index="16-7,16-3,16-4">InnoSepra, founded in 2007 by Dr. Ravi Jain and based in Middlesex, NJ, is testing its second-generation post-combustion carbon capture technology at Technology Centre Mongstad (TCM), with partial funding from the US Department of Energy.</cite> The company has received multiple DOE SBIR awards to develop a sorbent-based Direct Air Capture process, <cite index="2-1">advancing a DAC process using sorbent materials with high CO2 capacities and low regeneration energy requirements</cite>. It remains an R&D-stage DAC technology developer and therefore qualifies as a supplier.

name: Innsbrucker Kommunalbetriebe
tech_note: Biochar
