description: Innsbrucker Kommunalbetriebe AG is a municipal company in Innsbruck, Austria, involved in various communal services including biochar-based product production, electricity, water, gas supply, waste management, and telecommunications.

name: Inspiratus Technology
tech_note: Biochar
description: Inspiratus Technology is a company that focuses on carbon solutions, specifically biochar production through pyrolysis, and also offers water filtration solutions.

name: Institut National des Sciences Appliquées de Toulouse
Institute for Globally Distributed Open Research and Education
Institute of Agriculture and Animal Science
Institute of Genetics and Developmental Biology
Institute of Mountain Hazards and Environment
InterEarth
tech_note: InterEarth grows coppicing native Eucalyptus/Acacia on degraded low-rainfall Australian farmland, harvests the above-ground biomass, and stores it in engineered above-ground "Dry Stack" chambers designed to maintain biomass-inert conditions for 100+ years.
description: <cite index="20-1">InterEarth removes CO2 with the woody biomass burial method to store carbon captured within the biomass.</cite> <cite index="6-2,6-3">Their business is harvesting, transporting and stacking dried biomass within their Dry Stack above-ground storage chamber, using woody biomass from plantation-grown native Australian Eucalyptus and Acacia trees.</cite> <cite index="6-26">InterEarth lodged an Australian Provisional Patent in May 2023 and filed an International PCT in May 2024 for its Dry Stack Biomass Carbon sequestration technology.</cite>

name: Interholco
tech_note: Produces biochar from FSC-certified tropical hardwood sawmill residues at its sawmill in the Republic of Congo, applying the biochar to soils in its managed forest concession.
description: Interholco AG is a Swiss timber company (founded 1962) that manages 1.16 million hectares of FSC-certified tropical forest in the Republic of Congo via its IFO subsidiary. It operates a biochar carbon removal project converting sawmill residues into stable carbon, with C-sink certification through the EBC / Global C-Sink Registry. While timber is its core business, the biochar project is an integrated CDR supplier operation.

name: International Tie Disposal
tech_note: Biochar
description: International Tie Disposal is a BiCRS company that uses pyrolysis to convert creosote-treated railroad ties into high-quality biochar for industrial, agricultural, and horticultural applications.

name: Invert
tech_note: Biotech company engineering microbes for methane removal and carbon capture from the atmosphere.
description: No relevant search results were found for the company 'Invert' (invertbio.com). The provided search results refer to other entities or general topics.

name: Ionada
tech_note: Ionada develops containerized modular carbon capture systems based on patented hollow fiber membrane contactor (HFMC) technology using amine solvents, marketed as iDAC for direct air capture and iDeCarbon for post-combustion flue-gas capture.
description: <cite index="9-3,9-4">Ionada is an Ontario, Canada-based climate technology company that in August 2025 received grant funding from the NGIF Accelerator to advance its modular carbon capture system, supporting construction and demonstration of an industrial-scale unit.</cite> <cite index="5-3,5-4">In August 2025 the company announced completion and demonstration of the world's first production-scale Hollow Fiber Membrane Contactor (HFMC) carbon capture system.</cite> Its iDAC product applies the same membrane contactor technology to direct air capture, while its core commercial focus is point-source capture for natural gas, marine, hydrogen, steel, cement, and thermal power applications.

name: Isometric
tech_note: Isometric is a carbon removal registry and science/MRV platform that develops protocols, verifies CDR projects, and issues credits across pathways including enhanced weathering, biochar, DAC, and reforestation.
description: <cite index="3-19,3-20">Isometric is a carbon removal registry, which in 2025 signed its 100th supplier (Flux), with suppliers spanning every major CDR pathway.</cite> <cite index="7-2,7-3">In March 2025 it launched Certify, a platform that reduces the CDR verification process from years down to roughly one month.</cite> <cite index="10-14,10-15,10-16">Isometric has received endorsements from ICROA, CORSIA, and ICVCM, allowing it to issue credits under the Core Carbon Principles label.</cite>

name: Italian Carbon Removal Network
tech_note: Industry association/network coordinating Italian CDR stakeholders (startups, policymakers, researchers) — not a removal supplier itself.
description: The Italian Carbon Removal Network (Rete Italiana Rimozione Carbonio, RIRC) is Italy's first dedicated national carbon removal industry network, launched on 14 April 2026 in Padova during Padova Climate Action Week in collaboration with the Negative Emissions Platform. It serves as a coordinating industry body for CDR stakeholders in Italy, analogous to France's AFEN, Germany's DVNE, and the Nordic NCRA, promoting deployment, governance, and public understanding of carbon removal.

name: Jeevan Climate Solutions
tech_note: Solid-sorbent DAC using a copper-coordinated weak-base ion-exchange resin (DeCarbonHIX) that can be regenerated with low-grade heat or seawater; captured CO2 can be sequestered as bicarbonate/baking soda.
description: Jeevan Climate Solutions is a Pennsylvania-based (Allentown/Bethlehem) DAC startup spun out of Lehigh University, founded in 2022 by Prof. Arup SenGupta. It develops DeCarbonHIX, a copper-armored ion-exchange solid sorbent that captures CO2 from air or flue gas, regenerates with low-temperature heat or seawater, and can convert CO2 to baking soda for ocean storage. The company has received DOE SBIR Phase I funding and investment from Blue Action Accelerator, Founders Factory, and Ben Franklin Technology Partners.

name: Jeffries Group
tech_note: Jeffries operates a commercial biochar plant in South Australia using Pyrocal Continuous Carbonisation Technology to pyrolyze green waste, producing biochar for soil amendment and using syngas via an ORC turbine to generate renewable energy.
description: Jeffries Group is a 180+ year-old South Australian composting and soil products family business that commissioned one of the Southern Hemisphere's largest biochar plants in 2021. The plant pyrolyzes kerbside green waste into biochar (sold as soil amendment and in pelletized CulChar fertiliser) while powering itself via ORC turbines driven by syngas. The company is a Puro.earth-listed CORC supplier, though the CDR-credit project remains in early development status.

name: Jiaxing Tongao Technology/Climate Future
tech_note: Biochar
description: Jiaxing Tongao Technology is a Chinese company involved in biochar production, specifically noted for establishing a large-scale biochar facility in Uganda through a partnership.

name: Jord
tech_note: Cultivates perennial C4 grass on marginal/degraded land and pyrolyzes residues into biochar for soil sequestration, alongside producing solid biofuel pellets.
description: Jord is a Swedish company (founded 2017, HQ Stockholm) with cultivation operations in Senegal and the Dominican Republic that produces biochar and solid biofuel pellets from C4 grass grown on degraded land. The company also sells carbon credits combining avoidance and biochar-based removal. It has active 2024-2025 partnerships with Votion Biorefineries (SAF), TEXEL (electricity), and Borga (construction).

name: KEW Technology
tech_note: BECCS
description: KEW Technology is a UK-based sustainable energy solutions company that develops waste-to-hydrogen technology, specifically focusing on Bio-Energy with Carbon Capture and Storage (BECCS) to separate H2-CO2.

name: KORALL
tech_note: Liquid solvent DAC
description: KORALL is a Swedish company developing a novel liquid Direct Air Capture (DAC) technology that uses a liquid solvent to filter atmospheric air and bind carbon in solid form, aiming to make CO2 removal more efficient.

name: KWS Ökokraft
tech_note: Biochar
description: KWS Ökokraft GmbH operates a wood-fired power plant in Ternitz, Austria, that generates electricity and heat. A by-product of this process is biochar, which sequesters carbon dioxide.

name: Kairos Carbon
tech_note: Uses hydrothermal/supercritical water oxidation on wet organic wastes (manure, sewage sludge) to convert biogenic carbon to CO2 for geological sequestration, while recovering clean water and mineral fertilizer co-products.
description: Kairos Carbon is a UK-based CDR startup (incorporated April 2024) developing a supercritical water oxidation process that treats high-moisture biogenic waste streams, captures the resulting CO2 for permanent underground storage, and recovers phosphorus and other nutrients. The company is building a pilot facility and has received backing from Zero Carbon Capital, Grantham Foundation, Innovate UK, and a £1M Defra Farming Innovation grant. Milkywire's Climate Transformation Fund selected them as a 2025 CDR purchase.

name: Kanadevia Inova
tech_note: BECCS
description: Kanadevia Inova is a global green tech company specializing in Waste to Energy (WtE) and Renewable Gas. They are actively involved in projects that convert organic waste into biochar and renewable gas, which sequesters carbon.

name: Kanop
tech_note: AI-powered SaaS platform using satellite imagery (optical, radar, LiDAR) and machine learning to provide MRV, baselining, and monitoring for nature-based carbon projects (afforestation/reforestation, REDD+, mangroves, agroforestry).
description: Kanop is a Paris-based MRV software company founded in 2021 that provides satellite-based monitoring, baselining, and verification services for nature-based carbon projects and corporate supply chain reporting. It supports major carbon standards including Verra, Gold Standard, Isometric, and Equitable Earth, and was recently selected by Isometric as a nature-based service partner. Kanop does not remove CO2 itself but provides the measurement infrastructure used by project developers, investors, and buyers.

name: Karbonetiq
tech_note: Karbonetiq accelerates surficial mineralization by crushing alkaline industrial residues (slags, ash) and exposing them to air/moisture via passive aeration so atmospheric CO₂ bonds into stable carbonates on-site.
description: Karbonetiq is a Santa Barbara, California-based CDR startup (founded 2022) that mineralizes CO₂ by processing alkaline industrial residues through a low-cost passive aeration system with sensor-based MRV. It was selected in Frontier's Summer 2025 prepurchase round (2,142 tons) alongside Limenet and pHathom, on behalf of Stripe, Shopify, and Google. The company is a Puro.earth registry participant and an active mineralization supplier.

name: Karbonwerke
tech_note: Captures biogenic CO2 from biogas plants and biorefineries and sequesters it underground for permanent storage, selling carbon removal credits and long-term CO2 offtake.
description: <cite index="11-1,11-2,11-3,11-4">Karbonwerke is a Swiss company that captures and stores CO2 from biogenic sources — biogas plants and biorefineries that release CO2 as a byproduct — to provide negative emissions.</cite> They offer carbon removal credits and long-term CO2 offtake to partner facilities, and also run a small advisory arm on CDR technologies.

name: Kawasaki Heavy Industries
tech_note: Solid sorbent DAC
description: Kawasaki Heavy Industries develops and deploys Direct Air Capture (DAC) technology using a proprietary solid sorbent, often amine-coated beads, to capture CO2 from the atmosphere. They are also involved in projects to store captured CO2 in concrete.

name: Kepler ReCapture
tech_note: Designs autonomous offshore spar platforms that combine OTEC/wave-powered desalination with CO2 extraction from air and seawater, converting captured carbon into carbonate minerals and durable materials.
description: Kepler ReCapture is a U.S.-based (Austin, TX) division of aerospace firm Kepler Shipyards, developing conceptual ocean-based floating platforms that integrate carbon-negative desalination with CO2 removal from the ocean-atmosphere system. The company was founded in 2021 as an XPRIZE Carbon Removal entrant and remains in early/pre-deployment stage, with artist renderings rather than operational systems. Multiple revenue streams are claimed including freshwater, renewable energy, carbonate minerals, and gases.

name: Kita
tech_note: Kita is a Lloyd's of London Coverholder offering specialty insurance products (Non-Delivery, Non-Payment, Political Risk, Carbon Purchase Protection Cover) for carbon and CDR market participants.
description: <cite index="1-2,1-4">Kita is a Lloyd's of London Coverholder and carbon insurance specialist</cite>, <cite index="7-19,7-20">a UK-based startup formed in December 2021 to insure CO2 removal credits that are often forward-purchased and carry delivery risks</cite>. <cite index="1-9">Its policies provide coverage tailored to carbon and natural capital asset classes, including Delivery, Counterparty, Political and Buffer Depletion</cite>. They are part of the CDR ecosystem as a financial-infrastructure provider rather than a physical CO2 remover.

name: Klim
tech_note: Klim is a project developer and MRV provider that works with farmers to implement regenerative agriculture practices (cover cropping, reduced tillage, diverse rotations) that sequester carbon in agricultural soils, generating carbon credits and Scope 3 insetting outcomes for corporate partners.
description: Klim is a Berlin-based agritech company that scales regenerative agriculture by partnering with 3,500+ farmers across Germany, Poland, the USA, UK, Slovakia, and the Czech Republic. They act as project developer, manager, and MRV provider, offering Scope 3 insetting projects and soil-carbon credits to corporate buyers including Nestlé and ADM.

name: Klimafarmer
tech_note: Biochar
description: Klimafarmer is a German company that produces and trades biochar-based products, primarily for agriculture, to sequester carbon.

name: Klimate
tech_note: Klimate operates a CO2 asset management platform and brokerage that helps corporate buyers build and manage diversified carbon removal portfolios across biochar, BECCS, DAC, ERW, reforestation, and bio-oil projects.
description: <cite index="3-1,3-2">Klimate.co is a Copenhagen-based company founded in 2020 that specializes in carbon asset management, with a platform that enables businesses to secure high-quality carbon removal solutions.</cite> <cite index="7-9,7-10">Klimate buys the removal of CO2 from the atmosphere on behalf of its clients through different removal projects and combines them into portfolios, with options for custom portfolios.</cite> They are a broker/marketplace rather than a technology developer, making them part of the CDR ecosystem.

name: Kodama Systems
tech_note: Buries waste woody biomass from forest-thinning operations in engineered dryland "wood vaults" to prevent decomposition, paired with teleoperated/autonomous skidder technology for efficient feedstock collection.
description: Kodama Systems is a Sonora, California-based forest management and robotics company that thins fire-prone western US forests and sequesters the waste woody biomass in engineered underground "wood vaults." It combines teleoperated/autonomous skidder technology (Kodama Autopilot, RS1) with biomass burial CDR in partnership with the Yale Carbon Containment Lab. Backed by Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Congruent Ventures, and a Frontier/Stripe pre-purchase for ~415 tonnes of CO2.

name: KohleHelden
tech_note: Manufactures EBC- and GMP+ certified biochar (plant charcoal and feed charcoal) from German wood via pyrolysis, sold for soil amendment and animal feed.
description: <cite index="1-1">KohleHelden GmbH & Co. KG is a manufacturing company of biochar located in Zierenberg, Germany.</cite> <cite index="6-1">They produce EBC- and GMP+ certified plant charcoal and feed charcoal (Pflanzenkohle and Futterkohle), sourced regionally from North Hesse near Kassel.</cite> Products are actively sold via their website and Amazon, providing a permanent biochar carbon sink for agricultural applications.

name: Krajete/Audi
tech_note: Solid sorbent DAC
description: Krajete/Audi is a partnership that uses Direct Air Capture (DAC) with solid sorbents to filter CO2 directly from the air. The partnership was announced in 2022.

name: LOCOAL
tech_note: Biochar
description: LOCOAL utilizes proprietary mobile containerized fluidized gasifiers to convert commercial wood waste into clean energy and biochar, which sequesters carbon and filters soil and water.

name: Leilac/Calix
tech_note: Leilac builds indirectly heated electric calciners that separate pure process CO2 from limestone; the technology is licensed to Heirloom for DAC plants and applied to cement/lime process-emission capture.
description: Leilac is an Australian subsidiary of ASX-listed Calix Limited that develops indirectly heated electric calcination technology for decarbonising cement and lime production. Its CDR relevance stems from a perpetual global licence with Heirloom, whose Direct Air Capture facilities (including a 17,000 tpa Shreveport plant and a 300,000 tpa Project Cypress hub contribution) deploy Leilac's electric calciner as core hardware. Leilac also received Frontier's zero-carbon lime grant and continues projects like ZETA, Leilac-2, and two US DOE-funded pre-FEED studies.

name: Levitree
tech_note: Injects wood-chip slurry into shallow (5-100 m) subsurface apertures where anoxic conditions prevent decomposition, achieving long-duration carbon storage while raising ground elevation for flood mitigation.
description: Levitree is a San Rafael/Berkeley, California-based startup founded in 2021 that sequesters carbon by injecting wood-chip slurries 5-100 meters underground using AI-enabled robotic equipment, a technique called Subterranean Wood Injection (SWI). The process also raises the ground surface, providing a flood-protection co-benefit for infrastructure. The company was a finalist in NYU Tandon's 2025 Urban Future Prize Competition and is backed by Berkeley SkyDeck.

name: LightNET Carbon Capture
tech_note: Accelerated ex-situ mineralization of CO2 into stable carbonates via nanotech-engineered coatings (CO2atings) and ceramics (CO2rallites) using Ca/Mg oxides and industrial waste feedstocks like steel slags.
description: LightNET Carbon Capture (LNCC) is a Barcelona-based spin-off of ICN2 and CSIC that develops accelerated ex-situ CO2 mineralization technologies, turning CO2 into carbonates within coatings (CO2atings®) and advanced ceramics (CO2rallites®) using earth-abundant oxides/hydroxides and industrial waste. The company has run pilots with SACYR on construction sites, published a peer-reviewed paper in APL Energy (2025), was a finalist at the SteelTech Awards 2025, and had CSIC formalize shareholder participation in November 2025.

name: LignoCarbon
tech_note: Biochar
description: LignoCarbon Schweiz AG is a Swiss company that produces biochar-based products, marketed under the brand name LignoCarbon, and is actively seeking potential biochar customers.

name: Lillianah Technologies
tech_note: Cultivates and disperses native diatoms (phytoplankton) in coastal hypoxic dead zones to capture CO2 via the biological pump, with permanence claimed via marine sedimentation.
description: Lillianah Technologies is a Houston-based ocean CDR startup founded in 2021 that removes CO2 by dispersing diatoms into nutrient-rich marine dead zones (initially on the Gulf Coast), using MRV based on dissolved oxygen sensors and sediment traps. It is an IndieBio/SOSV portfolio company that has raised roughly $525K–$1.2M in seed and grant funding and signed an early offtake agreement with Clearyst°. Operational signals since 2023 are limited, with a small team (~4–7 employees) and no disclosed new funding rounds.

name: Limenet
tech_note: Limenet operates an industrial plant in Augusta, Sicily that combines CO2 (from a biogas source) with hydrated lime and seawater to produce calcium bicarbonates released into the ocean, increasing alkalinity and storing carbon durably.
description: <cite index="6-9,6-10">Limenet is an Italian climate tech company using a patented pH-equilibrated Ocean Alkalinization technology that stores CO₂ in seawater as equilibrated calcium bicarbonates, increasing ocean alkalinity.</cite> <cite index="3-9">Its Augusta (Sicily) plant has been operational since September 2023, currently processes 800 tonnes of CO₂ per year, with plans to scale to 100,000 tonnes annually by 2028.</cite> <cite index="3-3,3-4">In 2025, Carbonmark issued Limenet's first 14.7 OAE credits via Carbonmark Direct, a milestone for ocean-based carbon removal.</cite>

name: Linhe Climate Science & Technology Co. Ltd
tech_note: Solid sorbent DAC
description: Linhe Climate Science & Technology Co. Ltd (also known as Linhe Climate Technology) is a scientific and technology innovation company focused on low-cost, high-efficiency, distributed, need-based carbon capture technologies, specifically Direct Air Capture (DAC) using solid sorbents, and multi-path utilization technologies.

name: Liquid Trees
tech_note: Iron fertilization
description: Liquid Trees specializes in Marine CDR through Ocean Iron Fertilization (OIF), aiming to enhance marine productivity and sequester carbon in the deep ocean by adding iron to surface waters.

name: Lithos
tech_note: ERW
description: Lithos Carbon is a carbon removal company that scales Enhanced Rock Weathering (ERW) by applying crushed basalt rock dust to agricultural fields to permanently capture carbon dioxide and improve soil health.

name: Living Carbon
tech_note: Biotechnology company engineering trees for enhanced photosynthesis and carbon storage.
description: Living Carbon is a biotechnology company that uses genetically enhanced trees to capture and store CO2, focusing on reforestation projects on degraded land to generate high-quality carbon removal credits.

name: Longstraw Carbon
tech_note: Slow pyrolysis of agricultural residues (rice husk, crop straw) into biochar for soil application, with bio-oil and syngas co-products.
description: Longstraw Carbon is a Delhi, India-based biochar producer founded in 2024 that converts agricultural residues (rice husk, crop straw) into biochar, bio-oil, and syngas via its proprietary STS™ / RiceLoop™ pyrolysis technology. The company operates production sites in Kalahandi and Sambalpur (Odisha) and targets carbon removal markets for Indian smallholder agriculture.

name: Low Carbon Materials
tech_note: Manufactures carbon-negative lightweight aggregates (ACLA® for asphalt, OSTO® for concrete) that lock biogenic carbon and some carbonation-derived CO2 permanently into construction materials as a drop-in replacement for traditional aggregates.
description: Low Carbon Materials (LCM) is a Durham University spin-out based in Seaham, UK, that designs and manufactures carbon-negative aggregates — OSTO® for concrete and ACLA® for asphalt — which sequester biogenic carbon (with some additional carbonation uptake) permanently within construction materials. The company closed a £3M growth round led by Ada Ventures, won the BE100 SCALE competition at Blue Earth Summit 2025, and has deployed ACLA in trials on the M11 and numerous council road projects with National Highways, Skanska, and Tarmac. An EPD (EPD-IES-0016646) reports an A1-A3 GWP of –798 kg CO2e/t for ACLA.

name: LowCarbon
tech_note: N/A DAC tech
description: LowCarbon is a South Korean company focused on Direct Air Capture (DAC) technology to remove carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. They are actively involved in partnerships and technological advancements in climate tech.

name: Lucrat
tech_note: Biochar
description: Lucrat GmbH is a German company that produces biochar-based products, focusing on the construction industry and biogas, and has developed efficient biochar through scientific tests and real-life applications.

name: MARINIX Ocean Tech AS
tech_note: Developing an ocean CDR method that induces formation of marine snow aggregates in the Southern Ocean to sink organic carbon to the deep sea.
description: MARINIX Ocean Tech AS is a Norwegian early-stage Ocean CDR startup founded by Hanne M. Edvardsen Jelavic, with scientific work led by Prof. Staša Puškarić on marine snow and ocean carbon kinetics. The company is pre-revenue and in R&D/funding phase, seeking philanthropic and research funding to scale a marine-snow-based ocean carbon removal concept.

name: MASH Makes
tech_note: MASH Makes operates containerised pyrolysis reactors that convert agricultural residues (primarily cashew nut shells) into biochar and bio-oil/biofuel, generating EBC-certified carbon removal credits.
description: <cite index="2-10,2-11,2-12">MASH Makes A/S is a Danish company established in 2015 as a spin-off from the Technical University of Denmark, whose pyrolysis and gasification technology converts agricultural waste into carbon-negative energy commodities and biochar that removes CO2 from the atmosphere and produces carbon removal credits.</cite> <cite index="2-13,2-14">The company employs 11 people in Denmark and 49 at its subsidiary in India operating the production facility in Udupi, Karnataka, and aims to scale from two to 30 sites by 2027.</cite> Credits are distributed via Carbonfuture under EBC certification.

name: MK Collect
tech_note: Liquid solvent DAC
description: MK Collect is an Australian DAC company that uses an innovative catalytic solvent regeneration approach for low-temperature CO2 collection under vacuum, aiming for rapid, large-scale, and affordable carbon removal.

name: MOVA Technologies
tech_note: N/A DAC tech
description: MOVA Technologies develops advanced air filtration systems that capture airborne contaminants, such as ammonia, from industrial and agricultural environments, particularly poultry houses. While they mention "air capture technology" and "selectively capture and harvest air contaminants as valuable byproducts," the results do not explicitly state they are a Direct Air Capture (DAC) company for CO2 removal.

name: MYNO
tech_note: MYNO develops Carbon Removal Facilities that pyrolyze forest residuals and waste biomass into biochar for agriculture, infrastructure, and stormwater applications, while generating renewable energy and selling durable CDR credits.
description: MYNO Carbon is a Washington-based biochar producer founded in 2020 that planned a large-scale Carbon Removal Facility in Port Angeles, WA using forest residual feedstock. The company was awarded $20.4M from the USDA Fertilizer Production Expansion Program in late 2024, but that funding was cancelled by the Trump administration in April 2025, leaving the facility's status uncertain.

name: Macrocarbon
tech_note: MacroCarbon cultivates pelagic Sargassum seaweed in offshore aquafarms and converts the biomass via thermochemical processes (pyrolysis) into biochar, carbon black, and bio-hydrocarbons (including sustainable aviation fuel) for permanent carbon sequestration.
description: <cite index="2-3,2-4">MacroCarbon SL is a Spain-based (Gran Canaria) spin-off of Germany's Alfred Wegener Institute and Carbonwave (US), focused on domesticating and cultivating Sargassum seaweed for carbon dioxide removal and industrial feedstock.</cite> <cite index="4-5,4-6">The company produces sustainable aviation fuel and other biofuels from floating seaweeds like pelagic Sargassum, while storing part of the captured carbon in biochar and carbon black for long-term sequestration.</cite> <cite index="7-9,7-10">In October 2025 MacroCarbon received permits from the Canary Islands government for a 40,000 m² seaweed farm near the Plataforma Oceánica de Canarias, bridging pilot and commercial deployment, with a first commercial facility requiring €80 million targeted in the next few years.</cite>

name: Made In Ontario: CHAR Technologies Is Building Up Biocarbon
Made of Air
tech_note: Made of Air pyrolyzes forestry/agricultural waste into biochar and functionalizes it as a filler in thermoplastic composites used for building facades, automotive parts, and consumer goods, locking carbon into durable manufactured materials.
description: Berlin-based materials company founded in 2016 that turns wood-waste biochar into carbon-negative thermoplastic granules and composites for long-lived industrial applications (e.g., Audi dealership facades, H&M sunglasses). Each ton of material reportedly sequesters multiple tons of CO2 in products, positioning the firm as a biochar-based CDR supplier via durable material pools.

name: Mangrove Systems
tech_note: Marine CDR company developing seaweed-based carbon removal solutions.
description: Mangrove Systems provides a digital Measurement, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) platform called Mangrove Nexus for CDR and CCS projects. Their platform tracks CO2 molecules through project operations, supporting various CDR pathways like biochar, DAC, ERW, and RAE.

name: Marine carbon dioxide removal: What it is and how it works
tech_note: Carbon Direct is a science-led climate advisory firm providing CDR due diligence, quality criteria, procurement support, and software for corporate buyers — it does not physically remove CO2 itself.
description: <cite index="5-1,5-2">Carbon Direct provides science-backed carbon management solutions, including carbon measurement, emission reduction, and high-quality carbon removal services, supporting Fortune 500 companies, governments, and private entities.</cite> <cite index="3-10,3-11">In July 2025, Carbon Direct and Microsoft released the fifth edition of the Criteria for High-Quality Carbon Dioxide Removal, a leading industry benchmark for CDR quality.</cite> The seed URL is actually a Carbon Direct article on marine CDR, not a separate company; Carbon Direct is a CDR ecosystem advisor/consultancy, not a removal supplier.

name: Marquis Energy
tech_note: Marquis captures biogenic CO2 from its corn-ethanol fermentation process and injects it into an on-site Mt. Simon saline formation well for permanent geological storage (BECCS).
description: Marquis Energy operates the world's largest dry-mill ethanol plant in Hennepin, Illinois, and is developing a large-scale BECCS project (via subsidiary Marquis Carbon Capture LLC) to permanently sequester ~1.2 million tons/year of biogenic CO2 in the Mt. Simon formation beneath its industrial complex. While ethanol production is the core business, the company is building dedicated CDR removal infrastructure with permanent geological storage, qualifying it as a supplier.

name: Mast Reforestation
tech_note: Buries fire-killed trees in engineered low-oxygen underground chambers (Terrestrial Storage of Biomass) combined with post-wildfire reforestation, generating Puro.earth-certified durable CDR credits.
description: Mast Reforestation is a Seattle-based post-wildfire reforestation company that removes CO2 by burying unmerchantable fire-killed trees in engineered anoxic chambers, using credit revenue to fund native conifer replanting. Its MT1 project in Montana buried over 10 million pounds of biomass and issued 4,277 Puro.earth TSB credits in early 2026, with all MT1 credits sold to buyers including RBC, BMO, Bain & Company, CNaught, and Muir AI. The company operates two major Western US tree nurseries (Silvaseed and Cal Forest) and is scaling additional biomass burial projects.

name: Mati
tech_note: Spreads finely crushed basalt on smallholder croplands in India and Africa to accelerate silicate weathering and sequester CO2 as bicarbonate, supported by an in-house MRV platform (matiC) developed with IIT Kanpur and Yale.
description: Mati Carbon is a carbon removal supplier that deploys pulverized basalt onto smallholder farms in India, Tanzania, and Zambia to accelerate enhanced rock weathering. The company won the $50M XPRIZE Carbon Removal grand prize in 2025 and secured blended finance from J.P. Morgan backed by the Schmidt Family Foundation to expand across the Global South.

name: Metalplant
tech_note: Spreads crushed olivine/magnesium-silicate rock on fields planted with nickel-hyperaccumulating plants in Albania, producing both carbon-negative nickel ("NegativeNickel") and ERW-based CDR credits.
description: Metalplant is a US-headquartered CDR supplier operating field sites in Albania on serpentine-rich soils of the Mirdita Ophiolite. Its "Hyperweathering" approach couples enhanced rock weathering of olivine with nickel phytomining to co-produce carbon removal credits and critical minerals for the EV/green-steel supply chain. The company is working toward Puro.earth ERW methodology compliance and announced a commercial trial for 2025.

name: Metzler
tech_note: Rotary-kiln pyrolysis of sustainably harvested hardwood chips/sawdust at ~1,350°F, water-quenched to produce high-carbon (70–90%) biochar products.
description: Metzler Biochar, a division of Metzler Forest Products LLC in Reedsville, Pennsylvania, produces wood-based biochar from local sawmill co-products using an industrial-scale rotary kiln pyrolysis system. The company sells biochar and biochar-amended soil blends for agriculture, stormwater management, and livestock applications, and recovers excess process heat to displace propane in firewood drying kilns.

name: Meva Energy
tech_note: Modular biomass gasification plants producing industrial biosyngas with biochar as a carbon-sequestering by-product.
description: Meva Energy is a Swedish cleantech firm (founded 2008, based in Gothenburg) that builds modular biomass gasification plants producing renewable biosyngas for industrial customers, with biochar as a carbon-negative by-product used for soil carbon storage. In October 2025 the company secured €40M venture debt from the EIB to scale plants for Sofidel, IKEA Poland, and Elcowire.

name: Midori Partner
tech_note: Midori Climate Partner develops biochar carbon removal projects using agricultural biomass residues in Southeast Asia, alongside agroforestry and mangrove restoration.
description: <cite index="8-13,8-14,8-15">Midori Climate Partner Pte. Ltd. is a Singapore-based carbon credit developer specializing in ecosystem restoration, structuring biochar and agroforestry projects across Southeast Asia including Cambodia, Thailand, Vietnam, and Malaysia.</cite> <cite index="4-3,4-4">In early 2025 the company closed a pre-seed round led by Tokio Marine Holdings to expand biochar carbon removal projects across Asia, with its first project launching in Cambodia.</cite> Note: DB listed as Germany-based, but company is actually headquartered in Singapore.

name: Milkywire
tech_note: Milkywire is a Stockholm-based procurement platform and advisory that channels corporate funding into durable CDR suppliers via its Climate Transformation Fund and tailored Seed/Scale CDR portfolios.
description: <cite index="2-4,2-7">Stockholm-based Milkywire is an impact platform that pre-purchases durable carbon removal credits and has purchased from many suppliers through its Climate Transformation Fund, backed by companies like Klarna, Spotify and ING Bank.</cite> <cite index="5-5,5-6">Their 2025 round brought total CDR suppliers supported through the CTF to 40, second only to Shopify and Stripe per CDR.fyi data.</cite> They do not remove CO2 themselves — they run open calls, vet projects, and broker procurement for corporate buyers, placing them squarely in the CDR ecosystem.

name: MioTech
tech_note: MioTech's carbon asset team operates the Nian'da biochar facility in Nanjing, which pyrolyzes agricultural waste into biochar applied to farmland for durable carbon sequestration and CORC issuance.
description: MioTech is an AI-based ESG data and sustainability analytics company headquartered in Shanghai/Hong Kong that has expanded into CDR project development. <cite index="3-3,3-4">Its carbon asset team developed China's first biochar carbon credit project, registered on Puro.earth with support from Nanjing Nian'da Environmental Technology and Nanjing Forestry University</cite>, and <cite index="7-4,7-5">became the first biochar supplier in China to issue CORCs, with the Nanjing-based Nian'da project generating 330 CORCs in its first accreditation period</cite>. <cite index="3-14">MioTech has announced plans to develop 50,000 tons of carbon credits by 2027 spanning biochar, geological storage, carbonated materials, and enhanced rock weathering.</cite>

name: Miraïa
tech_note: Miraïa operates modernized continuous vertical-furnace pyrolysis of woody biomass to produce biochar, bio-oils and syngas/electricity, targeting agriculture and industrial (e.g. metallurgical coke replacement) uses.
description: Miraïa is a French (Toulouse-based) climate-tech startup, founded in 2023, commercializing continuous wood pyrolysis to produce biochar, bio-oils, and renewable energy. It is building a pilot demonstrator in Colomiers (Haute-Garonne) and plans its first commercial-scale plant in Garlin (Pyrénées-Atlantiques) with a target of 20,000 t/yr biochar, with longer-term ambitions for 6–7 plants.

name: Mission Zero
tech_note: Develops a modular electrochemical direct air capture system that uses a water-based solvent regenerated with renewable electricity to recover atmospheric CO2 for utilization or permanent storage.
description: <cite index="2-14,2-15">Mission Zero Technologies is a UK-based company that develops electrochemical direct air capture (DAC) technology inspired by biological reactions that manage CO₂ in the body, designed to recover atmospheric CO₂ at any scale.</cite> <cite index="10-1,10-2">The company has deployed three systems to date, including a UK plant with O.C.O Technology that pairs DAC with building-materials production and a third system now capturing CO₂ for permanent underground storage at Deep Sky in Canada.</cite>

name: Moola Pflanzenkohle
tech_note: Pyrolysis of plant biomass to produce EBC-certified biochar for soil amendment, animal feed, and stable bedding applications.
description: Moola is a German/Austrian biochar producer that uses pyrolysis to convert plant biomass into EBC-certified biochar, sold as a soil amendment, animal feed additive, and stable bedding. The company describes itself as an early industrial biochar pioneer in Germany, and is an active member of the Fachverband Pflanzenkohle industry association. Products remain available through retailers in 2024–2025.

name: Mote
tech_note: Mote gasifies woody biomass waste (forestry and agricultural residues) to produce clean hydrogen while capturing and geologically sequestering the byproduct CO2, a BiCRS/BECCS approach.
description: Mote is a Los Angeles-based BiCRS startup, spun out of Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, that converts wood waste into carbon-negative hydrogen with permanent CO2 sequestration. Its flagship Bakersfield, California facility has completed a FEL-2 study and received a DOE Loan Programs Office Part II invitation, with a second project planned with SMUD in Sacramento. In March 2025 Mote closed $7M in Series A funding to advance its first commercial-scale plant.

name: NAWARO ENERGIE Betrieb
tech_note: Operates wood-gasification CHP plants in Austria; biochar is produced as a by-product of wood gasification at the Perg site and sold for landscaping, agriculture, construction and metallurgy.
description: NAWARO ENERGIE Betrieb GmbH is an Austrian bioenergy producer headquartered in Zwettl, operating biomass and wood-gas power plants across the Waldviertel region. At its Perg location (in operation since 2023), wood gasification yields biochar as a co-product, which the company sells for agricultural, construction and metallurgical uses. The firm is listed as a member of the European Biochar Industry Consortium.

name: NEG8 Carbon
tech_note: Solid sorbent DAC
description: NEG8 Carbon is an Irish company that develops and utilizes modular solid sorbent-based Direct Air Capture (DAC) technology to remove CO2 from the atmosphere. They aim to capture and store CO2 permanently or for reuse.

name: NULIFE GreenTech
tech_note: Bio-oil
description: NULIFE GreenTech transforms waste biomass into stable, carbon-rich bio-oil using Hydrothermal Liquefaction (HTL) technology, which is then permanently sequestered in underground reservoirs.

name: NY Carbon
tech_note: Produces high-carbon biochar via pyrolysis (Tigercat Carbonator 6050) from locally sourced woody waste biomass, primarily eastern white pine off-cuts from an adjacent lumber mill.
description: NY Carbon is a Saugerties, NY-based commercial-scale biochar producer serving the Hudson Valley and New England. They use 100% woody waste feedstock from within a 15-mile radius and supply biochar for agricultural soil applications, including partnerships with the 4 Corners Carbon Coalition, American Farmland Trust, and Cornell Cooperative Extension.

name: National Institute for Research and Development of Isotopic and Molecular Technologies
National Institute of Oceanography and Fisheries
Nattergal
tech_note: Nattergal is a UK-based rewilding/nature-recovery company that purchases degraded farmland and restores it to biodiverse habitat mosaics, selling carbon credits, Biodiversity Net Gain units, and other ecosystem-service credits.
description: Nattergal is a UK private nature recovery company founded in 2021 that acquires and rewilds degraded agricultural land at scale, currently operating three sites (Boothby Wildland in Lincolnshire, High Fen Wildland in Norfolk, and Harold's Park in Essex). It generates revenue from carbon credits, Biodiversity Net Gain units, water credits, UK Landscape Recovery Scheme funding, and ecotourism, and partnered with Knepp Estate and Arup on the Knepp Wildland Carbon Project to quantify rewilding carbon sequestration.

name: Negative Emissions Platform
tech_note: Brussels-based industry coalition and trade association that advocates for EU policy recognition of permanent carbon dioxide removal technologies (DAC, BECCS, ERW, biochar, mineralisation, marine CDR).
description: The Negative Emissions Platform (NEP) is a Brussels-based membership association representing CDR technology developers, researchers and sponsors before EU institutions. It does not remove CO2 itself; instead it lobbies for the Carbon Removal Certification Framework, responds to EU consultations, and convenes the CDR community (e.g. hosting the CDR30 Pavilion at COP30). It is a core ecosystem/advocacy body dedicated solely to the CDR industry.

name: Nellie
tech_note: Grows microalgae in photobioreactors to capture CO2 from ambient air or point sources, then pyrolyzes the biomass into biochar (PhycoChar) used as a soil amendment/biofertiliser in UK agriculture.
description: Nellie Technologies is a UK-based CDR supplier operating a pilot facility in Mwyndy, South Wales, that cultivates microalgae for CO2 capture and converts the biomass into durable biochar. The company sells Puro.earth CORCs and signed a 17,500-ton, 5-year offtake with Zurich Insurance in January 2025, and won the 2025 IOP Business Start-Up Award.

name: NeoCarbon
tech_note: Solid-sorbent direct air capture modules retrofitted into industrial cooling towers, using existing airflow and waste heat; captured CO2 mineralized into concrete via partnership with Carbonaide.
description: NeoCarbon is a Berlin-based DAC startup that retrofits solid-sorbent carbon-capture modules onto industrial cooling towers, leveraging existing airflow and waste heat to reduce DAC costs. The company has built autonomous pilot modules, produced its first batch of low-carbon concrete with partner Carbonaide in early 2025, and plans to deploy its third DAC unit at a live data center in 2026.

name: Net Zero Lab
tech_note: Academic research group at the Max Planck Institute for Innovation and Competition studying climate tech, corporate decarbonization, and carbon markets, and co-organizing the ACRA accelerator for Sub-Saharan African CDR startups.
description: Net Zero Lab is an independent Max Planck research group (launched 2024, led by Benedict Probst) based in Munich, focused on economics of climate technology, corporate net-zero strategies, and carbon markets. It is a co-organizer of the Africa Carbon Removal Accelerator (ACRA) alongside sus.lab ETH Zurich, Strathmore University, Nuvoni, and remove. It is not a CDR supplier but an academic/ecosystem actor supporting CDR startup development.

name: NetZero
tech_note: Produces biochar via pyrolysis of tropical agricultural residues (coffee husks, cocoa shells, sugarcane bagasse) at modular industrial plants and applies it to soils for high-permanence carbon removal.
description: <cite index="6-1">NetZero is a French startup founded in 2021 and headquartered in Paris, specializing in large-scale biochar production from unused tropical crop residues for permanent atmospheric carbon removal and soil enhancement.</cite> <cite index="8-17,8-18">It operates three first-generation plants — one in Cameroon processing cocoa husks and two in Brazil dedicated to coffee parchment, together processing 22,000 tonnes of organic waste into biochar per year (≈6,000 tCO2 sequestered annually).</cite> <cite index="6-8">NetZero was first runner-up in the 2025 XPRIZE Carbon Removal competition, earning a $15 million prize.</cite>

name: Neustark
tech_note: Captures biogenic CO2 from biogas plants and permanently stores it via accelerated mineralization (carbonation) in demolished concrete and other mineral wastes such as slag and incinerator bottom ash.
description: <cite index="4-12,4-13">Founded in 2019, neustark is a spin-off from ETH Zurich based in Bern, and is expanding across Europe with 38 active capture and storage projects in Switzerland, Germany, Austria, the UK, France, Italy and Liechtenstein.</cite> <cite index="6-10,6-11,6-12,6-13">The company captures CO2 at point source, then binds it in mineral waste streams via an accelerated mineralization process — biogenic CO2 is captured from partnering biogas plants, liquified and transported to construction waste recycling sites where it is injected into concrete granulates or other mineral waste such as slag, permanently binding the CO2.</cite>

name: Neutralizing Environmental Trash Inc.
tech_note: Biochar
description: Neutralizing Environmental Trash Inc. (N.E.T. Inc) converts biomass into biochar to address environmental challenges. They are involved in a joint venture for biochar projects.

name: Neutura
tech_note: Biochar
description: Neutura is a carbon removal company that transforms agricultural waste and biomass into biochar via pyrolysis, effectively sequestering carbon and preventing its release into the atmosphere. They have launched a pioneering biochar project in Indonesia.

name: Next Wave Carbon Removals
tech_note: Produces biochar from waste wood using ARTi pyrolysis technology in partnership with Maxsum Environmental, with plans to sell carbon credits.
description: Next Wave Carbon Removal is a US-based (Des Moines, Iowa) biochar producer combining ARTi Biochar's pyrolysis technology with Maxsum Environmental's investment backing. The company aims to be a vertically integrated biochar-to-carbon-credit operation, starting in the US and expanding into Latin America.

name: NextGen CDR
tech_note: CDR buyers' club / advance market commitment purchasing certified permanent removal credits on behalf of a collective of corporate buyers.
description: NextGen CDR is a buyers' club / advance-market-commitment facility jointly established by South Pole and Mitsubishi Corporation to aggregate corporate demand for durable, certified carbon removals at a target price of $200/tonne. Founding and subsequent buyers include BCG, LGT, Mitsui O.S.K. Lines, Swiss Re, UBS and Mizuho. It has contracted offtakes across DAC, BiCRS, biochar, mineralization and enhanced weathering (e.g. Neustark, Exomad Green, Alt Carbon) but does not itself remove CO2 — it is a demand-side aggregator in the CDR ecosystem.

name: Nina Energy
tech_note: Biochar
description: Nina Energy is an Ecuadorian company that transforms agro-industrial residues into biochar, renewable energy, and biofuels, promoting a sustainable bioeconomy across Latin America. They specialize in manufacturing modular, automated reactors for biochar production.

name: Nordbex
tech_note: BECCS
description: Nordbex is a Swedish company that finances, develops, builds, and operates carbon-negative power plants, specifically utilizing Bio Energy with Carbon Capture and Storage (BECCS) to provide baseload power and remove CO2 from the atmosphere.

name: Nordgau Carbon
tech_note: Biochar
description: Nordgau Carbon is a German company that produces biochar from wood chips through pyrolysis, safely capturing CO2 and selling it under the Nordgau Carbon brand for animal, soil, and garden needs.

name: Nordic Carbon
tech_note: Biochar
description: Nordic Carbon transforms waste biomass into stable, high-quality biochar through advanced pyrolysis, locking away CO₂ for centuries. They focus on sustainable carbon dioxide removal.

name: Nordiczero
tech_note: Develops biochar and bioash from biogenic residues for use as additives in concrete and building materials, locking carbon into durable construction products.
description: Nordiczero is a Sweden-based company developing solutions that utilize biochar and bioash produced from biogenic residues as components in concrete and building materials. By embedding stable pyrolysis carbon in cementitious products, the company targets durable carbon storage in the built environment.

name: Nordvästra Skånes Renhållnings
tech_note: Municipal waste utility operating Sweden's largest biochar plant, pyrolyzing urban garden waste (~7,000 t/yr) into ~1,500 t/yr of biochar using Vow/Scanship BioGreen pyrolysis technology, with surplus heat fed to district heating.
description: Nordvästra Skånes Renhållnings AB (NSR) is a Swedish municipal recycling company owned by six northwest Skåne municipalities (Bjuv, Båstad, Helsingborg, Höganäs, Åstorp, Ängelholm). At its Filborna site in Helsingborg it operates a biochar production facility inaugurated in June 2022 — the largest of its kind in Sweden — converting residual urban green waste into biochar while supplying district heating, and hosts a Biochar Competence Centre opened alongside the 2023 International Biochar Summit.

name: Norma
tech_note: Norma is developing a supercapacitive electrochemical Direct Air Capture system that integrates energy storage with CO2 capture to dramatically reduce energy consumption.
description: <cite index="3-1,3-13">Norma is a Paris-based climate tech startup building low-cost, modular machines for direct air capture, co-founded by CTO Silvia Pugliese and CEO Mónica Larrazábal (ex-McKinsey, MIT MBA).</cite> <cite index="2-3,2-4">The company is developing a breakthrough DAC technology that integrates supercapacitor-based energy storage with carbon capture in a single electrochemical system, storing and reusing the energy required to capture CO₂.</cite> <cite index="3-10,3-11">It secured its first customer for carbon removal through the Milkywire Climate Transformation Fund and is building its first pilot system.</cite>

name: NormaTech
tech_note: CDR company currently hiring (2 open positions). Category: Direct Air Capture.
description: No information found for NormaTech, a DAC company based in Germany, in the provided search results.

name: Norsk e-Fuel
tech_note: DAC project developer
description: Norsk e-Fuel is a Norwegian company that produces sustainable aviation fuel (e-fuel) using Direct Air Capture (DAC) technology to source CO2, combined with Power-to-Liquid and Fischer-Tropsch synthesis.

name: North America's Largest Biochar Plant Announced In Canada
tech_note: Carbonity operates an industrial-scale pyrolysis plant in Port-Cartier, Quebec that converts forestry residues from Groupe Rémabec into biochar using Airex Energy's proprietary DryFX and CarbonFX technologies.
description: Carbonity is a joint venture equally owned by Airex Energy, Groupe Rémabec, and SUEZ that operates Canada's first industrial-scale biochar plant in Port-Cartier, Quebec, inaugurated in May 2025. The facility starts at 10,000 tonnes/year biochar capacity, set to triple by 2026 to become North America's largest, and at full capacity will sequester 75,000 tCO2e per year. Carbon credits are marketed on the voluntary market by First Climate, and Microsoft signed a 36,000-credit offtake in 2024.

name: NorthStar Clean Energy
tech_note: Developing a BECCS/BiCRS project by converting the TES Filer City coal plant in Michigan to biomass fuel retrofitted with Babcock & Wilcox's SolveBright post-combustion CO2 capture, targeting ~500,000 tons CO2/yr permanently stored underground.
description: NorthStar Clean Energy is a wholly owned subsidiary of CMS Energy (NYSE: CMS) developing one of the first US large-scale BECCS/BiCRS projects at the Filer City Station in Michigan, with planned commercial operation in 2029. The project would capture and permanently store up to 550,000 tons of CO2 annually and sell carbon removal credits to corporate buyers, alongside the parent firm's broader solar, wind, storage, and natural gas portfolio.

name: Nova Pangaea Technologies
tech_note: Biochar
description: Nova Pangaea Technologies converts woody and non-food derived agricultural residues into high-value products like 2G ethanol and biochar. Their biochar sequesters CO2 from the atmosphere, providing a net negative emissions process.

name: Novocarbo
tech_note: Operates pyrolysis-based Carbon Removal Parks that convert biogenic residues into biochar plus renewable heat for district heating networks.
description: Novocarbo is a Hamburg-based climate tech company that operates Carbon Removal Parks across Germany, using pyrolysis to convert biogenic residues into biochar while producing renewable heat. Recent activity includes new sites in Bochum and Dessau, the German Sustainability Award 2025, and a 2025 pilot with Hansa Asphalt that produced the first certified CDR credits from biochar-infused asphalt.

name: NuAria
tech_note: NuAria develops solid-sorbent Direct Air Capture systems using cylindrical wound sorbent-filled membranes designed to be low-cost and scalable, and offers carbon credit subscriptions.
description: NuAria is a US-based direct air capture startup developing a novel sorbent packaged as cylindrical wound membranes, aiming at affordable and scalable CO2 removal. The company sells carbon credits via subscriptions and upfront purchases to industries and governments pursuing net-zero targets. Public signals are limited — the website is live and it was featured on a 2025 DAC watchlist, but there is no recent funding or deployment news.

name: NuWa Solutions
tech_note: Develops Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement (OAE) pilots with MRV, safety stop-rules, and community-first permitting to deliver verifiable marine CO2 removals.
description: <cite index="13-1,13-2">NuWa Solutions is a Delaware-based marine carbon dioxide removal company specializing in ocean alkalinity enhancement and blue carbon approaches, working with governments, institutions, and enterprises.</cite> <cite index="11-1,11-4">The company develops OAE for verifiable marine CO2 removal with rigorous MRV and safety guardrails, and is currently pre-credit with a buyer interest list.</cite>

name: Nuxsen
tech_note: Solid sorbent DAC
description: Nuxsen develops novel direct air capture (DAC) technologies, specifically using electrochemically-activated cellular monolithic sorbent geometries, for large-scale CO2 removal.

name: Néolithe
tech_note: Néolithe shreds non-recyclable waste and binds it with a mineral binder under high pressure to produce construction aggregates ("Anthropocite") that lock in biogenic carbon from the waste.
description: Néolithe is a French industrial startup (based in Anjou, ~100-200 employees) that operates "Fossilizers" — machines that transform non-recyclable, non-hazardous waste into mineral aggregates via its Accelerated Fossilization process, sequestering biogenic carbon contained in the waste. The aggregates substitute natural aggregates in concrete and are claimed to store ~337-420 kg CO2e per tonne. The company raised €60M in 2023 and is scaling plants across France.

name: O.C.O Technology
tech_note: Uses patented Accelerated Carbonation Technology (ACT) to react CO2 with Air Pollution Control residues and other industrial wastes, permanently sequestering CO2 as stable carbonate minerals in a carbon-negative manufactured limestone aggregate for construction.
description: O.C.O Technology is a UK-based mineralization CDR supplier operating multiple aggregate manufacturing facilities (Brandon, Avonmouth, Leeds, Wretham) that transform hazardous waste residues and CO2 into carbon-negative construction aggregate. They sell verified carbon removal credits via the Puro.earth registry and are partnering with Mission Zero Technologies to co-locate DAC at their Wretham site.

name: OBIO
tech_note: Operates an industrial-scale pyrolysis plant at Rudshøgda, Norway, converting PEFC-certified forestry wood chips into EBC-certified biochar for soil amendment, animal feed, and concrete applications.
description: <cite index="6-1,6-2">OBIO is a Norwegian biochar company based in the Opland/central region that built the first industrial-scale pyrolysis plant in Norway at Rudshøgda in Ringsaker municipality.</cite> <cite index="4-5,4-6,4-7">Obio AS was founded in December 2022 when the pyrolysis business was transferred from Oplandske Bioenergi, and is owned 60% by district heating company Eidsiva Bioenergi and 40% by forest owners cooperative Glommen Mjøsen Skog.</cite> The company sells Puro.earth CORCs and produces biochar for agricultural, livestock feed, and concrete applications.

name: OLNEO
tech_note: Produces biochar from agricultural residues via pyrolysis and applies it to degraded soils, with integrated sensor/satellite-based MRV for carbon credit certification.
description: <cite index="10-1">OLNEO is a climate deeptech startup developing modular carbon removal systems, based in Paris, France with 1-10 employees.</cite> <cite index="6-1,6-2">The company is building carbon removal infrastructure in Africa using biochar, converting local agricultural residues into high-quality biochar</cite>, <cite index="2-14,2-15">rooted in Algeria and designed to scale across Africa and the MENA region.</cite>

name: Occidental Petroleum
tech_note: Develops and operates liquid-solvent (KOH/calciner) Direct Air Capture plants with saline-formation geologic sequestration via Class VI injection wells in the Permian Basin.
description: Occidental Petroleum (NYSE: OXY) is a major U.S. oil and gas company that operates a significant Direct Air Capture business through its wholly-owned subsidiaries 1PointFive and Carbon Engineering (acquired 2023). Its flagship STRATOS facility in Ector County, Texas — designed to capture up to 500,000 tonnes of CO2 per year — is in final startup, with Phase 1 expected online in Q2 2026 and CDR credit offtakes signed with Microsoft, Amazon, BlackRock, JPMorgan, Palo Alto Networks, and Bain & Company.

name: Ocean Frontier Institute
tech_note: Ocean research institute at Dalhousie University studying marine carbon dioxide removal and ocean carbon cycling.
description: The Ocean Frontier Institute is a Canadian organization focused on transnational interdisciplinary ocean research, including ocean-based Carbon Dioxide Removal (CDR) methods. They aim to produce social, economic, and environmental benefits through their research and initiatives.

name: Ocean Nourishment Corporation
tech_note: Ocean Nourishment Corporation develops macronutrient ocean fertilization technology (PhytoPlus biostimulant, now green-ammonia-based) deployed from ships or offshore platforms to stimulate phytoplankton growth and export carbon to the deep ocean.
description: Ocean Nourishment Corporation (ONC) is an Australian marine CDR company founded in 2004 that uses ocean fertilization by adding balanced macronutrients to nutrient-poor waters to stimulate phytoplankton growth and sequester CO2. Together with its sister WhaleX Foundation, ONC is a Top 100 XPRIZE Carbon Removal team and is running small-scale biopod and photobioreactor experiments while seeking partners in green hydrogen, green ammonia, shipping, and offshore platforms.

name: Ocean pHix
tech_note: OAE
description: No information about Ocean pHix was found in the provided search results.

name: Octavia Carbon
tech_note: Solid sorbent DAC
description: Octavia Carbon is a Direct Air Capture (DAC) company based in Kenya that designs, builds, and deploys solid sorbent DAC technology to capture CO2 from the atmosphere, which is then permanently stored through mineralization in volcanic rock.

name: One Earth Energy
tech_note: BECCS
description: One Earth Energy is an ethanol producer that is actively pursuing carbon sequestration through BECCS, specifically by capturing CO2 from its ethanol production and storing it underground.

name: OnePoint5
tech_note: Converts surplus agricultural crop residue in South Asia into biochar via pyrolysis for soil and infrastructure applications, generating durable carbon removal credits.
description: OnePoint5 is an India-based biochar CDR supplier that transforms agricultural residue (crop stubble) into high-quality biochar for soil and infrastructure applications. They operate a batch-tracing platform called StubbleX and are listed as a supplier on the Isometric registry.

name: Onnu
tech_note: Onnu develops pyrolysis plants and manufactures biochar from waste biomass (including poultry litter, oil palm residues), selling EBC-certified biochar and generating Puro.Earth CORCs.
description: <cite index="2-1,2-2">Onnu is a UK-headquartered project developer and technology provider that develops its own pyrolysis plants and consults on plants for clients across Europe and SE Asia.</cite> <cite index="2-6,2-7">It operates Onnu Biochar, the biochar trading arm selling EBC-certified biochar for retail customers in Europe, and Onnu Bioflow, the renewable commodities trading arm for larger-scale customers.</cite> <cite index="4-16">Onnu is registered with the Puro.Earth carbon registry and biochar from its Wye Valley hubs qualifies for CO2 Removal Certificates (CORCs).</cite>

name: Oraquel
tech_note: Solid sorbent DAC
description: Oraquel is a Swiss company that develops and operates DAC reactors using patented filters with a sorbent insert made of eight natural absorbent and adsorbent substances to capture and store CO2 from the air.

name: Oregon Biochar Solutions
tech_note: Biochar
description: Oregon Biochar Solutions manufactures and sells ultra-pure biochar sourced from forest wood in the Pacific Northwest, utilizing biochar as a carbon dioxide removal method.

name: Organic Mechanics
tech_note: Biochar
description: Organic Mechanics produces biochar and biochar blends as soil amendments. Their biochar is made from softwood pine through pyrolysis, which is a method of Carbon Dioxide Removal (CDR).

name: Origen
tech_note: Solid sorbent DAC
description: Origen is a Carbon Dioxide Removal (CDR) company that uses a proprietary limestone-based Direct Air Capture (DAC) method, integrating a lime kiln and air contactor technology to permanently sequester CO₂.

name: Origin Biochar
tech_note: Biochar
description: Origin Biochar produces biochar through pyrolysis, offering products like feedchar for livestock and horticultural biochar for soil amendment, aiming to sequester CO2 and provide co-benefits.

name: Orsted
tech_note: BECCS
description: Orsted is a renewable energy company actively involved in Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Storage (BECCS) projects, capturing CO2 from biomass-fired power plants and storing it underground.

name: Oxford Charcoal Company
tech_note: Biochar
description: Oxford Charcoal Company manufactures and sells biochar, a soil enhancer produced from hardwoods as a byproduct of their clean charcoal-making process. They offer biochar products for agriculture, gardening, and environmental restoration, contributing to carbon dioxide removal.

name: Oxy
tech_note: Oxy deploys Carbon Engineering's liquid-solvent DAC technology at commercial scale via subsidiary 1PointFive, with captured CO2 sequestered in Class VI wells or used for enhanced oil recovery.
description: Occidental (Oxy) is a major US oil & gas producer that, through its subsidiary 1PointFive (and with Carbon Engineering technology and OxyChem operations), is building large-scale Direct Air Capture facilities including STRATOS in Ector County, Texas. <cite index="8-2">STRATOS, described as the world's largest DAC facility, received EPA Class VI sequestration permits in April 2025 for Ector County, Texas</cite> and <cite index="4-1">in January 2026, 1PointFive announced Bain & Company had purchased 9,000 metric tons of DAC-based CDR credits over three years</cite>.

name: Ozen
tech_note: Ozen operates a wood pyrolysis plant in Wałcz, Poland producing charcoal/biochar briquettes and renewable electricity, with an EBC C-Sink certificate showing ~3.22 t CO2eq sink potential per ton of biochar.
description: Ozen Sp. z o.o. is a Polish charcoal and biochar manufacturer based in Wałcz that uses a patented wood-pyrolysis technology to produce charcoal, briquettes, and green electricity from pyrolysis heat. The company obtained a European Biochar Certificate (EBC) C-Sink certification for a batch produced in 2021-2022, qualifying it as a biochar CDR supplier, though its primary commercial focus remains industrial/BBQ charcoal rather than CDR credit sales.

name: PUHI
tech_note: PUHI operates pyrolysis reactors that convert wood- and agriculture-based side streams (including recycled demolition wood) into biochar, district heat, and biochar carbon removal credits.
description: <cite index="1-1,1-2">PUHI is a Finland-based biochar and carbon removal company offering pyrolysis-based climate tech, biochar products, and biomass piloting services, with its first biochar production plant in Industrial Park MORE, Hämeenlinna.</cite> <cite index="3-2">Its environmental permit allows PUHI to process up to 20,000 tons of wood- and agriculture-based side streams annually into biochar, district heating, and carbon removal credits.</cite> PUHI is listed as a CORC supplier on Puro.earth and is a member of the European Biochar Industry Consortium.

name: Pacific Biochar
tech_note: I’ll break down how I think this ... of Pacific Biochar. Response to 1.) Yes, of course. It doesn’t appear to be new on Microsoft’s radar, but I’m thankful they’re highlighting it because I appreci...
description: Pacific Biochar is a BiCRS company that produces biochar from forest residue biomass through pyrolysis, which is then applied to soil to remove and store carbon dioxide while improving soil health and aiding forest management.

name: Pacific Biochar/Wren
tech_note: Retrofits existing biomass power plants and sawmills to co-produce biochar from forest and sawmill residues, which is then applied to agricultural soils for durable carbon storage.
description: Pacific Biochar is a California-based benefit corporation that partners with biomass power plants and sawmills to produce biochar from forestry residues. The biochar is distributed to agricultural operations, primarily vineyards and compost yards, and the company sells verified carbon removal credits under standards including Isometric's Biochar Protocol.

name: Paebbl
tech_note: Reacts captured CO₂ with crushed olivine in a reactor to form magnesium carbonate powder used as a supplementary cementitious material in concrete.
description: Paebbl is a Dutch-Nordic mineralization company that converts captured CO₂ into a stable mineral powder used as a supplementary cementitious material (SCM) for the construction industry. In March 2025 the company launched its continuous demo plant in Rotterdam, claimed as a world-first for continuous CO₂ mineralization at demo scale, and plans a commercial plant by 2027.

name: Pannonia Bio
tech_note: BECCS
description: Pannonia Bio is Europe's leading biorefinery, producing bioethanol, proteins, organic fertilizer, and advanced biomethane. While the company focuses on sustainable production, the search results do not explicitly detail their BECCS (Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Storage) method, but rather their broader bioeconomy activities.

name: Parallel Carbon
tech_note: Electrochemical DAC using a mineral sorbent coupled to water electrolysis, producing CO2 removal credits plus green hydrogen as a co-product.
description: Parallel Carbon is a UK-based (Manchester) direct air capture startup founded in 2021 that combines mineral-sorbent DAC with water electrolysis to co-produce CDR credits and green hydrogen. In February 2026 it signed a pre-purchase deal with Zurich Insurance Group for 1,200 tonnes of CDR, and it is joining the 2025 Shell StartUp Engine UK cohort while preparing a commercial pilot (100 t H2 and 1,000–2,000 t CO2/yr).

name: Partanna
tech_note: Produces a Portland-cement alternative from brine and steel slag that cures by absorbing atmospheric CO2 via mineralization, embedding permanent carbon into concrete building products.
description: <cite index="7-9,7-10,7-11,7-12">Partanna Global is an advanced materials company co-founded by Rick Fox that has developed a sustainable alternative to Portland cement, eliminating the clinkering process while permanently removing CO₂ from the atmosphere.</cite> <cite index="8-7">Their concrete substitute uses upcycled brine and steel slag that, when mixed, generate compounds that capture carbon dioxide.</cite> The company has a Verra-registered project and is expanding via partnerships with ADIO and Exeed Industries in the UAE.

name: Patch
tech_note: Carbon credit marketplace and API platform enabling businesses to buy high-quality carbon removal credits.
description: Patch is a platform and marketplace that provides technology to help organizations manage, sell, and buy high-integrity carbon credits from a global network of climate solutions, including various CDR methods.

name: Pathway Energy
tech_note: Integrates biomass gasification, Fischer-Tropsch syngas conversion, and geological CO2 sequestration to co-produce carbon-negative SAF and engineered carbon removals.
description: Pathway Energy is a Houston-based developer of carbon-negative sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) projects and a wholly-owned subsidiary of Nexus Holdings. Its first project in Port Arthur, Texas, aims to pair biomass gasification + Fischer-Tropsch SAF production with a BECCS system expected to remove ~1.9 million tonnes of CO2 annually, with construction targeted for 2026 and operations in 2029. Biomass will be supplied under a heads-of-terms agreement with Drax Group.

name: Pelican Renewables
tech_note: Captures biogenic CO2 from an ethanol plant and transports it by barge for permanent geologic sequestration in Class VI wells beneath the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta.
description: Pelican Renewables LLC is developing the Pelican Carbon Sequestration Hub on Rindge Tract in California's Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta, anchored by their Stockton ethanol facility which provides biogenic CO2 for permanent geologic storage via Class VI injection wells. The project also accepts third-party CO2 delivered by rail and barge (via affiliate ZuCO2 Transport), and was selected for a $45.2M DOE CarbonSAFE Phase III award in 2024-2025.

name: Perennial
tech_note: Perennial provides MMRV (measurement, monitoring, reporting, verification) software and digital soil mapping (ATLAS-SOC, VT0014) for soil carbon projects and agricultural Scope 3 programs; they quantify soil organic carbon rather than physically removing CO2.
description: Perennial (formerly Cloud Agronomics) is a Boulder, CO-based MRV platform for soil-based carbon removal, using AI, remote sensing, and digital soil mapping to quantify soil organic carbon at scale. They led the development of Verra's VT0014 tool and serve project developers, food/ag companies, and sustainability teams — they are part of the CDR ecosystem as a verifier/MRV provider, not a CO2 remover themselves.

name: Phlair
tech_note: Phlair develops an electrochemical hydrolyzer-based Direct Air Capture (DAC) system using a liquid pH-swing sorbent regenerated with renewable electricity.
description: <cite index="3-1,3-3,3-4">Founded in 2022 and based in Munich, Germany, Phlair develops hydrolyzer-based Direct Air Capture technology that uses a pH-swing mechanism for CO2 capture and release, enabling permanent storage or use in CO2-negative chemicals.</cite> <cite index="6-10,6-11,6-12">The company serves buyers including Google, McKinsey, JPMorganChase, Shopify, Stripe, H&M, and Deep Sky, closed a €12M+ seed round in 2024 with a €2.5M EU grant, and announced a $30M offtake agreement in 2025.</cite>

name: Phoenix Energy
tech_note: Phoenix Energy builds, owns, and operates community-scale biomass gasification plants in California that generate renewable electricity from forest/agricultural waste while producing biochar and carbon removal credits.
description: Phoenix Energy is a California-based developer and operator of community-scale BECCS plants that convert forestry and agricultural waste into renewable energy and biochar (sold under the Earthworks Biochar brand). Its North Fork Community Power plant is operational and it is constructing the 3 MW Blue Mountain Electric Company (BMEC) plant, with a third project planned at Napa Recycling & Waste Services. The company sells carbon removal credits alongside wildfire-mitigation services to agencies like Cal Fire and the US Forest Service.

name: Phykos
tech_note: Phykos grows fast-growing seaweed on solar-powered autonomous ocean platforms, then harvests and sinks the biomass below 1,500 m for long-term carbon sequestration.
description: Phykos, PBC is an Oakland, California ocean CDR startup (YC S21) founded in 2020 that develops mobile, solar-powered robotic vessels to cultivate seaweed in the open ocean and sink the biomass in the deep sea for carbon sequestration. The company sells carbon credits based on biomass sunk and remains a small early-stage team with limited public activity in the last ~12 months.

name: Pina Earth
tech_note: Develops forest conversion (monoculture-to-mixed-forest) carbon projects in Central Europe using remote-sensing and digital-twin simulation for MRV, then issues and sells the resulting certified carbon credits.
description: Pina Earth is a Munich-based climate-tech company that develops forest conversion and adaptation projects in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland, turning monoculture stands into climate-resilient mixed forests and issuing carbon credits certified under ISO 14064-2 and the eva Forest Climate Standard. In July 2025 it merged with Tree.ly to form Europe's largest forest carbon platform, and it has ongoing active partnerships (e.g. with myclimate on the Herzfelde project in Brandenburg).

name: Planet Savers
tech_note: Solid sorbent DAC
description: Planet Savers is the first Japanese Direct Air Capture (DAC) startup, focusing on DAC (Solid Sorbent) technology, specifically applying innovative zeolite material to DAC.

name: Planetary
tech_note: OAE
description: Planetary Technologies is a Canadian Marine CDR company that uses Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement (OAE) to remove carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and reduce ocean acidity. They have delivered the world's first verified OAE credits.

name: Planeteers
tech_note: OAE
description: Planeteers is a German climate tech startup that uses ocean alkalinity enhancement (OAE) through its patented HCM technology to produce mineral compounds (ikaite) that increase ocean alkalinity, allowing seawater to absorb and store additional CO2.

name: Plantd Materials
tech_note: Building materials company growing fast-growing perennial grasses to create carbon-negative structural panels.
description: Plantd Materials cultivates Arundo Donax grass to capture CO2 from the atmosphere and transform it into carbon-negative building materials, specifically structural panels.

name: Positive Biocarbon
tech_note: Biochar
description: Positive Biocarbon is a UK-based manufacturer and distributor specializing in sustainable biochar for commercial horticulture, arboriculture, agriculture, and large-scale environmental projects.

name: Poás Bioenergy
tech_note: Biochar
description: Poás Bioenergy designs, fabricates, and implements carbon-negative biomass gasification systems that convert agricultural waste into high-energy syngas and biochar, which regenerates soils and sequesters carbon.

name: Pratt Energy
tech_note: BECCS
description: Pratt Energy is a renewable energy manufacturer that produces ethanol fuel from corn and milo. They are actively seeking permission for a carbon sequestration project in Kansas, indicating a move towards BECCS.

name: Precision Combustion
tech_note: Solid sorbent DAC
description: Precision Combustion is a clean energy technology company that develops and manufactures catalytic reactors and systems, specifically focusing on solid sorbent-based Direct Air Capture (DAC) technology.

name: Premier Forest
tech_note: Pyrolysis of wood-waste feedstock into carbon-dense biochar bricks (>85% carbon) certified under the Puro.earth biochar methodology.
description: Premier Forest Products is a UK timber importer and distributor based in South Wales that also operates a pyrolysis facility converting wood waste into biochar bricks. The biochar project is registered under the Puro.earth biochar methodology and issues CO2 Removal Certificates (CORCs). Biochar is one revenue stream within a larger timber/panel-products business.

name: Preol
tech_note: Operates a PX1500 pyrolysis unit that converts rapeseed chaff (post-harvest agricultural residues) into biochar at its Lovosice facility, with expected annual production of ~715 tons of biochar from 2,350 tons of feedstock.
description: PREOL is the largest Czech rapeseed processor (subsidiary of the AGROFERT Group) producing biofuels, rapeseed oil, glycerin, and animal feed, with biochar added as a product line. Their pyrolysis unit for rapeseed chaff was commissioned in November 2024 following a CZK 38 million investment, producing biochar marketed as a soil amendment and long-term carbon storage medium.

name: Preterra
tech_note: Produces biochar from sustainably sourced BC wood waste (sawmill residues, forest-thinning slash) using SPSC pyrolysis retort/kiln technology, for soil amendment and carbon-optimized concrete applications.
description: <cite index="3-3,3-4,3-5">Preterra BioCarbon Solutions, based on Salt Spring Island, BC, identifies proven European biochar technologies and brings them to North America, offering tools to sequester carbon in soils and building materials while improving wildfire resiliency.</cite> <cite index="1-17,1-18,1-19">The company uses BC wood waste (slash from clearcut logging and sawmill residues) as feedstock, focusing on slash from forest-thinning for wildfire resiliency.</cite> They also sell bagged biochar to consumers via Amazon.ca.

name: ProE Bioenergie
tech_note: Produces and distributes biochar (under the Carbio® brand) made via pyrolysis of biomass at ~450°C for soil improvement, animal husbandry, and construction use.
