description: ProE Bioenergie GmbH is a German company founded in 2006, based in Auenwald, that produces and sells biochar products (marketed as Carbio®) and offers consulting services around biochar, pyrolysis, and renewable energy. They supply EBC-certified and non-certified biochar for agricultural, animal, and industrial applications. Scale appears modest and focus is commercial biochar distribution rather than engineered CDR with carbon-credit issuance.

name: Prometheus Materials
tech_note: Building materials
description: Prometheus Materials creates carbon-negative cement and concrete by harnessing mineralized microalgae combined with natural binders, sequestering and storing CO2 in the material.

name: Pronoe
tech_note: OAE
description: Pronoe is a French Marine CDR company that removes CO2 by increasing ocean alkalinity through an electrically driven process that dissolves crushed limestone into seawater, often connected to desalination plants.

name: Provocative
tech_note: Builds data centers where conventional cooling is replaced by direct air capture units, using waste heat from AI compute to drive sorbent regeneration and deliver carbon-negative compute.
description: <cite index="11-2,11-3">Provocative is a Boston-based Greentown Labs member founded in 2024 (CEO Nick Meyer, President Rob Fisher, Head of Engineering Andrew Bouma) that makes AI carbon-negative by combining data centers and direct air capture, replacing conventional cooling systems with carbon capture.</cite> The company is a DAC supplier integrating removal hardware directly into air-cooled high-performance compute facilities.

name: Pull to Refresh
tech_note: Biochar
description: Pull to Refresh is a BiCRS company that uses a biomass-fueled process to transform shredded garbage into carbon and hydrogen char for long-term soil carbon storage, while also generating energy.

name: Pure Carbon Blue
tech_note: DOR
description: Pure Carbon Blue is a Dutch company that uses Direct Water Capture (DWC) technology to remove carbon from the ocean, aiming to capture 1 gigaton of carbon by 2030.

name: PureField Carbon
tech_note: Captures biogenic CO2 from wheat-starch ethanol fermentation at its Russell, Kansas facility and permanently stores it via a Class VI injection well (bioethanol CCS / BECCS).
description: <cite index="1-3,1-7">PureField Ingredients (operating carbon-capture through its Purefield Carbon Capture LLC subsidiary) received EPA approval in April 2026 to begin permanent geologic sequestration of CO2 from its Russell, Kansas ethanol and wheat-protein operations, and will launch CCS operations following commissioning.</cite> <cite index="10-1">The permit allows injection of up to 1.8 million metric tons of CO2 into deep rock formations in Russell County over a 12-year period.</cite> The company is an integrated wheat-to-ethanol producer, making the fermentation-CO2 sequestration a BECCS CDR pathway.

name: PureField Ingredients
tech_note: Captures biogenic CO2 from wheat-starch ethanol fermentation at its Russell, Kansas plant and permanently stores it underground via a newly permitted EPA Class VI injection well.
description: <cite index="1-7,1-8">PureField Ingredients operates a U.S.-based integrated food ingredient and advanced biofuels platform in Russell, Kansas, producing wheat protein ingredients and low-carbon biofuels from U.S.-grown crops.</cite> <cite index="1-2,1-6">In April 2026, the EPA approved the company's request to begin permanent geologic sequestration of CO2 from the Russell operations, and following final commissioning PureField will begin CCS operations.</cite> <cite index="6-3,6-4">The Class VI well permit allows PureField Carbon Capture LLC to permanently store up to 1.8 million metric tons of CO2 over 12 years at a depth of about 3,500 feet.</cite>

name: Puro
tech_note: Puro.earth is a carbon removal standard and registry that certifies CDR suppliers via third-party verification and issues CO2 Removal Certificates (CORCs) tracked in the Puro Registry.
description: Puro.earth is a Finland-based carbon removal standard and registry (majority-owned by Nasdaq since 2021) that certifies engineered CDR projects such as biochar, BECCS, DAC, and enhanced weathering. They issue and track CO2 Removal Certificates (CORCs) representing verified, durable removals of 100+ years, and operate a supplier marketplace connecting buyers with certified CDR project developers. They do not physically remove CO2 themselves — they are the leading CDR-focused registry and standards body.

name: Pyrocal
tech_note: Pyrocal makes this possible with its high-performing, cost-saving carbonisation technology which converts biosolids and other organic waste from businesses, councils, and utilities into biochar.
description: Pyrocal is an Australian company that designs and installs advanced carbonisation systems to convert biomass and organic waste into biochar, generating carbon removal credits.

name: Pyrogen
tech_note: Pyrogen produces biochar from waste/invasive biomass and infuses it into patented low-carbon concrete mix designs for construction products.
description: Pyrogen is a Kenya-based biochar-concrete carbon removals company founded in 2022 and headquartered in Gilgil. It holds a Kenyan utility model patent for biochar-infused concrete mixes and is developing a commercial pilot plant in Baringo County targeting ~3,000 tonnes CO2/yr of sequestration. It is a listed Puro.earth supplier and has piloted biochar-concrete affordable housing with CGAP (World Bank) and Habitat for Humanity.

name: Pyronam
tech_note: Biochar
description: Pyronam is a Namibian subsidiary of PyroCCS that produces high-quality biochar from invasive bush biomass through pyrolysis to capture carbon, improve soil health, and support local farmers.

name: Q&A: Enhanced rock weathering 101 with Syntopa, a new startup 'flipping the script' on ag biologics
tech_note: Develops microbial biologics and a proprietary Toposight matching platform that accelerate silicate rock dissolution on croplands to boost enhanced rock weathering CO2 removal rates.
description: <cite index="1-4">Syntopa was founded in 2023 by Hans Holtan to develop microbial products at the intersection of crops and climate change, starting with microbes that do enhanced rock weathering.</cite> <cite index="2-21,2-22,2-23">The team operates out of a lab in Alameda, California, has built a collection of over 1,200 rock-weathering soil microbes from soil samples spanning three continents, and uses custom high-throughput strain analysis to quantify each microbe's carbon capture potential.</cite> <cite index="5-8">From their Alameda lab, they enable EW companies worldwide to improve weathering efficiency and carbon capture.

name: Qualterra
tech_note: Qualterra designs and operates Biomass Processing Units (BPUs) that use pyrolysis and gasification to convert agricultural and forestry residues into biochar soil amendment while generating renewable thermal energy.
description: <cite index="6-3,6-4">Qualterra is an agricultural technology company whose Cheney, Washington biochar production facility was listed on the Climate Action Reserve (CAR) registry in April 2025 — only the third biochar project globally to achieve registration under CAR's U.S. Biochar Protocol.</cite> <cite index="3-4">Headquartered in Washington State, Qualterra operates three commercial facilities that serve customers all over the world.</cite> They sell biochar to farmers and manufacture/sell biomass processing units to customers such as Vaagen Timbers, and partner with 3Degrees to deliver verified carbon removal credits.

name: RWE
tech_note: Post-combustion amine CO2 capture retrofitted to biomass-fired (wood pellet) power plants, with CO2 to be transported by pipeline/ship for permanent storage in North Sea offshore depleted gas fields.
description: RWE is a major German energy utility (~46.8 GW generation capacity) whose BECCUS initiative at its Dutch Amer and Eemshaven biomass-co-fired power plants is planned to deliver 11–14 Mt/yr of negative emissions from 2030, subject to technical and economic feasibility. The project is still in permitting/development with no final investment decision announced, and RWE's broader 2025–2030 capex plan has been reduced by €10B. CDR is a small part of RWE's overall business, but they would be the physical operator of the BECCS plants.

name: Rainbow Bee Eater
tech_note: Designs and builds modular ECHO2 pyrolysis systems that convert agricultural/wood residues into biochar, syngas, and wood vinegar, generating Puro.earth CORCs.
description: <cite index="1-1">Rainbow Bee Eater's ECHO2 is a modular automated carbon-negative system for transforming low-value biomass residues into energy, biochar, wood vinegar, horticultural CO2 and carbon drawdown certificates.</cite> <cite index="2-10,2-11">They were the first company outside Europe to produce and sell Puro.earth certified CORCs, generating roughly 1 CORC per tonne of feedstock.</cite> <cite index="7-1,7-9">RBE installed a Mark 4 ECHO2 system at Holla-Fresh in June 2024 and is installing six Mark 4 modules at Katunga Fresh in Victoria.</cite>

name: Rainforest Builder
tech_note: Fully integrated tropical forest restoration developer planting native species across degraded land in West Africa (Sierra Leone, Ghana, Guinea) to generate Verra VM0047/CCB carbon removal credits.
description: Rainforest Builder is a UK-headquartered tropical reforestation company founded in 2022, operating in Sierra Leone, Ghana and Guinea with four active projects targeting 370,000+ hectares of restoration. In February 2026 it signed a 15-year, 1.8M-credit offtake with Microsoft from Project Buffalo (Sierra Leone), and in March 2026 closed a Series A led by BNP Paribas AM Alts with parallel project financing for Project Colobus in Ghana. The company owns the full restoration stack — nurseries, planting operations, MRV (Chameleon data platform), and carbon project development.

name: Re-Vi
tech_note: Re-Vi operates a large-scale pyrolysis biochar facility on Kangaroo Island, converting fire-damaged forestry biomass into agricultural-grade biochar and issuing Puro.earth CORC carbon removal credits.
description: Re-Vi is an Australian CDR developer building one of the world's largest biochar projects, on Kangaroo Island, South Australia. The project converts 4.5 million tonnes of bushfire-damaged timber plantations into biochar and durable CDR credits, with full production targeted for 2026 at ~200,000 tCO2/yr. It is listed as a supplier on Puro.earth.

name: ReCarber
tech_note: BECCS project developer and commercialization platform that partners with Nordic biomass CHP/district-heating operators to build carbon capture and permanent geological storage, issuing carbon removal credits from biogenic CO2.
description: ReCarber is a Swedish startup (founded 2024, based in Stockholm) that commercially develops, finances, and brings to market BECCS/bio-CCS projects in the Nordics, partnering with biomass-fired heat and power operators like Skellefteå Kraft. The company raised SEK 60M (~$5.3M) seed in February 2025 from Luminar Ventures, Spintop Ventures, and Course Corrected, and operates a digital platform that matches CDR suppliers with buyers and orchestrates project financing.

name: ReGenEarth
tech_note: Biochar
description: ReGenEarth produces biochar through a clean, efficient process to improve soil fertility, boost water retention, and promote plant growth while sequestering carbon. They are actively scaling biochar carbon removal technology across the UK.

name: ReGenerate Livermore Falls
tech_note: Biochar
description: ReGenerate Livermore Falls is a biomass energy facility that produces electricity and is certified by Puro.earth for biochar carbon removal.

name: Reclimate
tech_note: Reclimate designs and deploys biochar projects in Southeast Asia and the Global South, converting agricultural waste (paddy straw, bamboo, coconut husk, woody biomass) into biochar via pit/kiln pyrolysis, with a proprietary digital MRV platform for carbon credit issuance.
description: Reclimate is a Malaysia- and Singapore-based biochar project developer that partners with farmers and agricultural operators across Asia to convert agricultural waste into biochar, which is returned to soil and sold as carbon removal credits. The company operates projects in Malaysia (rice straw in Kedah, bamboo with Orang Asli communities via SEAD Bamboo, lemon myrtle waste) and Sri Lanka (coconut mill), and holds European Biochar Certificate / World Biochar Certificate (Carbon Standards International).

name: Recoal
tech_note: Recoal uses hydrothermal carbonization (HTC) to convert wet-waste biomass into hydrochar/carbonisate, which is then permanently stored in underground geological formations in Switzerland.
description: Recoal AG is a Zurich-based CDR startup founded in 2023 that converts moist organic waste biomass into a stable carbon-rich solid (hydrochar) via hydrothermal carbonization, then stores it underground for durable CO2 removal. The company is backed by the Migros Pioneer Fund and was validated under the Rainbow Standard (formerly Riverse) carbon registry in 2025.

name: RecyCoal
tech_note: Biochar
description: RecyCoal is a German-financed company that produces biochar from unused crop waste or other biomass. This biochar is used for soil improvement, as an alternative fuel, and for carbon removal.

name: Red Mountain Biochar
tech_note: Biochar
description: Red Mountain Biochar transforms biomass residuals, such as sawdust and wood chips, into valuable biochar, biocoal, and carbon black through pyrolysis, driving sustainability and innovation in industries like concrete, steel, and agriculture.

name: RedoxNRG
tech_note: 🔍🔋💡 📍 sTartup Days Festival 🗓️ March 16-17 👋 See you there! #RedoxNRG #sTartupDaysFestival #sustainability #innovation #technology #DirectAirCapture #CarbonDioxideRemoval #CO2Valorization ... We&#x...
description: RedoxNRG is a Swiss company that develops electrochemical direct air capture (DAC) technology, utilizing renewable energy to capture CO2 from the atmosphere and convert it into carbon-neutral fuels and chemicals.

name: Reforestaction
tech_note: Reforestation and agroforestry project developer restoring forest ecosystems at scale and issuing certified carbon credits from those projects.
description: Reforest'Action is a French B-Corp certified reforestation project developer founded in 2010 and headquartered in Rueil-Malmaison. It designs, develops and monitors large-scale afforestation, reforestation and agroforestry projects across 45+ countries, generating VCS-certified carbon credits, funded by 650+ corporate clients. In 2024 it secured a €20m growth investment from Blisce and Eiffel Essentiel.

name: Regen Agri-Source
tech_note: Produces and distributes high-carbon-content biochar for soil amendment, wastewater treatment, and poultry litter applications.
description: Regen Agri-Source is a small Missouri-based agricultural supplier selling high-grade biochar (82%+ fixed carbon) alongside microbial and enzyme soil-health products under the BLOOMFIELD brand. They market biochar for soil improvement, wastewater treatment, poultry litter, and carbon sequestration, and are listed as a member of the US Biochar Initiative. Operations appear active but modest in scale, primarily serving agricultural customers rather than the compliance/voluntary CDR credit market.

name: Regen Organics
tech_note: Biochar
description: Regen Organics decarbonizes the production of food, feed, and fuel by locally manufacturing regenerative products, including biochar briquettes, organic fertilizer, and insect protein.

name: Regionalwerke AG Baden
tech_note: Biogas upgrading with CO2 capture and liquefaction; early plants sold captured CO2 for industrial use (CCU), while the new Niederwil plant (2026) routes biogenic CO2 to permanent mineral storage.
description: Regionalwerke AG Baden (RWB) is a Swiss municipal utility supplying the Baden region with electricity, water, gas and heat. Through its joint venture CO2 Energie AG (with Recycling Energie AG), it operates a BECCS-style CO2 capture and liquefaction plant at the Nesselnbach biogas-upgrading facility, and is building a third plant in Niederwil (commissioning spring 2026) designed to deliver ~5,000 t/yr of biogenic negative emissions via mineral storage in partnership with Airfix/South Pole. The original Nesselnbach output is sold to Messer Schweiz for industrial reuse (CCU), but the Niederwil expansion extends the operation into true permanent CDR.

name: Releaf Earth
tech_note: Releaf Earth runs an industrial biochar production facility in Iwuru, Cross River State, Nigeria, using its proprietary Kraken pyrolysis system to convert palm kernel shell waste into biochar for soil application and carbon removal.
description: <cite index="7-3,7-4,7-5">Releaf Earth is a Nigerian climate-agritech startup that launched the country's first operational industrial biochar production facility in Iwuru, Cross River State, using palm kernel shells processed through its proprietary Kraken machine to produce biochar that enhances soil and sequesters carbon.</cite> <cite index="8-3,8-4">In early 2026, the company issued Nigeria's first industrial-scale carbon removal credits — an initial tranche of 190 tCO₂e — purchased by global buyers including Salesforce via Milkywire.</cite>

name: Rement
tech_note: Ex-situ CO2 mineralization: reacts CO2 with cement paste from crushed demolition concrete to produce precipitated calcium carbonate (PCC) and recovered aggregates.
description: Rement is a Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT) spin-off based in Germany that develops a CO2-negative concrete upcycling process. The technology processes demolition concrete fines with CO2 to recover sand/aggregates while producing precipitated calcium carbonate (PCC), permanently storing the CO2 in mineral form. The company operates a lab-scale prototype and is building a pilot plant, supported by the EXIST research transfer program and a pre-commercial procurement contract from the Schwedt Startup Challenge.

name: Remova
tech_note: Developing a greenfield BECCS/Bio-CCS facility in Central Alberta that converts forest and mill residuals into renewable energy while permanently storing biogenic CO2 underground.
description: Remova Carbon Systems is a Calgary-based CDR developer building compact, replicable BECCS facilities in Alberta using forestry residuals as feedstock with geological CO2 storage. In March 2026 it partnered with Mangrove Systems for digital MRV and is pursuing Isometric certification for its first facility. The team has a background in oil & gas EPC and energy finance.

name: Removall Carbon
tech_note: Carbon project developer originating and financing nature-based carbon sink projects including mangrove restoration and reforestation.
description: Removall Carbon is a France-based carbon project developer that designs, operates, and invests in nature-based carbon projects (including mangrove restoration and reforestation), with a joint venture "Summit Removall" launched with Sumitomo Corporation to scale its portfolio. The company also helps corporates finance high-integrity carbon credits. Portfolio includes both removal (restoration) and avoidance/reduction projects.

name: Removr
tech_note: Solid sorbent DAC
description: Removr is a Norwegian Direct Air Capture (DAC) company that develops large-scale solid sorbent DAC plants, specifically utilizing zeolite adsorbents, to remove CO2 from the atmosphere.

name: Renergi
tech_note: Patented "grinding pyrolysis" technology that simultaneously grinds and pyrolyses biomass/MSW feedstocks to produce biochar, bio-oil and wood vinegar.
description: Renergi is an Australian waste-to-energy and carbon removal company based in Collie, Western Australia, spun out of Curtin University in 2012. It operates a patented "grinding pyrolysis" demonstration plant that converts municipal solid waste, forestry and agricultural residues into biochar, bio-oil and wood vinegar, with the biochar sold as a soil conditioner and used for permanent carbon sequestration.

name: Renewables Plus
tech_note: Malaysia-based gasification specialist and EPC contractor providing the Blue Flame™ downdraft biomass gasification system, which produces biochar as a byproduct used for permanent carbon sequestration.
description: <cite index="10-1,10-2,10-3,10-4,10-5,10-6">Renewables Plus Sdn. Bhd. (R+) is a gasification specialist system provider and EPC contractor, incorporated in April 2004 in Malaysia, with completed projects in 6 countries.</cite> <cite index="1-4,1-5">Their gasification technology powers Malaysia's first industrial biochar facility (Bukit Selar Carbon Station, operated by Carbon Plus), using bamboo and palm kernel shell feedstocks</cite>, generating Puro.earth CORCs. They also market a Biofix biochar product alongside the Blue Flame™ gasifier.

name: RepAir
tech_note: Electrochemical dual-cell DAC system using a selective membrane and electrical current (no heat, no water added) to separate CO2 from ambient air at ~600 kWh/tCO2.
description: <cite index="6-9,6-10,6-11">RepAir Carbon Capture is an Israeli direct air capture company developing an electrochemical device inspired by batteries and fuel cells that uses electricity and a selective membrane to separate CO2 from the atmosphere.</cite> <cite index="6-12">The company raised a $10M Series A led by Extantia Capital, with participation from Equinor Ventures, Shell Ventures, and Zero Carbon Capital.</cite> <cite index="3-18,3-19,3-20">They received a Frontier purchase for 199 tons of CO2 removal in 2022</cite> and <cite index="9-3,9-4">unveiled a field prototype in November 2023, achieving TRL 6.</cite>

name: Repsol Sinopec
tech_note: Repsol Sinopec Brasil operates the DAC.SI project, a DAC pilot plant in Porto Alegre (15 tCO2/yr operational since April 2024 and a 300 tCO2/yr unit commissioned in late 2024) in partnership with PUCRS and German DAC developer DACMA, with research into storage in Brazilian basalt for mineralization.
description: Repsol Sinopec Brasil is a joint venture (Repsol 60% / Sinopec 40%) oil & gas operator in Brazil that has established a CDR technology division developing Latin America's first Direct Air Capture pilot plants. Through the DAC.SI initiative, it partners with PUCRS University and German startup DACMA to test adsorbent-based DAC systems with planned CO2 mineralization in basalt. The CDR program is a sub-unit of a much larger fossil-fuel parent, so it is classified as a division/supplier for our directory.

name: Residual Carbon
tech_note: Project developer that designs and structures industrial biomass CDR projects (biochar, BECCS) end-to-end including MRV, registry, ratings, and offtake commercialization.
description: Residual (residualcarbon.com) is a UK-based carbon project developer founded in 2024 by ex-Oka and ex-BeZero executives. It partners with industrial biomass asset owners to design, structure, document, and commercialize biochar and BECCS carbon removal projects, handling methodology, MRV, ratings, insurance preparation, and buyer matchmaking — but does not itself operate removal technology.

name: Restoration Bioproducts
tech_note: Operates pyrolysis facilities that convert waste wood and purpose-grown biomass into biochar, bio-oil, syngas, and thermal energy, with carbon removal credits issued via Puro.earth and marketed through Carbon Streaming.
description: Restoration Bioproducts is a Virginia-based biochar producer developing pyrolysis-based projects that refine low-value biomass and forestry waste into biochar, bio-oil, and power. Its flagship ~$10M Waverly, VA facility opened in October 2024 and is expected to generate ~10,000 tCO2e/year of removal credits, with Microsoft having pre-purchased credits via Carbon Streaming Corporation.

name: Restoration Fuels
tech_note: Thermal processing/pyrolysis facility that produced biochar from sawmill wood waste, with Puro.earth-registered carbon removal credits, after pivoting from torrefied wood pellets in 2021.
description: Restoration Fuels was a biochar production facility in John Day, Oregon, operated as a subsidiary of the U.S. Endowment for Forestry and Communities. The plant shut down on July 15, 2024, laying off 11 employees, after establishing proof-of-concept but failing to attract private investors to take it over. It is defunct.

name: Restord
tech_note: Biochar
description: Restord is a UK-based company in Cornwall that produces biochar through pyrolysis, transforming local waste into biochar to remove CO2 from the atmosphere and improve soil quality.

name: Retort Biofuels
tech_note: Produces biochar and wood vinegar (pyroligneous acid) via controlled pyrolysis of wood waste, sold primarily as an agricultural input in India.
description: Retort Biofuels is a small India-based (Jaipur/Nagpur) biochar producer that pyrolyzes wood waste to manufacture biochar and wood vinegar for sustainable agriculture applications (soil amendment, pest control). The company markets through IndiaMart and LinkedIn, positioning itself as a renewable-fuels and agri-input supplier rather than a dedicated carbon-removal credit issuer. No registry listings or CDR credit sales were identified.

name: Retract
tech_note: Retract is a small U.S. startup focused on developing, constructing, and operating direct air capture (DAC) facilities to remove CO2 from the atmosphere.
description: Retract is a Boulder, Colorado-based company positioning itself as a U.S. developer, constructor, and operator of direct air capture facilities. The company is very small (2-10 employees, ~87 LinkedIn followers) with a minimal website and no recent public news, press, funding announcements, or project milestones.

name: Return Carbon
tech_note: Return Carbon is a Dutch project development and investment company that integrates DAC technology, CO2 transport, and permanent subsurface storage into deliverable DACCS/BECCS projects in Europe and the US.
description: <cite index="1-1,1-2">Return Carbon deploys integrated solutions for DACCS and BECCS developments, aiming at IPCC carbon dioxide removal goals.</cite> The company partners with technology owners such as Skytree and Carbon8, storage investors such as CapeOmega, and emitters such as RWE to develop carbon removal projects — including the NoordKaap CCS project servicing RWE's Eemshaven BECCS plant and, as of November 2025, the Trinity Campus DAC testbed in the Permian Basin with PEDL.

name: Revalue
tech_note: Revalue’s new system, called Model R, implements various sophisticated components to ensure integrity and carbon measurement accuracy in avoided deforestation activities. Following a standard indep...
description: Revalue is a UK-based platform that designs and monitors nature credits, aiming to improve the quality of carbon credits by assessing project pipelines and continuously monitoring projects.

name: Reverion
tech_note: Reversible solid oxide fuel cell power plants that convert biogas to electricity at ~74-80% efficiency while producing a pure biogenic CO2 stream for permanent geological storage.
description: Reverion is a German BECCS company (2022 TUM spin-off) that builds solid oxide fuel cell power plants converting biogas into clean electricity while capturing and permanently storing biogenic CO2. In November 2025 it signed a $41M offtake with Frontier for 96,000 tons of permanent CO2 removal between 2027-2030, following a $62M Series A in 2024.

name: Reverse Carbon
tech_note: Produces biochar via pyrolysis of sustainable agri-industrial biomass residues in developing countries (Kenya), then permanently sequesters biochar in deep repositories and degraded-land restoration sites, selling BCR carbon credits.
description: Reverse Carbon is a Stockholm-based CDR startup founded in 2020 by Jenny Fellenius and Kenneth Möllersten, with a project team in Nairobi, Kenya. It combines large-scale biochar production from agri-industrial residues with permanent sequestration in disused mining sites and ecological restoration projects, issuing biochar carbon removal credits.

name: Reverse Coal
tech_note: Grows short-rotation coppice willow on rewetted lowland peat, pyrolyses the biomass to produce biochar, and buries the biochar in concentrated underground deposits for permanent carbon sequestration.
description: Reverse Coal is a UK biochar CDR project led by Lapwing Energy at The Lapwing Estate in Nottinghamshire/South Yorkshire. It combines peatland rewetting, paludiculture (willow SRC), pyrolysis, and biochar burial, with heat/power output feeding controlled environment agriculture. The project received £3–5M from the UK government's DAC & GGR Innovation Competition and completed its Phase 2 pilot in 2025.

name: Rewind
tech_note: Rewind stores surplus agricultural and forestry biomass in anoxic (oxygen-free) environments — originally the Black Sea seabed and now primarily deep underground mines — to preserve plant carbon on geological timescales.
description: Rewind is an Israeli biomass carbon removal and storage (BiCRS) company that sequesters surplus plant residue in anoxic environments such as deep mines and marine basins. In October 2025 it launched DMS Georgia, billed as the world's first commercial deep mine carbon storage project, 1.3 km underground in western Georgia, with over 400 tCO2e already stored and first certified credits expected in early 2026. The company targets 1 MtCO2/yr of removals by 2030 and is certified via Isometric and Puro.earth with a BlueLayer-based dMRV system.

name: Ricardo
tech_note: Biochar
description: Ricardo develops and implements an integrated energy system called BIOCCUS that uses pyrolysis to convert sustainably sourced biomass (like waste wood or grass cuttings) into biochar for permanent carbon removal, alongside generating heat and power.

name: Riziki Nature Based Solutions
tech_note: Biochar
description: Riziki Nature Based Solutions (nbs-ea.com) produces biofuel from renewable biomass sources, offering a cleaner, high-energy solution for industrial processes. While the company name suggests nature-based solutions, the website focuses on biofuel production rather than direct carbon dioxide removal via biochar.

name: Robinson Lumber
tech_note: Pyrolysis of waste wood from lumber operations to produce biochar for carbon credit sales on the voluntary market.
description: Robinson Lumber Company is a 132-year-old, fifth-generation family-owned wholesale wood products business headquartered in New Orleans, with roughly 75-100 employees and customers in 70+ countries. In 2025 the company launched a biochar initiative that converts waste wood from its lumber operations into biochar with the intent to sell carbon credits on the voluntary market. The biochar effort is an emerging side program within a larger hardwood/softwood wholesaling and manufacturing business.

name: Rock Flour Company
tech_note: Harvests ultra-fine Greenlandic glacial rock flour (naturally pre-crushed silicate) and applies it to croplands in warmer climates to fertilize soils and sequester CO2 via enhanced rock weathering.
description: <cite index="4-12,4-13,4-14">Founded in 2023 by Greenland-native geologist Minik Rosing and climate investor 2degrees, Rock Flour Company is a Danish mining and climate innovation company that ships nutrient-rich Greenlandic glacial rock flour to warmer climates, where it fertilizes crops and converts atmospheric CO2 into stable bicarbonate via enhanced rock weathering.</cite> <cite index="6-1">In September 2025 the company raised approximately €6.1 million ($7.1 million) to scale its ERW-based CDR solution.</cite>

name: Rockburst Technologies
tech_note: Industrial mineralization
description: Rockburst Technologies utilizes proprietary CoreBurst™ technology, which employs CO₂ to pulverize rocks from within, offering an energy-efficient alternative to traditional crushing methods. This technology aims to reduce energy use in mineral extraction and create virtuous GHG emission reduction loops by using CO2 flue gas from industrial processes.

name: RubisCO2
tech_note: Pyrolyzes Sargassum seaweed collected from Caribbean/Mexican coastlines into biochar, which they aim to incorporate into construction materials.
description: <cite index="13-1,13-2">RubisCO2 is an early-stage startup founded by Pablo Navarro Maldonado, who paused his studies to focus on the company, which leverages algae blooms caused by climate change to decarbonize construction.</cite> <cite index="1-8,1-9,1-10,1-11">The team developed prototype pyrolysis reactors in Mexico, upscaled via sponsorships and grants, and planned to transport a larger self-sustaining pyrolysis system to the Caribbean for Sargassum testing.</cite> <cite index="13-5">The company is a small team of about three based in Guadalajara, Mexico, with additional German engineers.</cite>

name: RubiscoBlack
tech_note: Developing microbial technologies to accelerate olivine dissolution and reduce passivation layer formation for enhanced rock weathering CDR.
description: RubiscoBlack Environmental Technologies and Services Pvt Ltd is an India-based early-stage startup (based in Hyderabad and Chennai) developing microbial approaches to overcome two key bottlenecks of olivine-based Enhanced Rock Weathering: rock powder wastage and passivation layer formation on mineral grain surfaces. The company positions itself as a CDR technology developer aiming to increase ERW efficiency on agricultural fields.

name: Running Tide
tech_note: Ocean-based CDR startup that sank limestone-coated wood chip buoys seeded with kelp spores into the deep North Atlantic to sequester carbon via biomass sinking, macroalgae growth, and ocean alkalinity enhancement.
description: Running Tide was a Portland, Maine-based ocean carbon removal startup founded in 2017 that operated out of Iceland and delivered early ocean CDR credits to buyers including Shopify, Stripe, and Microsoft. The company shut down in June 2024, laying off all remaining staff after raising over $50M, citing insufficient voluntary carbon market demand and inability to secure further financing. It is no longer operational.

name: SABIC
tech_note: BECCS
description: SABIC is a Saudi chemical manufacturing company that produces chemicals, plastics, agri-nutrients, and metals. While they are a large chemical company, there is no evidence in the search results that they are involved in BiCRS or BECCS.

name: SAWA
tech_note: Biochar
description: SAWA (also known as Sawa EcoSolutions) transforms agricultural residues into high-quality biochar for CO2 removal and soil enhancement. They have opened their first commercial biochar factory in Majalengka, West Java, Indonesia.

name: SCS
tech_note: Biochar
description: SCS GmbH is a German consultancy specializing in biochar project development. They focus on local biochar production to improve soil and address environmental challenges.

name: SCW Systems
tech_note: SCW Systems operates a supercritical water gasification plant in Alkmaar that converts wet organic waste into green gas/hydrogen with biogenic CO2 capture (BECCS), and is separately piloting a 'CO2 CleanUp' direct air capture process that stores CO2 underground or in mineral products.
description: SCW Systems is a Dutch climate-tech scale-up (founded 2013, ~89 employees) headquartered in Alkmaar that builds and operates the world's first industrial supercritical water gasification facility in partnership with Gasunie, producing green gas from waste while capturing biogenic CO2. It is also developing a parallel Direct Air Capture technology branded CO2 CleanUp that permanently stores CO2 in geological formations or converts it into feedstocks like sustainable cement. The company is backed by Invest-NL and PGGM/PFZW.

name: SIOTUU
tech_note: Biochar
description: SIOTUU Group is an Austrian company that produces high-quality biochar from residual wood biomass, developing customized biochar solutions for CO₂-sequestration.

name: SOLER Group
tech_note: Biochar
description: SOLER Group is a French company that produces biochar from wood residues using pyrolysis technology. Their biochar is used for soil improvement, building materials, and CO2 storage, and they also generate renewable electricity.

name: SPSC
tech_note: Biochar
description: SPSC GmbH is a German technology provider specializing in biochar production. They offer professional retorts and plant systems for converting biomass into biochar, ensuring stable production conditions and high environmental compatibility.

name: SUEZ
tech_note: BECCS
description: SUEZ is a French utility company specializing in water and waste management. They are active in Carbon Dioxide Removal (CDR) through BiCRS methods, specifically Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Storage (BECCS) from waste-to-energy plants and anaerobic digestion, and also produce biochar from forestry residues.

name: SVEC
tech_note: SVEC operates pyrolysis/gasification units that convert woody biomass into syngas for electricity plus biochar for soil amendment and carbon sequestration.
description: <cite index="6-1,6-7">Scotts Valley Energy Company (SVEC) is a business enterprise of the Scotts Valley Band of Pomo Indians developing a bioenergy/biochar production facility on tribal lands in Lake County, California, with a sister enterprise (The Clean Carbon Co.) that processes the biochar into activated charcoal.</cite> <cite index="7-1,7-4">A biochar processing plant in Upper Lake, California, had its permit approved in December 2024; the project led by SVEC with the Habematolel Pomo Tribal Nation will convert forest woodchips into syngas to power generators.</cite> <cite index="9-1,9-4,9-5">The company is listed as a Puro.earth CORC supplier (Red Hills, Biochar 2022) in early development status with an ongoing feasibility study.</cite>

name: SYNAERGY
tech_note: Solid sorbent DAC
description: There is no information in the search results to describe what SYNAERGY does, beyond being a DAC company.

name: Sacurn
tech_note: Biochar
description: Sacurn is a Taiwanese company focused on carbon dioxide removal, likely utilizing biochar as its primary method based on its category and the general search context.

name: Safi Organics
tech_note: Pyrolyzes agricultural residues (primarily rice husks) into biochar that is blended into organic fertilizer applied to farmland.
description: Safi Organics is a Kenyan MIT-spinout that makes biochar-blended organic fertilizer (Safi Sarvi) from rice husks and other crop residues via pyrolysis. The biochar component sequesters carbon in soils while improving fertility for smallholder farmers. The website is live with active product ordering pages and KEBS-certified products distributed across Kenya.

name: Salient DOC
tech_note: Salient DOC is developing electrochemical direct ocean capture (DOC) technology to extract CO2 from seawater for carbon dioxide removal.
description: <cite index="5-1,5-2">Salient Direct Ocean Capture (DOC) is described as pioneering electrochemical technology for scalable, cost-effective carbon dioxide removal (CDR) from seawater, working to scale up technology from concept to pilot to commercial stages.</cite> Public footprint is very limited — no standalone website, no funding announcements, and no press coverage or pilot deployments could be located, with only an advisor's LinkedIn profile referencing the company.

name: SaltX
tech_note: OAE
description: SaltX is a Swedish energy storage firm with project plans for Europe. While primarily an energy storage company, one search result mentions them in the context of Google's DAC initiatives, suggesting a potential connection to CDR, though their specific CDR method (Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement) is not explicitly confirmed in the search results.

name: Sanbra Foods
tech_note: Produces biochar from agricultural residues in Ghana for soil application and durable carbon sequestration, certified under Puro.earth's biochar methodology.
description: Sanbra Foods Ghana is a sustainable agriculture company based in Ghana that is listed on Puro.earth as a prospective biochar carbon removal supplier. The project is in early development stage with feasibility studies ongoing and no CORCs issued to date. The company website is live but minimal, suggesting limited public activity.

name: Scaled Carbon
tech_note: Scaled Carbon pursues Oceanic Enhanced Weathering (OEW) by grinding alkaline rocks into sand, dispersing them in the ocean, and using a novel tracer-based MRV approach to quantify resulting CO2 removal.
description: Scaled Carbon is an early-stage US-based marine CDR developer working on Oceanic Enhanced Weathering, a form of ocean alkalinity enhancement that accelerates the natural weathering carbon cycle. The company is pre-pilot: actively fundraising, developing a tracer-based MRV methodology, and working toward an in-ocean pilot deployment.

name: Scientists Are Trying to Coax the Ocean to Absorb More CO2
Scotia BioChar
tech_note: Produces biochar by pyrolyzing waste wood biomass using BluSky Carbon's Vulcan pyrolysis equipment.
description: Scotia BioChar Inc. is a Nova Scotia-based company aiming to produce biochar from waste wood biomass (including fallen trees from Hurricane Fiona) using pyrolysis technology. In October 2024 they signed a master services agreement with BluSky Carbon to deploy a Vulcan pyrolysis system in Eastern Canada, with biochar intended for mine reclamation, soil amendment, concrete, and water treatment applications.

name: Sea-Up
tech_note: Sea-Up builds wave-powered artificial upwelling pumps (paired with a downwelling ribbon) that bring deep, nutrient-rich water to the sunlit surface to stimulate phytoplankton photosynthesis and ocean carbon sequestration.
description: <cite index="4-1,4-2">Sea-Up (The Sea Upwelling Company Inc, formerly Ocean-Based Climate Solutions) is a US ocean CDR developer that pairs deep (450 m) upwelling with an equal-depth downwelling ribbon using wave energy to achieve carbon removal, sea-surface cooling, and sargassum suppression.</cite> <cite index="15-1,15-2,15-3">The company commercializes fractional "Sea-Shares" of its upwelling pumps rather than tons of CDR, measures ocean pH to confirm photosynthesis in real time, and has announced a first deployment off Bermuda.</cite> <cite index="13-8,13-9,13-10">Their planned deployment east of Bermuda, in partnership with the Bermuda Institute of Ocean Sciences (BIOS), was billed as the first open-ocean upwelling CDR project worldwide.</cite>

name: SeaGen
tech_note: Builds solar-powered autonomous robots (AlgaRay) that intercept invasive Sargassum at the ocean surface and sink it to the deep seabed for long-duration carbon sequestration.
description: <cite index="11-8,11-9,11-10">Seaweed Generation (trading as SeaGen) was founded in 2021, is headquartered in Falmouth, United Kingdom, and has 19 total employees.</cite> The company physically removes CO2 by <cite index="13-7">developing its AlgaRay technology, which intercepts and sinks invasive Sargassum into the deep ocean, before it can reach coasts.</cite> <cite index="19-4">It has a 49-year license for trials in Antigua and Barbuda while it develops an autonomous version of the bot.</cite>

name: SeaO2
tech_note: Electrochemical Direct Ocean Capture: uses electrochemistry and vacuum to shift the carbonate equilibrium in seawater and release gaseous CO2 for geological storage or mineralization.
description: SeaO2 is a Netherlands-based TU Delft spin-off (founded 2021) developing electrochemical Direct Ocean Capture (DOCC) technology that extracts CO2 directly from seawater using renewable electricity. The company is operating a 25 tCO2/year pilot ("Project Swell") at the Afsluitdijk and plans a larger commercial-scale "Project Breaker" for 2028 that will deliver carbon credits.

name: Seafields
tech_note: Biomass sinking
description: Seafields cultivates floating sargassum seaweed in the open ocean, combining seaweed aquaculture with artificial upwelling, and converts unsold pulp into biochar for long-term carbon sequestration.

name: Seqana
tech_note: Carbon removal analytics and intelligence platform.
description: Seqana is a Berlin-based SaaS platform that provides data-driven, remote, and cost-efficient MRV (Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification) tools for soil organic carbon in regenerative agriculture and carbon farming projects, leveraging earth observation and machine learning.

name: Shell
tech_note: In-house solid sorbent DAC technology being demonstrated at Shell Technology Center Houston, plus development of the Pelican DAC Hub in Louisiana integrating multiple third-party DAC technologies with CO2 transport and geological storage.
description: Shell is developing an in-house solid sorbent Direct Air Capture technology, with an industrial-scale demonstration unit at the Shell Technology Center Houston (FID taken in 2023, targeted start-up 2025). In 2025, Shell US Gas and Power and Mitsubishi Corporation (Americas) advanced the Pelican DAC Hub in Louisiana, bringing in technology partners including RepAir (electrochemical) and Origen (limestone-based), and Shell Ventures co-invested $17M with Mitsubishi in Avnos's Project Cedar. Shell's CDR activity is a dedicated division of a larger oil & gas major.

name: Shell, Mitsubishi invest $17M in hybrid direct air capture startup
tech_note: Hybrid Direct Air Capture (HDAC) using a moisture-swing sorbent that captures atmospheric CO2 without thermal input while co-producing clean water.
description: Avnos is a US-based (LA/New Jersey) startup developing Hybrid Direct Air Capture (HDAC) technology that captures CO2 while producing clean water as a byproduct, using a moisture-swing sorbent that eliminates the need for external heat. The company has secured over $100M in funding from Shell, Mitsubishi, NextEra, ConocoPhillips, JetBlue, DOE and the US Navy, and in November 2025 announced Project Cedar, its first commercial-scale facility (3,000 tCO2/yr) coming online in late 2026.

name: Silica
tech_note: ERW
description: No search results directly refer to 'Silica' as a CDR company. The provided search results discuss 'Silicate' (a different company) or the general method of 'silicate weathering' and 'enhanced rock weathering'.

name: Silicate
tech_note: Processes limestone, reactive silicate minerals, and returned concrete into fine dust applied to farmland to accelerate enhanced rock weathering, converting atmospheric CO2 into dissolved bicarbonate for long-term ocean storage.
description: Silicate is an Irish CDR supplier headquartered in Dublin with a U.S. subsidiary in Chicago, running enhanced weathering field trials across Ireland and the U.S. Midwest on 650+ hectares. The company spreads pulverized limestone, silicate minerals, and surplus concrete on farmers' fields to remove CO2 while optimizing soil pH, and sells durable carbon removal credits.

name: Silver Bullet Biochar
tech_note: Biochar producer (pyrolysis of biomass to stable carbon), based in Singapore.
description: Silver Bullet Biochar appears to be a Singapore-based biochar venture with a LinkedIn page but virtually no public footprint — no press, no product pages surfaced in search, and no evidence of deliveries or certifications. The pathway is biochar (pyrolysis of biomass), not BECCS as previously tagged.

name: Sinkco Labs
tech_note: Injects waste terrestrial biomass slurry into anoxic marine sub-sediments using a patent-pending vibration-based micro-injection system to permanently sequester organic carbon.
description: <cite index="4-1,4-8,4-9">Sinkco Labs is developing a scalable solution for permanently storing organic carbon in marine sediments, using a delivery system for micro-injecting organic carbon into marine sediments where anoxic compaction preserves the carbon.</cite> <cite index="2-4,2-6">The company was selected for the Breakthrough Energy Fellows Program, with co-founders Viji Thomas, Victor Choquet, and Brenna Boehman receiving non-dilutive funding to launch a pilot in the Gulf of Mexico.</cite> <cite index="8-4">Sinkco has secured state and federal permits from the Louisiana Department of Natural Resources and the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers to embed waste biomass beneath degraded marsh sediments across 11 acres.</cite>

name: Sirona Technologies
tech_note: Solid sorbent DAC
description: Sirona Technologies is a Belgium-based company that develops modular Direct Air Capture (DAC) systems using solid sorbents to remove CO2 from the atmosphere. They are actively working on projects in Kenya and the Middle East.

name: Sitos Group
tech_note: Slow pyrolysis of California agricultural, municipal and forest biomass (almond shells, vineyard residue, wood) into durable biochar applied as soil amendment with deep injection via sister company SAI.
description: <cite index="3-1,3-6">Sitos Group launched a pilot-scale biochar production facility at ReGen Monterey in early 2023 using slow pyrolysis technology to produce high-quality biochar for agriculture and carbon markets.</cite> <cite index="3-13,3-14">The pilot has concluded and they are now building a commercial biochar production facility in partnership with Treehouse California Almonds.</cite> <cite index="9-1,9-4">They work with sister company Soil Amendment Injection (SAI) to precisely apply biochar at depth for long-term soil health and carbon sequestration.</cite>

name: Sizewell C/EDF Energy
tech_note: DAC project developer
description: Sizewell C/EDF Energy is primarily involved in nuclear energy and sustainable infrastructure projects in the UK. While the company's website mentions DAC funding, the search results do not provide specific details about their DAC method or active operations in this area.

name: Skyology
tech_note: Uses a wave-powered reactor to accelerate weathering of abundant crustal minerals in seawater, producing carbonate/bicarbonate that locks atmospheric CO2 into the ocean while deacidifying surrounding waters.
description: Skyology is a UK-based ocean carbon dioxide removal developer pursuing ocean alkalinity enhancement (OAE) via a renewable-energy, wave-powered reactor that accelerates natural mineral weathering. The company is frequently listed among early OAE players but appears to be very early stage with minimal disclosed funding (~$63K per PitchBook) and limited recent public activity.

name: Skyrenu
tech_note: Solid-sorbent DAC using monolithic amine-functionalized polymer sorbents in a reactor-less moving-cell design, paired with mineralization/geological storage partners.
description: Skyrenu Technologies is a Quebec-based DAC company spun out of the Université de Sherbrooke, winner of the 2021 XPRIZE Carbon Removal student competition. It builds modular solid-sorbent direct air capture systems using a reactor-less, moving-cell architecture, with captured CO2 stored via mineralization in mine tailings, underground sequestration, or green concrete production.

name: Skytree
tech_note: Builds modular solid-sorbent direct air capture machines based on European Space Agency-derived technology for both onsite CO₂ supply and permanent removal.
description: Skytree is a Dutch direct air capture technology company founded in 2014, headquartered in Amsterdam with offices in Toronto and Nashville. It develops modular solid-sorbent DAC machines (Cumulus and Stratus product lines) for both CO₂ utilization (greenhouses, beverages) and permanent carbon removal, including a planned 500,000 tpa DAC park in Texas with EDF Renewables and Return Carbon.

name: Skånefrö
tech_note: Operates pyrolysis facilities (Pyreg-based) that convert agricultural/seed-production residues and organic wastes into EBC-certified biochar used as a soil amendment and carbon sink.
description: <cite index="2-22">Skånefrö is one of Sweden's leading seed companies with one of Europe's most modern seed-cleaning facilities</cite>, and it operates a biochar business line producing EBC-certified biochar from plant-based residues. <cite index="10-7,10-8,10-10">The company operates pyrolysis facilities (using Pyreg kit) that process park/garden waste, seaweed, and wastewater sludge into biochar</cite>, and was <cite index="7-1,7-2">the first Swedish producer to receive the European Biochar Certificate, using residues from seed and grass-seed production</cite>.

name: Slíglas
tech_note: Pyrolysis of woody/forestry residues into stable biochar applied to agricultural soils for carbon sequestration.
description: Slíglas is an Irish biochar startup based in Sligo that transforms residual forestry biomass into biochar for carbon dioxide removal. Founded in 2024 by Paul McGoldrick and Sadhbh McCarrick, the company partners with local farmers to apply biochar to agricultural land.

name: Soil Reef
tech_note: Soil Reef LLC markets and distributes premium wood-based biochar (pyrolyzed forest residue/hardwood, ~82% carbon) as a soil amendment with carbon sequestration co-benefits, sold in bulk and retail channels including Amazon.
description: Soil Reef LLC is a Berwyn, PA-based integrated biochar product development, marketing and sales company founded in 2011 (originally The Biochar Company). It sells Soil Reef-branded pure biochar and biochar-compost blends sourced from sustainably produced U.S. wood waste, targeting home gardeners, commercial agriculture, and industrial/environmental applications.

name: Soletair Power
tech_note: Develops modular solid-sorbent (amine-functionalized) Direct Air Capture units that retrofit into building HVAC systems, using temperature-vacuum-swing adsorption to capture CO2 from ventilation air for downstream storage or utilization.
description: Soletair Power is a Finnish DAC technology supplier (founded 2016) that integrates carbon capture modules into building HVAC systems, turning commercial buildings into distributed CO2 scrubbers. Recent deployments include Wärtsilä's Sustainable Technology Hub (Vaasa), a factory in Vantaa, and Danica Pension's building in Aarhus, Denmark; in December 2024 they partnered with Carbonaide to deliver captured CO2 for net-negative concrete.

name: Solid Carbon
tech_note: Integrates DAC on offshore floating platforms powered by renewables with injection of CO2 into sub-seafloor ocean basalt where it mineralizes into rock.
description: Solid Carbon is a Canadian research initiative led by Ocean Networks Canada (University of Victoria) developing an integrated offshore CDR system combining Direct Air Capture on floating platforms with injection of CO2 into sub-seafloor ocean basalt for permanent mineralization. In 2025 the project was awarded $24M over six years through the Government of Canada's New Frontiers in Research Fund to advance from feasibility study to demonstration. It is a research/demonstration-stage supplier rather than a commercial credit vendor.

name: Solör Bioenergy
tech_note: Operates wood-fuel district heating plants retrofitted with pyrolysis reactors (PyCCS) to co-produce heat and biochar from woodchips/pellets for soil amendment.
description: <cite index="4-1,4-2">Solör Bioenergy Group is a Scandinavian renewable energy company producing district heating, steam and electricity from wood fuels across roughly 300 sites in Sweden and Norway.</cite> <cite index="3-27,3-28">It runs biochar production at district heating plants in Skurup, Svedala, Munka-Ljungby and Herrljunga, which together produced over 2,900 m³ of biochar in 2023.</cite> <cite index="3-11,3-12,3-13">In 2025 it commissioned a new pyrolysis-with-carbon-capture (PyCC) facility at Ulricehamn together with local partners, supplementing its existing Herrljunga plant with biochar production.</cite>

name: Sonnenerde
tech_note: Operates Pyreg-based pyrolysis units (heating biogenic residues to 850 °C with air exclusion) to produce EBC-certified biochar that is sold into soils, livestock and composting markets while generating Puro.earth carbon removal credits.
description: Sonnenerde GmbH is an Austrian biochar producer based in Riedlingsdorf, Burgenland, operating since 2012 what it claims is the first waste-law-approved biochar plant in Europe. The company pyrolyzes agricultural and composting residues into EBC-certified biochar for soils, livestock and Terra Preta products, and issues Puro.earth carbon removal credits. A new ~10x larger pyrolysis facility ("KOHLOSS") opened on April 30, 2025.

name: Sosna Metelyk
tech_note: Concept-stage portable micro DAC pods combining cryogenic passive capture with integrated solar power, plus parallel R&D divisions for Gen-IV nuclear reactors, clean engines, and orbital aircraft.
description: Sosna Metelyk is an early-stage American-Ukrainian multi-division climate hardware startup (founded 2023, based in Cherkasy, Ukraine) developing portable solar-powered DAC pods alongside other technology concepts. The company self-reports TRL 4 R&D phase and is unfunded, positioning itself across CDR, CCUS, nuclear, solar, clean engines, and aerospace.

name: South Ocean Air
tech_note: Develops a passive direct air capture system using plasma-treated cellulose as a sorbent that binds CO2 without fans or active energy input, with captured CO2 intended for concrete storage or industrial reuse.
description: <cite index="14-4,14-5,14-6">South Ocean Air is a Houston, Texas-based Direct Air Capture company that launched on Earth Day (April 22) 2023, using cellulose as the core material for its carbon removal technology.</cite> <cite index="1-10,1-11">The company uses a low-energy plasma treatment to turn plant cellulose into a passive "carbon magnet" that pulls ambient CO2 from the air for permanent storage or reuse.</cite> The company is pre-commercial, targeting a long-term cost of under $20/ton based on techno-economic projections, with no publicly announced deliveries or funding rounds to date.

name: Southern Green Gas
tech_note: Develops solar-powered modular Direct Air Capture units using Metal-Organic Framework (MOF) solid sorbent cartridges, with captured CO2 used for permanent geological storage or conversion into e-fuels (methane, methanol, SAF).
description: Southern Green Gas (SGG) is an Australian DAC technology developer founded in 2018 and based in Southbank, Victoria. They build solar-powered DAC modules using MOF-based solid sorbents, originally partnering with AspiraDAC on a Frontier/Stripe-backed solar DAC project, and now focused on coupling DAC with e-fuel production (methanol, SAF, renewable methane). Activity is real but modest — ~5 employees and CCU-leaning, though permanent storage is still an advertised pathway.

name: Southwest Biochar Products
tech_note: Produces biochar via slow pyrolysis using wood chip feedstock sourced from National Forest thinning projects in eastern Arizona.
description: <cite index="4-1,4-2">Southwest Biochar Products, operating since 2022, scaled up in fall 2024 from a single reactor to a 5-reactor system with capacity to produce over 12,000 yards per year.</cite> <cite index="4-9,4-10,4-11">Feedstock is sourced entirely from National Forest thinning projects, using biomass that would otherwise be burned to reduce wildfire risk.</cite> The company sells biochar as a soil amendment and partners with 3Degrees on carbon credit offtake.

name: Spiritus
tech_note: Solid-sorbent passive-contacting DAC ("Carbon Orchard") with low-temperature desorption, paired with geologic sequestration (DAC+S).
description: Spiritus is a US-based climate-tech company developing low-cost Direct Air Capture using a novel solid sorbent and a passive "Carbon Orchard" contacting system with low-temperature desorption. The company raised a $30M Series A in March 2025 led by Aramco Ventures, and is building a 1,000-ton/year pilot in New Mexico and a 2 Mt/year "Orchard One" DAC+S facility in Wyoming.

name: Sponge DAC
tech_note: N/A DAC tech
description: Sponge DAC is a Direct Air Capture (DAC) company that removes carbon directly from the atmosphere. They are creating jobs and working towards net-zero.

name: Stack Carbon
tech_note: Stack Carbon develops biochar production from agricultural waste via pyrolysis and applies finely crushed basalt to farmlands for enhanced rock weathering in Uganda.
description: Stack Carbon Investments UG Ltd is a Uganda-based CDR supplier developing the Nile Char Carbon Removal Project, a $12M biochar facility in partnership with China's Jiaxing Tongao Environmental Technology and Norway's TerraCapX AS. The company also operates Enhanced Rock Weathering using basalt on Ugandan farmlands, with commercial biochar operations planned to begin in Q3 2026.

name: Standard Biocarbon
tech_note: Operates a Pyreg-based pyrolysis facility in Enfield, Maine that converts spruce/fir sawmill residuals from Pleasant River Lumber into high-carbon biochar for soil, remediation (PFAS), and industrial applications.
description: Standard Biocarbon is a Maine-based biochar manufacturer that pyrolyzes softwood sawmill residuals using Pyreg technology, producing roughly 50-60 cubic yards per day of engineered biochar. The company sells bulk biochar to composters, soil blenders, landscapers, and agricultural users, and also supplies material for PFAS remediation research with Northern Tilth, Purdue, and the University of Maine.

name: Standard Gas/Carbon Char Store
tech_note: Uses the SG100 "Advanced Thermal Cracking" process (pyrolysis + high-temperature gas cracking) to convert non-recyclable waste into syngas and biogenic carbon char (~90-95% carbon), which is sequestered in concrete/asphalt or soil applications.
description: Standard Gas Technologies is a UK company whose SG100 pyrolysis technology processes non-recyclable waste into clean syngas and carbon-removing biochar. Its Carbon Char Store subsidiary markets and sells the resulting durable carbon removals (char bound into construction materials such as concrete and asphalt). The first commercial SG100 plant is under construction at Scottow Enterprise Park in Norfolk, UK.

name: State Key Laboratory of Chemical Engineering
Stathmos
tech_note: Solid-sorbent Direct Air Capture via modular "Statbox" units that also co-produce water from atmospheric humidity.
description: <cite index="7-1,7-4">Stathmos is a French startup using Direct Air Capture (DAC) to address both CO2 removal and water scarcity, with Statbox systems designed to capture up to 1,000 tonnes of CO2 annually while producing clean water in arid regions.</cite> <cite index="8-5,8-6">The company was founded in 2023 from Marble Studio by Amandine Cadiau and uses solid alkaline carbonate sorbents</cite> at its headquarters in Le Mans, France.

name: Stiesdal
tech_note: Stiesdal SkyClean builds fully automated slow-pyrolysis plants that convert agricultural/forestry residues into biochar plus bio-oil and syngas, with the biochar applied to soils for durable carbon removal.
description: SkyClean is the biochar/pyrolysis division of Danish cleantech group Stiesdal (founded by wind pioneer Henrik Stiesdal). It develops and commercializes 20 MW turnkey pyrolysis plants; a commercial-scale plant in Vraa, Denmark was inaugurated in October 2024. The broader Stiesdal group also works on offshore wind, electrolyzers and energy storage, but SkyClean is a dedicated CDR supplier.

name: Stockholm Exergi
tech_note: Stockholm Exergi is building a large-scale BECCS facility at its biomass-fired CHP plant in Värtan, Stockholm, capturing biogenic CO2 for liquefaction and permanent geological storage via Northern Lights offshore Norway.
description: Stockholm Exergi is a Swedish municipal energy utility (owned by the City of Stockholm and a European pension-fund consortium Ankhiale) constructing one of the world's largest BECCS facilities at its Värtaverket KVV8 biomass CHP plant. The project reached FID in 2025, is under construction with Saipem as EPC contractor, targets 2028 operations at up to 800,000 tCO2/yr, and has secured EU Innovation Fund grants, Swedish state aid, and major offtakes including an expanded deal with Microsoft for 5.08 Mt.

name: Storegga/Pale Blue Dot Energy
tech_note: UK decarbonisation developer of carbon capture, hydrogen and geological CO2 storage projects, including a proposed large-scale DAC facility in NE Scotland with Carbon Engineering and the Acorn CCS project.
description: Storegga (which acquired Pale Blue Dot Energy) is a UK-based independent decarbonisation developer building carbon capture, hydrogen and permanent CO2 storage infrastructure. It partnered with Carbon Engineering on a planned 0.5–1 Mt/yr DAC facility in Scotland, though the DAC project is reported as stalled and Storegga announced in late 2025 it would sell its stake in the flagship Acorn CCS project.

name: Strategic Biofuels
tech_note: Developing a 100MW biomass-fired power plant in Caldwell Parish, Louisiana, that combines bioenergy with carbon capture and geologic sequestration (BECCS) to produce carbon-negative electricity and, in Phase 2, sustainable aviation fuel, using forestry residues as feedstock and Class VI wells for permanent CO2 storage.
description: Strategic Biofuels is a US project developer advancing the Louisiana Green Fuels (LGF) project, a BECCS facility that will burn regional forestry waste to generate 75 MW of dispatchable electricity while capturing and sequestering roughly one million tonnes of CO2 per year in deep saline formations. The project recently received a draft Class VI well permit and has a partnership with Carbon Direct to supply durable carbon removal credits to Carbon Direct's clients.

name: Submarine Scientific
tech_note: Ocean CDR research company developing marine carbon dioxide removal approaches.
description: Submarine Scientific is a scientific consulting company focused on ocean modeling, expert verification support, and system-wide strategy development for ocean-based Carbon Dioxide Removal (CDR) applications, specifically Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement (OAE).

name: Subtidal
tech_note: Digital MRV for marine CDR
description: Subtidal is a marine CDR company developing a scalable solution for directly measuring ocean carbon dioxide removals.

name: SunCarbon
tech_note: Produces biochar from agricultural residues (e.g. coconut husk/shell) via controlled pyrolysis at owned sites in India, selling it as a soil enhancer while generating carbon removal credits.
description: <cite index="1-2">SunCarbon, a brand of Teo Ventures, markets itself as India's first biochar-based soil enhancer</cite>, producing biochar from natural biomass for agricultural soil applications. <cite index="4-6,4-7">The company joined Cohort 2 of the Remove India CDR Accelerator Program with a mission to make, monitor, and monetise biochar for carbon removal</cite>, and also operates a SunCarbon Saarthi platform that registers projects, trains farmers, and connects them with carbon markets.

name: Super Biochar
tech_note: Biochar
description: Super Biochar is a BiCRS company that produces carbon-rich biochar, which it pairs with organic amendments and diagnostics-driven application to improve soil fertility, reduce contaminant mobility, and restore soil biology.

name: Super6 Carbon
tech_note: Aggregates biogenic CO2 from concentrated capture sites via transload hubs and sequesters it permanently in Class VI wells (e.g., ADM's Mt. Simon sandstone formation in Decatur, IL).
description: Super6 Carbon is a U.S.-based engineered CDR project developer that aggregates biogenic/concentrated CO2 from multiple capture sites at transload hubs and delivers it for permanent geological storage. In October 2025 it signed an MOU with ADM to produce CDR credits at ADM's Class VI CCS facility in Decatur, Illinois, with ADM taking a minority stake once definitive agreements are finalized. First carbon is expected in 2027 with megatonne-scale targets by 2030.

name: Supercritical
tech_note: Carbon removal marketplace connecting businesses with high-quality permanent CDR projects.
description: Supercritical is a carbon removal marketplace and software platform that helps businesses measure, reduce, and offset their climate impact. They facilitate the procurement of high-quality, vetted carbon removal credits from projects including biochar, direct air capture (DAC), enhanced weathering, and bio-oil sequestration.

name: Sustaera
tech_note: Develops a solid-sorbent Direct Air Capture system using nano-structured alkali-based sorbents with integrated electric resistive heating, powered by renewable electricity.
description: <cite index="16-12,16-13">Founded in 2021 and headquartered in Cary, North Carolina, Sustaera's technology captures CO2 directly from the atmosphere using renewable energy, designed for scalability and cost-effectiveness.</cite> The company is backed by Breakthrough Energy Ventures and the Grantham Foundation, and <cite index="15-8">its technology was selected for the Ankeron Hub, a Department of Energy (DOE)-backed initiative designed to validate technologies at a readiness level of 4-6.</cite> <cite index="17-18,17-19">Sustaera is also changing how its technology reaches the market by offering a technology licensing model, which reduces risk for carbon removal project developers.</cite>

name: Sustainable Green Team
tech_note: SGTM operates pyrolysis/gasification equipment (e.g. the Gasifier Forge) converting organic waste (yard waste, tree trimmings, storm debris) into biochar-based regenerative soils and carbon removal credits, paired with a blockchain-based MRV platform called Restore.Earth.
description: Sustainable Green Team, Ltd. (OTC: SGTM) is a Florida-based publicly-traded company that converts organic waste into biochar, regenerative soils, and carbon removal credits. The company is repositioning around its Restore.Earth "Physical Truth Infrastructure" verification platform while continuing biochar production via its patented pyrolysis technology stack.

name: Svante Technologies
tech_note: Svante manufactures solid-sorbent (metal-organic framework/CALF-20) structured filters and rotary adsorption machines used in both point-source carbon capture and direct air capture, including supplying filters to Climeworks' Gen 3 DAC and co-developing BECCS projects.
description: <cite index="7-4,7-5">Svante Technologies is a Vancouver, BC-based carbon capture and removal technology company that in May 2025 commissioned the "Redwood" facility, the world's first gigafactory dedicated to producing commercial-scale carbon capture and removal filters designed to trap CO2 from industrial emissions and the atmosphere.</cite> <cite index="7-18">Svante also manufactures filters for Climeworks' Gen 3 direct air capture technology</cite>, and <cite index="5-3">has advanced a joint BECCS project with Mercer International at Mercer's Peace River pulp mill in Alberta targeting biogenic CO₂ from sustainably sourced biomass.</cite>

name: Svante/Carbon Alpha
tech_note: Svante manufactures nanoengineered solid-sorbent (MOF/CALF-20) filters and modular rotary contactor machines for post-combustion and DAC applications, and via its Carbon Alpha acquisition develops/operates integrated BECCS projects with geological storage.
description: <cite index="2-15,2-16">Svante is a carbon capture and removal solutions provider that makes nanoengineered filters and modular rotating contactor machines that capture and remove CO2 from industrial emissions and the air.</cite> <cite index="5-3,5-4">In March 2026 Svante acquired Calgary-based Carbon Alpha Corporation, including its ownership interests in North Star Carbon Solutions and its flagship North Star BECCS project</cite> in Meadow Lake, Saskatchewan. <cite index="20-9">In April 2026 North Star Carbon Solutions LP signed an offtake agreement with Microsoft to deliver 626,000 tonnes of durable CDR credits over 15 years from the North Star BECCS project.</cite>

name: Swiss Biochar
tech_note: Produces EBC-certified biochar via pyrolysis and biochar-based soil substrates for agriculture and urban greening, with the biochar storing carbon long-term.
description: Swiss Biochar, based in Belmont-sur-Lausanne, is Europe's first EBC-certified biochar producer, operating since 2010. It has been part of the Novocarbo Group since 2021, and manufactures pure biochar plus activated soil substrates for agriculture, viticulture, and urban green spaces, also offering carbon reduction certificates.

name: Sylva Fertilis
tech_note: Pyrolysis of wood pellets from sustainably-managed French forests to produce biochar for soil amendment and carbon sequestration.
description: Sylva Fertilis is a French biochar manufacturer based in Argentan, Normandy, part of the SLB Group forestry consortium. They produce biochar via pyrolysis of sustainably-sourced wood pellets, selling products under the Terra Fertilis brand for agriculture, viticulture, municipalities, and golf courses. They are Puro.earth certified and in 2024 consolidated biochar activities under Sylva Fertilis International.

name: Sylvera
tech_note: Sylvera provides independent ratings, market intelligence, pre-issuance assessments, and geospatial MRV data for carbon credits (including CDR projects like biochar, DAC, BECCS).
description: UK-based carbon credit ratings agency that uses satellite data, machine learning and field measurements to independently assess the quality of carbon projects on a AAA-D scale. Sylvera serves corporates, investors, developers and governments with ratings, market intelligence and pre-issuance risk assessments across voluntary and compliance-adjacent markets. They are an ecosystem player (ratings/data provider), not a CO2-removal supplier.

name: Syncraft
tech_note: Builds patented floating fixed-bed biomass gasification power plants that co-produce electricity, heat, and biochar from forest residues for permanent carbon storage.
description: Syncraft is an Austrian technology firm (founded 2009, based in Schwaz, Tyrol) that builds "Reversepowerplants" — biomass gasification plants using a patented floating fixed-bed gasifier to convert forest residues into renewable electricity, heat, and biochar ("Green Carbon"). More than 40 plants have been built across Europe and Japan, and the company is actively expanding with new installations (e.g., Gänserndorf 2024, Stanglwirt 2025, Zwickau 2025, Bruck an der Leitha 2026). The biochar permanently stores roughly 30% of the feedstock CO2, qualifying their systems as Biochar Carbon Removal (BCR).

name: Syntopa
tech_note: Develops microbial inoculants that accelerate silicate rock dissolution in agricultural soils, boosting CO2 capture rates of enhanced rock weathering deployments.
description: Syntopa is a US startup (founded 2023, based in Alameda, California) developing living microbial products that accelerate enhanced rock weathering (ERW) on croplands. They match microbial strains to specific soils using their proprietary Toposight platform, aiming to boost silicate dissolution rates and thereby durable CO2 removal. They sell to EW operators as a performance enhancer and have raised pre-seed funding from Ponderosa Ventures and Carbon Drawdown Initiative.

name: Söderenergi
tech_note: Söderenergi planned to capture, liquefy, and geologically store up to 500,000 tonnes/year of biogenic CO2 from its Igelsta biomass-fired CHP plant in Södertälje, with shipping via its Baltic port.
description: Söderenergi is a Swedish municipal energy utility (owned by Södertälje, Huddinge, and Botkyrka) that was developing a BECCS project at its Igelsta CHP plant. In August 2025 it signed an offtake deal with AstraZeneca, but in February 2026 the Board paused the BECCS project citing excessive risk exposure, insufficient financing, and a slow Nordic voluntary carbon market.

name: Südwestdeutsche Salzwerke
tech_note: Biochar
description: Südwestdeutsche Salzwerke AG is a German company primarily engaged in the production of rock salt and boiled salt for various applications. There is no evidence in the search results that this company is involved in Biochar or any other CDR method.

name: TCHAR
tech_note: Biochar
description: TCHAR is a Taiwanese BiCRS company that converts industrial, agricultural, and wastewater treatment waste into biochar on-site, generating renewable energy and offering certified carbon dioxide removal.

name: TDA
tech_note: Develops 3D-printed sorbent monoliths and polymer sorbents for Direct Air Capture using a rapid thermal swing adsorption (RTSA) process under DOE/NETL contracts.
description: <cite index="13-3">TDA Research, under DOE contract DE-FE0032260, is developing novel 3D-printed sorbent structures that can capture carbon dioxide from air via a rapid thermal swing adsorption (RTSA) process.</cite> <cite index="6-2,6-3">The company was also awarded a DOE contract valued at up to $49 million for a pilot project to evaluate a sorbent-based CO2 capture system after combustion at the Wyoming Integrated Test Center, in collaboration with SLB.</cite> TDA is a contract R&D firm based in Wheat Ridge, CO, with DAC being one of several R&D focus areas.

name: TREEO
tech_note: TREEO runs smallholder reforestation projects in Uganda and Indonesia combined with a single-tree monitoring app (TREEO App) and Impact Storyboard dashboard for MRV, with long-term carbon storage via harvested wood products and biochar.
description: <cite index="19-4,19-10">TREEO is operated by Fairventures Digital GmbH in Stuttgart, Germany, originally spun out of reforestation NGO Fairventures Worldwide.</cite> <cite index="17-20,17-21,17-22">Through the TREEO technology, they empower tree growers in the Global South, finance reforestation and restoration projects, store the carbon long-term in harvested wood products and biochar, and provide full transparency via single-tree monitoring.</cite> <cite index="17-9">TREEO is certified as a C-Sink Manager and dMRV Provider by Carbon Standards International.</cite>

name: TVERF
tech_note: BECCS
description: TVERF (Tees Valley Energy Recovery Facility) is developing a facility in the North-East of the UK that will process general rubbish to generate electricity, with operations expected to begin in 2029. While it is an energy recovery facility, the provided search results do not explicitly state it is a Carbon Dioxide Removal (CDR) company using BECCS, but rather an Energy Recovery Facility.

name: Takachar
tech_note: Biochar
description: Takachar develops small-scale, low-cost, portable systems that convert agricultural and forest waste biomass into higher-value bio-products like biochar, which locks away CO2 when applied to soil.

name: Takatena
tech_note: Operates pyrolysis plants in Nanyuki, Kenya converting sewage and organic waste into biochar for soil application and carbon removal.
description: <cite index="16-1,16-2">Takatena transforms Kenya's organic waste into biochar via pyrolysis plants, aiming to enhance soil health and reduce carbon emissions.</cite> They sell biochar in volumes tied to CO2 removal (e.g. <cite index="6-4">1000 kg biochar representing ~3 tons CO2</cite>) and have received early-stage investment from Remove (Netherlands).

name: Taking Root
tech_note: Develops Plan Vivo-certified smallholder reforestation/agroforestry projects and operates a mobile+web MRV platform to quantify and verify forest carbon removals.
description: Taking Root is a Canadian project developer that partners with smallholder farmers (primarily in Nicaragua through its CommuniTree Carbon Program, certified under Plan Vivo) to restore forests and generate forest carbon removal credits.
