The company provides technology (FARM-TRACE platform/mobile app), MRV support, and handles project design, certification, and sale of removals.

name: Tambora
tech_note: ERW
description: Tambora Carbon Removal is an Indonesian climate tech startup specializing in enhanced rock weathering (ERW) for smallholder farmers.

name: Tapovanam
tech_note: Operates a pyrolysis plant in India that converts agricultural crop residues into biochar, bio-oil and syngas, using the syngas to power the reactor and generate electricity.
description: Tapovanam (Tapovanam Organic Farming Systems LLP) is an India-based biochar producer that pyrolyzes agricultural residues into biochar for soil amendment and durable carbon storage. The company is a member of CDR30 and aligns its methodology with Puro.earth and Isometric standards; it also runs an organic-produce marketplace ("Organic Tap") and an agriculture consultancy alongside its CDR activity.

name: Tau Carbon
tech_note: TSB
description: Tau Carbon removes CO2 from the atmosphere by preserving dry, densified wood waste in rugged fiberglass tanks and sells carbon credits. Their process involves collecting, transporting, and storing waste wood in containers to sequester carbon for millennia.

name: Telge Återvinning
tech_note: Biochar
description: Telge Återvinning is a Swedish company that produces biochar and biochar-based products through pyrolysis, diverting organic waste from landfills to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

name: Tellus
tech_note: Tellus converts biomass residues into biochar via pyrolysis, producing a stable carbon soil amendment sold as certified carbon removal.
description: Tellus Biocarbon is a Brazilian climate-tech company that works with local producers to transform biomass waste into biochar, marketed as a soil-improving, carbon-removing product. They are listed as a CDR30 member and their biochar is reportedly certified under international CDR standards.

name: Tera
tech_note: Tera operates a pyrolysis facility in Kisumu, Kenya that converts sugarcane bagasse into biochar, which is applied to farmland for soil improvement and long-term carbon sequestration.
description: Tera (Tera Carbon) is a Kenyan climate-tech startup producing biochar from sugarcane bagasse waste collected from mills in the Kisumu/Lake Victoria sugarcane belt. In 2025 it became the first African project developer independently validated on the Riverse carbon registry, and uses a custom digital MRV system (built with partner CYNK) to track carbon removal from biomass collection through pyrolysis and field application.

name: Terra fertilis
tech_note: Biochar
description: Terra Fertilis is a French company that produces biochar, a 100% natural charcoal derived from biomass pyrolysis, which is used as a soil amendment to improve fertility and retain water and nutrients, thereby contributing to carbon dioxide removal.

name: TerraBaru
tech_note: Pyrolysis of agricultural waste biomass to produce stable biochar for soil amendment and durable carbon storage.
description: TerraBaru is an Indonesian biochar producer that converts agricultural waste into engineered biochar ("TerraKarbon") via pyrolysis, generating carbon removal credits alongside soil, infrastructure, and energy applications. The company operates in Indonesia with a Singapore office and is actively representing itself at carbon industry events in 2025.

name: TerraFixing
tech_note: Solid sorbent DAC
description: TerraFixing is a Canadian Direct Air Capture (DAC) company that uses proprietary zeolite minerals (faujasite type) and adsorption technology to capture CO2, specifically designed for cold climates.

name: TerraNova Energy
tech_note: TerraNova Energy is a German technology provider and licensor of the TerraNova®ultra hydrothermal carbonization (HTC) process, which converts moist biomass and sewage sludge into hydrochar — a lignite-like, carbon-rich solid suitable for permanent CO2 storage.
description: <cite index="4-1,4-3">TerraNova Energy is a technology provider for upgrading organic waste streams via Thermal Hydrolysis Process (THP) and Hydrothermal Carbonization (HTC).</cite> <cite index="4-9,4-10,4-11">Its TerraNova®ultra process enables the use of moist biomass, particularly waste streams such as sewage sludge or organic waste, to generate "Hydrochar," in which over 90% of the biomass carbon is stored; it has a stability comparable to lignite and is positioned for permanent CO2 removal.</cite> <cite index="2-16,2-17">A plant based on TerraNova HTC technology including a pyrolysis unit was built in Mexico City to process 23,000 tons of organic waste per year.</cite>

name: TerraWatt
tech_note: Biochar
description: TerraWatt develops a process combining thermochemical treatment and biotechnological processes to produce biochar for carbon sequestration and biogas (biomethane) from various organic waste materials.

name: Terradot
tech_note: ERW
description: Terradot is a climate company that uses Enhanced Rock Weathering (ERW) to permanently remove CO2 by spreading crushed volcanic rock over farmland. They are building a global ERW carbon removal platform to deliver durable, high-quality carbon removal at scale.

name: Terradot acquires Eion to build global enhanced rock weathering carbon removal platform
Terraform Industries
tech_note: Synthetic fuels company using DAC and solar energy to produce carbon-neutral natural gas.
description: Terraform Industries uses Direct Air Capture (DAC) to capture CO2 from the air, which is then combined with green hydrogen to produce synthetic natural gas.

name: Terraformation
tech_note: Forest restoration technology company providing software, seed banking, and solar-powered desalination for reforestation at scale.
description: Terraformation is a "forest tech" startup that scales high-quality afforestation/reforestation (A/R) projects, focusing on native biodiverse reforestation to drive climate impact and boost biodiversity.

name: Terrafront
tech_note: Terrafront develops carbon removal projects across multiple pathways—biochar from agricultural residues (Terrachar), agroforestry/reforestation (Terraroots), and enhanced rock weathering (TerraRevive)—primarily working with smallholder farmers in South Asia and Africa.
description: <cite index="1-4">Terrafront develops climate change adaptation and mitigation infrastructure in South Asia and Africa</cite>, operating three project lines: Terrachar for biochar, Terraroots for agroforestry/reforestation under Verra VM47 and Gold Standard ARR, and TerraRevive for enhanced rock weathering. <cite index="3-1,3-7">They collaborate with Carboneers to process agricultural residues into biochar and heat, and partner with Together for Restoration to work with smallholder farmers in Assam, India.</cite>

name: Terranova
tech_note: TSB
description: No relevant search results were found for the specified CDR company 'Terranova' that uses BiCRS (Other) methods. The provided search results refer to other entities with similar names.

name: Terrasols
tech_note: Crushes volcanic basalt to optimal particle size and spreads it on Indian agricultural fields to accelerate silicate weathering reactions that convert atmospheric CO₂ into stable bicarbonates/carbonates.
description: Terrasols (terrasols.earth) is an India-based enhanced rock weathering supplier that crushes volcanic basalt and applies it on farmers' fields to permanently remove atmospheric CO₂ while improving soil health. <cite index="17-2,17-7">They are profiled in the remove. Carbon Removal Accelerator as "Harnessing the power of ERW to permanently remove CO₂ while regenerating soils and enhancing microbial activity for long-term fertility."</cite> They also describe themselves as a sustainability consulting firm, but the operational activity is ERW deployment on smallholder farms.

name: Terraton
tech_note: Full-stack biochar franchise platform: hardware, operating SaaS, and MRV/credit sales for pyrolysis facilities converting agricultural waste into stable soil carbon.
description: Terraton is a U.S.-based biochar carbon removal platform that partners with agribusinesses in emerging markets to build and operate biochar production facilities, providing hardware, SaaS, financing, and MRV. <cite index="2-2,2-3,2-4">The company raised an $11.5 million seed round in August 2025 led by Lowercarbon Capital and Gigascale Capital, with participation from ANA Future Frontier Fund, East Japan Railway's Takanawa Gateway fund, and angels including Jeff Dean and Bret Taylor.</cite> <cite index="2-1">It has developed two facilities in Africa, one in Ghana and the other in Kenya.</cite>

name: The Carbon Removers
tech_note: Captures biogenic CO2 from whisky distilleries and biogas plants in the UK and stores it via mineralization in building aggregates or permanent geological storage under the North Sea.
description: <cite index="6-1,6-2">The Carbon Removers, formerly known as Carbon Capture Scotland, is a Scottish company specializing in engineered biogenic carbon dioxide removal, co-founded by brothers Richard and Ed Nimmons, having grown from dry ice production into a carbon removal provider.</cite> <cite index="2-1">The company scales biogenic carbon capture and storage (BECCS) in Scotland, capturing CO₂ from distilleries and biogas facilities for mineralization into building aggregates and long-term storage.</cite> <cite index="7-9">They also have an agreement to permanently sequester 50,000 tons of CO2 beneath the North Sea for the Greensand Future project.</cite>

name: The Future Forest Company
tech_note: Native tree planting and peatland restoration on UK estates, generating Woodland and Peatland Carbon Code units.
description: The Future Forest Company is a UK-based reforestation and peatland restoration developer operating sites in Scotland and Northern England, issuing Woodland Carbon Units and Peatland Carbon Units under the UK Woodland Carbon Code and Peatland Code. They have planted over one million trees and published a 2025 Impact Report. Their enhanced-weathering arm spun out as UNDO in 2022, leaving the parent focused on nature-based removals.

name: The New Black Biochar
tech_note: Biochar
description: The New Black Biochar is an Australian company based in Tasmania that produces biochar from organic waste streams to sequester carbon and create products for home gardens and environmental remediation.

name: The Vast Promise And Uncertain Future Of Carbon Removals
Three Mountains Cocoa
tech_note: Host agribusiness for a biochar facility that pyrolyzes cocoa pod husk waste into stable carbon, developed in partnership with Terraton.
description: <cite index="10-3,10-10,10-11">Three Mountains Cocoa (TMC) is a Ghanaian cocoa cooperative founded by Leslie Agyare that works with over 2,000 farmers across 15 communities producing organic single-origin cocoa beans.</cite> <cite index="13-1,13-6">The Three Mountains Cocoa biochar project in Ghana, developed with Terraton and with preliminary approval from Puro.earth, is expected to contribute to over 20,000 tons of annual CO₂ removal, and Terraset has committed a six-figure carbon credit pre-purchase from the project.</cite> TMC serves as the host site and feedstock supplier (cocoa pod husk) for the biochar facility, which is listed on Puro.earth under its name.

name: Tierra Foods
tech_note: Uses oxalogenic trees (ramón/Brosimum alicastrum, English Oak) in agroforestry systems to drive the oxalate-carbonate pathway, precipitating atmospheric CO2 as stable calcium carbonate in soil, with AI-driven MRV.
description: <cite index="12-4,12-6,12-7">Tierra Foods is a UK climate tech startup developing a carbon-removal system centred on plants that perform biomineralisation — specifically oxalogenic species that convert atmospheric CO2 into calcium carbonate stored in soil.</cite> <cite index="5-2,5-3">The company develops agroforestry projects using biomineralisation-capable plants like the Uje/ramón tree (Brosimum alicastrum) via the Oxalate-Carbonate Pathway, producing both permanent carbon removal and sustainable food ingredients.</cite> <cite index="13-3,12-3">It has raised a $520K round announced in early 2025 and is backed by £496,000 of Innovate UK funding for an AI-based MRV methodology with the University of Huddersfield.</cite>

name: Tierra Prieta
tech_note: Pyrolyzes waste pecan shells at an industrial facility in Parras, Coahuila, Mexico to produce biochar used as a soil amendment, generating durable carbon removal credits certified under Puro.earth.
description: <cite index="1-1,1-2">Tierra Prieta is a Mexican biochar producer with a facility in Parras, Coahuila that uses pecan shells as feedstock, and is certifying its carbon removal for the voluntary carbon market.</cite> <cite index="12-3,12-4">Carbon removal was to be certified by Puro.earth in Q2 2024, with current biochar production capacity of 500 tons per year, inaugurated in May 2023.</cite> <cite index="17-2">The startup recently obtained certification of its first 1,200 carbon removal credits.</cite>

name: Timber Finance
tech_note: Sustainable forestry investment firm managing timberland assets for carbon sequestration and timber production.
description: Timber Finance focuses on biomass carbon removal by promoting the use of timber as a construction material to store CO2 long-term in buildings and by developing financial instruments for timber investments.

name: TimberTurn
tech_note: TSB
description: TimberTurn provides a scalable solution for uneconomical, non-merchantable waste wood from fuel thinning treatments, preventing wildfires and storing carbon.

name: Tivano Carbon
tech_note: Harvests invasive encroacher bush from Namibian savannas and stores it in engineered, sensor-monitored underground vaults designed for centuries of stability, generating biomass-burial carbon removal credits.
description: <cite index="1-1,1-2">Tivano Carbon restores Namibia's savanna rangelands by converting invasive encroacher bush into permanently stored carbon using engineered underground burial in sensor-monitored vaults with MRV to produce verified carbon removal credits.</cite> <cite index="2-5">The company collaborates with local farmers and experts from TU Berlin on its carbon vaults and landscape regeneration initiatives.</cite> This is a biomass burial supplier, not BECCS.

name: TorrCoal
tech_note: Torrefaction (mild pyrolysis at 200-300°C) of wood/agro residues and scrap wood into bio-carbon powder used mainly as a fossil-coal substitute in steel, cement and chemicals.
description: TorrCoal is a Belgian torrefaction technology specialist (founded 2005, based in Dilsen-Stokkem) that was acquired by Dutch climate-tech firm Perpetual Next in September 2021 and now operates as its subsidiary. The company uses torrefaction (mild pyrolysis) to convert wood and agro-residues — including scrap wood and plastic-containing waste — into bio-carbon powder supplied to steel (ArcelorMittal), chemical and cement industries as a fossil coal replacement. Parent Perpetual Next frames the activity as carbon removal via stable bio-carbon, though a significant share of output is used as a reductant/fuel which raises CCU-vs-CDR questions.

name: Toshiba ESS
tech_note: Post-combustion amine-based CO2 capture retrofitted to a 50 MW palm-kernel-shell biomass power plant, with CO2 liquefaction and planned ship transport for storage.
description: Toshiba Energy Systems & Solutions (Toshiba ESS) is the energy division of Toshiba Corporation that developed and operates a large-scale BECCS demonstration facility at the 50 MW Mikawa biomass power plant (operated by its subsidiary SIGMA POWER Ariake) in Omuta, Japan, capturing more than 500 tonnes of CO2 per day from palm kernel shell-fueled flue gas. The project, funded by Japan's Ministry of the Environment, began operations in 2020 and expanded under a FY2021–FY2025 demonstration including CO2 liquefaction and transport. Toshiba ESS's core business remains power generation equipment; CDR is an R&D/demonstration activity within the division.

name: Towing
tech_note: Produces "Soratan," a high-performance biochar inoculated with microorganisms and mixed with organic fertilizer, applied to farmland for soil improvement and carbon sequestration under Japan's J-Credit Scheme.
description: <cite index="9-2,9-8">TOWING is a Japanese Nagoya University spinout founded in 2020 that has developed a crop cultivation system to enable more sustainable farming practices.</cite> <cite index="2-3">In June 2023, a project of Soratan was registered under Japan's J-Credit Scheme for "Biochar Application to Farmland" and has issued carbon credits three times.</cite> The company partners with firms like Suntory and Biocare to scale biochar-based carbon removal globally.

name: Travertine
tech_note: Liquid solvent DAC
description: Travertine Technologies uses an electrochemical platform to accelerate the Earth's natural carbon cycle, precipitating carbonate minerals from carbon dioxide in the air, inspired by enhanced rock weathering.

name: Treeconomy
tech_note: Reforestation platform connecting landowners with investors for afforestation carbon credits in Europe.
description: Treeconomy is a London-based start-up that uses remote sensing and machine learning to monitor and measure forest carbon stocks, bringing trust and traceability to nature-based afforestation/reforestation carbon removal projects.

name: Tropicarbon
tech_note: Spreads fine silicate rock dust on Colombian farmland to accelerate weathering and permanently sequester CO2, with proprietary aqueous-phase MRV aligned to Isometric and Puro.earth protocols.
description: <cite index="2-1,2-2">Tropicarbon leads Enhanced Rock Weathering in Colombia, targeting 1 million tons of CO2 removal by 2030, with a mission to achieve trustworthy carbon removal with innovative technology while optimizing benefits for local farmers.</cite> <cite index="1-9,1-10">In partnership with Universidad del Norte, Tropicarbon launched the Barranquilla Project, testing how its rock powder interacts with dozens of Colombian soils under tropical conditions.</cite> <cite index="4-6,4-7,4-11,4-12">Founded in 2023 and headquartered in Colombia, the company has raised $100K with investment from GLOCAL (Argentina).</cite>

name: Truecoco
tech_note: Controlled pyrolysis of coconut husk agricultural waste in Ghana to produce Puro.earth-certified biochar applied as soil amendment.
description: Truecoco is a Ghana-based biochar carbon removal developer that originated as an organic coconut processor in 2017 and launched West Africa's first industrial-scale biochar facility in 2025, using coconut husk waste as feedstock. The company is Puro.earth certified and signed a multi-year offtake agreement with Climeworks extending to 2032. It aims to remove 250,000 tonnes of CO2 by 2030 while benefiting smallholder farmers.

name: Truecoco Ghana
tech_note: Biochar
description: Truecoco Ghana is a BiCRS company that produces biochar from agricultural waste, specifically coconut husks, to remove CO2 from the atmosphere and improve the livelihoods of smallholder farmers in Ghana.

name: UNDO
tech_note: UNDO spreads crushed silicate rock (basalt in UK, wollastonite in Canada) on agricultural land to accelerate natural weathering, permanently mineralizing atmospheric CO2 as bicarbonate.
description: UNDO is a UK-based carbon removal developer specializing in Enhanced Rock Weathering (ERW), operating in the UK and Canada with a hub in Kingston, Ontario and an expanding footprint via a Brazil partnership. The company was named one of four global winners of the $100M XPRIZE Carbon Removal competition in April 2025, and has delivery agreements with Microsoft, Barclays, British Airways, McLaren, and Stripe. UNDO handles both physical feedstock deployment and MRV, making it a full-stack ERW supplier.

name: Ucaneo
tech_note: Ucaneo develops a biomimetic electrochemical Direct Air Capture system using a specialized solvent that mimics the human lung to capture CO2 at room temperature, powered by renewable electricity.
description: Ucaneo is a Berlin-based DAC startup founded in 2022 that operates an industrial pilot capturing 30-50 tons CO2/year and is building what it claims will be Germany's largest DAC demonstration plant, targeted for commissioning in H1 2026. The company raised €6.75M in seed funding in September 2024, with Aramco Ventures joining the round in March 2025.

name: Uisa
tech_note: Sugarcane/corn biorefinery planning post-fermentation CO2 capture and geological injection into the Parecis Sedimentary Basin at its Nova Olímpia plant.
description: Uisa is one of Brazil's largest integrated biorefineries, producing sugar, ethanol, renewable energy, and yeast from sugarcane at its Nova Olímpia plant in Mato Grosso. The company announced BECCS plans to capture CO2 from its corn-to-ethanol operations and inject it into the Parecis Sedimentary Basin ~15 km from the plant, with drilling scheduled for 2024 and construction for 2025. The project is still in pre-operational development and depends on Brazil's CCS regulatory framework.

name: Underground Forest
tech_note: Drives Norway spruce wooden piles into anoxic Dutch peat and clay soils below the water table as building foundations, storing biogenic carbon for 1,000+ years while replacing emissions-heavy concrete piles.
description: <cite index="3-9,3-10,3-11">Founded by Kees de Gruiter in 2023, Underground Forest revives ancient wood-piling techniques for long-term carbon storage, using sustainably sourced logs to store CO₂ for up to 1,000 years while offering solutions for peatland restoration and climate-neutral housing, with support from CarbonFix preparing to sequester its first kiloton of CO₂ by 2025.</cite> <cite index="1-11">Their method is certified according to the IPCC CDR Taxonomy and the EU CRCF programme with a permanence of more than a thousand years.</cite> <cite index="4-1">In 2025, greenhouse builder KUBO launched a partnership with Underground Forest to use wooden pile foundations that enable long-term CO2 storage.</cite>

name: Unemit
tech_note: Solid sorbent DAC
description: Unemit is a company working to reverse climate change with permanent Carbon Dioxide Removal using novel Direct Air Capture (DAC) technology, specifically employing a chemical sorbent to capture CO2.

name: United Earth Energy
tech_note: Builds a containerized, mobile pyrolysis reactor (UNI-Box) that thermally decomposes organic waste in an oxygen-free environment to produce biochar, bio-oil, and syngas.
description: United Earth Energy is a US-based waste-to-energy technology company selling the UNI-Box mobile pyrolysis system, which converts agricultural, municipal, and industrial organic waste into biochar, bio-oil, and syngas. The biochar output provides carbon sequestration and soil enrichment, while the system also processes non-CDR feedstocks such as tires and plastics. The company markets the UNI-Box to municipalities, farms, and industrial clients and references carbon credit eligibility as a customer value proposition.

name: Unyte
tech_note: Unyte operates pyrolysis furnaces in Theddingworth, UK to convert hemp production waste and local green/wood waste into biochar, generating carbon removal credits via the Riverse registry.
description: Unyte Group is a UK-based sustainability group whose Unyte Hemp/Unyte Solutions division produces biochar from hemp and wood waste using Multi-Eco pyrolysing furnaces at a facility in Leicestershire. The project is registered under the Riverse biochar methodology and the company is an active participant in UK hemp-carbon research consortia including CHCx3.

name: UrjanovaC
tech_note: Aqueous-based carbon capture using a patented earth-abundant catalyst that captures CO2 from flue gas or ambient air in water (including wastewater/seawater) and permanently fixes it as stable mineral carbonates.
description: UrjanovaC is a Mumbai-based startup spun out of IIT Bombay's DST-supported National Centre of Excellence in Carbon Capture and Utilization, co-founded by Prof. Vikram Vishal and Prof. Arnab Dutta. The company is developing a catalyst-based aqueous CO2 capture technology (TRL 5) that works on both industrial flue gas and ambient air, with captured CO2 converted into stable mineral carbonates. The team is building a 3 tonnes-per-day pilot at IIT Bombay.

name: UseNexus
tech_note: Solid sorbent DAC
description: UseNexus (Nexus Carbon Capture) harnesses direct air capture (DAC) technology to capture atmospheric and metabolic CO2 directly from the air, specifically using a solid sorbent method.

name: V-Grid Energy Systems
tech_note: VGrid operates modular, trailer-based high-temperature biomass gasification units ("Bioservers") that convert agricultural waste (e.g. pistachio shells) into renewable electricity and biochar, which stabilizes carbon for 1,000+ years.
description: V-Grid Energy Systems is a California-based clean energy and biochar producer headquartered in Camarillo, operating Bioserver gasification units in the Central Valley since 2019. The company sells CORC carbon removal credits through Puro.earth and markets biochar and bio-liquid products under the Persist and Karrikaid brands.

name: VIB-KU Leuven Center for Brain & Disease Research
Valero
tech_note: BECCS
description: Valero is a major producer of fuels and renewable fuels, including biofuels. They are involved in Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Storage (BECCS) through partnerships and carbon capture projects at their ethanol plants to reduce the carbon intensity of ethanol.

name: Varaha
tech_note: Develops biochar via industrial gasification reactors plus regenerative agriculture, agroforestry and enhanced rock weathering projects with smallholder farmers in South Asia and Africa, using an in-house digital MRV system to generate verified carbon removal credits.
description: Varaha is an India-based carbon removal project developer operating across India, Nepal, Bangladesh, Bhutan and Ivory Coast, working with ~170,000+ smallholder farmers. Their primary pathway is industrial and artisanal biochar (registered on Puro.earth), supplemented by regenerative agriculture, agroforestry, and enhanced rock weathering. Major offtake deals with Google (100,000t, Jan 2025) and Microsoft (100,000t+, Jan 2026), and they raised $20M of a $45M Series B led by WestBridge Capital in Feb 2026.

name: Varhad
tech_note: Produces biochar via Kon-Tiki kilns and industrial pyrolysis reactors using cotton and pigeon pea stalks from farmer cooperatives in Maharashtra, India, and is expanding into biomethanol-linked CDR.
description: <cite index="3-3">VCAP, a Varhad Group subsidiary, is India's largest artisanal biochar producer and registered C-sink manager, offering expert advisory on eco-friendly biocoal and biochar production.</cite> <cite index="5-6,5-7">The company partnered with Japan's Green Carbon Inc. and Switzerland's Carbonfuture on a large-scale CDR project that will make approximately 120,300 tonnes of carbon removal credits available via Carbonfuture.</cite> <cite index="2-1">As of early 2026, Varhad is scaling up carbon-removal capacity using both biochar and biomethanol pathways in an integrated biomass-to-biofuel and CDR model.</cite>

name: Varme
tech_note: Municipal solid waste incineration for electricity generation with post-combustion amine carbon capture and permanent geologic CO2 storage, generating BECCS credits from the biogenic fraction of the waste.
description: Varme Energy is a Canadian subsidiary of Norway-based Varme Energy AS developing Canada's first commercial-scale waste-to-energy facility with integrated carbon capture and storage in Alberta's Industrial Heartland. The AIH1 project targets commercial operations in 2029 and plans to deliver approximately 130,000 tonnes/year of BECCS carbon removal credits, with Carbon Direct marketing the credits. The project has received AUC approval, Alberta government funding, and partnership commitments from Canada Growth Fund and Gibson Energy.

name: Vault 44.01
tech_note: BECCS
description: Vault 44.01 is a carbon capture and sequestration (CCS) project development team focused on enabling cost-effective, wholesale decarbonization of industrial emissions through permanent geological storage of CO2, specifically using BECCS as a method.

name: Vaulted Deep
tech_note: Bio-slurry
description: Vaulted Deep is a BiCRS company that removes carbon dioxide by geologically sequestering carbon-filled organic waste, such as excess manure, treated sewage, paper sludge, and agricultural byproducts, deep underground.

name: Verde Resources
tech_note: Produces biochar from biogenic waste and embeds it in asphalt (BioAsphalt™) for road construction to achieve durable, verifiable carbon sequestration.
description: Verde Resources (OTCQB: VRDR) is a US-listed sustainable infrastructure company that produces BioAsphalt™, incorporating engineered biochar into road construction materials to create durable carbon sinks. The company generated the first Puro.earth-verified carbon removal credits from an asphalt application (8 tons) via its NCAT pilot, and in March 2026 signed a supply deal with Biochar Solutions LLC for up to 38,500 tons of biochar annually, alongside a $2M strategic investment from Ergon.

name: Verdox
tech_note: MIT spin-off developing electro-swing adsorption (electrochemical) carbon capture using quinone-based electrodes that bind and release CO2 via small voltage changes, targeting both dilute industrial off-gas and direct air capture.
description: Verdox is a Boston-based electric carbon capture company founded in 2019 out of MIT, commercializing an all-electric electro-swing adsorption process that captures CO2 using electricity instead of heat or pressure. In November 2025 it completed a successful two-month industrial trial capturing CO2 from 1%-concentration aluminum smelter off-gas at Hydro's Sunndal plant in Norway, and commissioned a pilot-scale unit in October 2025 ahead of 2026 customer pilots. The company is backed by $80M from Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Prelude Ventures, Lowercarbon Capital, and strategic investor Hydro.

name: Verora
tech_note: Biochar
description: Verora produces high-quality biochar from agricultural and landscaping residues, which is marketed under the brand name Verora Pflanzenkohle and certified according to the European Biochar Certificate.

name: Verra
tech_note: Verra is a non-profit carbon standards body and registry that administers the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) Program, certifying and issuing carbon credits (VCUs) for projects including nature-based removals, and operating the Verra Registry.
description: Verra is a US-based non-profit that operates the world's largest voluntary carbon crediting program (VCS) and public registry, setting methodologies and certifying projects that issue Verified Carbon Units. It is core ecosystem infrastructure — a standards-setter, verifier, and registry rather than a physical CDR supplier — and is widely used across forestry, REDD+, and emerging engineered-removal pathways.

name: Vesta
tech_note: OAE
description: Vesta (also known as Project Vesta) is a marine CDR company that uses ocean alkalinity enhancement by adding olivine minerals to coastal waters to reduce ocean acidity and remove carbon dioxide.

name: Viochar
tech_note: Biochar
description: Viochar provides robust solutions for scalable biochar carbon capture, specifically through the production of biochar using pyrolysis batch reactors to sequester carbon and improve soil quality.

name: Viridor
tech_note: BECCS
description: Viridor is a UK-based recycling and waste management company that aims to transform waste for a climate-positive future. They are investing in technologies such as carbon capture to support the transition to a circular economy, specifically working on a carbon capture and storage project at an energy-from-waste plant.

name: Vital Chemical
tech_note: Biochar
description: Vital Chemical is an Australian company that produces Vital Biochar from sustainably sourced forestry biomass using pyrolysis. This biochar is used as a soil amendment and revegetation product, contributing to carbon dioxide removal by sequestering organic carbon in soil.

name: Vycarb
tech_note: Vycarb builds modular, sensor-driven hardware/software systems that add alkaline minerals to CO2-rich coastal and industrial waters, converting CO2 into stable bicarbonate via ocean alkalinity enhancement with real-time MRV.
description: Brooklyn-based climate tech startup founded in 2022 by Dr. Garrett Boudinot that deploys modular autonomous OAE systems to permanently store CO2 as bicarbonate in natural waters. Vycarb operates a flagship pilot at Brooklyn Navy Yard on the East River (~100 tCO2/yr) and targets integration with cement, steel, power, bioenergy and port facilities. Closed a $5M seed round in October 2025 led by Twynam with MOL Switch, Hatch Blue, Clocktower Ventures, Idemitsu, SGInnovate, and Shell.

name: Växjö Energi
tech_note: Swedish municipal energy utility developing bioenergy carbon capture and storage (BECCS) at its biomass-fired Sandviksverket CHP plant, targeting ~200,000 t CO2/yr captured and permanently stored (e.g. Greensand, North Sea) from 2028.
description: <cite index="9-8,9-9,9-10">Växjö Energi AB is a Swedish municipal energy company collaborating with Sumitomo SHI FW on hot potassium carbonate carbon capture at its fully fossil-free CHP plant, aiming to capture approximately 200,000 tonnes of CO2 annually starting in 2028.</cite> <cite index="3-4,3-5,3-6,3-7">Forestry residues fuel their bioenergy plant, flue-gas CO2 is separated and liquefied, then transported for permanent storage in the North Sea 2,000–3,000 m below sea level, yielding carbon dioxide removal.</cite> <cite index="2-27,2-28">A permit application with Mark- och miljödomstolen is in progress, with a scoping consultation held in November 2024.</cite>

name: Wakefield BioChar
tech_note: Biochar
description: Wakefield BioChar is a BiCRS company that produces biochar from wood waste, which is used as a soil conditioner to enhance soil health, conserve water, and sequester carbon for generations.

name: Waste to Energy
tech_note: Wholesale distributor of biochar (granular and liquid) sourced from virgin wood feedstock for nationwide US markets.
description: Waste to Energy (WTE) is a US-based wholesale distributor of biochar, offering product in granular and liquid forms derived from virgin wood biomass. They are listed on the US Biochar Initiative member directory and describe themselves as the largest wholesale bio carbon provider in the US. Limited recent public signals (news, press, funding) are available.

name: WasteX
tech_note: Biochar
description: WasteX is a climate-tech startup that provides a full-stack biochar solution, converting biomass waste into biochar using proprietary small-scale carbonizer equipment for agricultural producers and farms.

name: Waterberg Carbon Co
tech_note: Biochar
description: Waterberg Carbon Co is a BiCRS company that utilizes biochar for carbon dioxide removal, partnering with other technology companies for its operations.

name: Watershed
tech_note: Enterprise sustainability platform for carbon measurement, reduction, and offsetting.
description: Watershed is an enterprise sustainability platform that helps companies measure, reduce, and report emissions. It operates a marketplace offering a rigorously vetted supply of carbon removal options, including nature-based and permanent CDR projects like direct air capture and bio-oil sequestration.

name: Wonderchar
tech_note: Operates pyrolysis kilns that convert Texas pecan shells (and some softwood) into biochar sold in multiple granular/powder grades as soil amendment, sequestering carbon long-term.
description: Wonderchar INC. is a Texas-based biochar producer that converts waste pecan shells into OMRI-certified biochar products (PecanChar Natural, LG+, Soil+, Powder+, EZ MIX) sold to farmers, nurseries, landscapers and fertilizer manufacturers. Products are offered in bulk bags and sacks for soil, compost, turf and fertilizer blending applications, with carbon sequestration as a co-benefit.

name: Woodcache
tech_note: Buries waste woody biomass from wildfire-risk forests in engineered anaerobic underground pits designed to inhibit decomposition, with MRV via flux chambers and subterranean sensors.
description: Woodcache PBC is a U.S. public benefit corporation that buries waste woody biomass (from wildfire mitigation and forestry thinning) in engineered, cold/dry/anaerobic underground pits for durable CO2 removal. They completed their La Veta, Colorado production-scale project in 2024 with support from a 4 Corners Carbon Removal grant and sell Puro.earth-certified CORCs.

name: Woodtek Biochar
tech_note: Biochar
description: Woodtek Biochar is a UK-based company that designs and builds pyrolysis plants to convert biomass into EBC-grade biochar, a form of captured and sequestered carbon.

name: Wundergarten
tech_note: Formulates and sells biochar-containing gardening substrates, fertilizers, and seeds using EBC-certified pyrolysis biochar from cocoa shells and herbs.
description: Wundergarten is a German consumer gardening brand founded in 2019 that sells biochar-based soils, fertilizers, and biochar-coated seeds to retail customers via its webshop, Amazon, and selected supermarkets. The biochar is made from cocoa shells and herbs via pyrolysis (EBC-certified), and the company markets CO2 storage in soil as a co-benefit. They function as a biochar product formulator/distributor rather than a credit-issuing CDR project developer.

name: XPRIZE Carbon Removal Competition Page
tech_note: Global incentive-prize competition that funded and validated CDR suppliers across DAC, ERW, biochar, ocean, and biomass pathways; ran 2021–2025 with a $100M purse.
description: XPRIZE Carbon Removal was a $100M incentive competition funded by the Musk Foundation, launched on Earth Day 2021 and concluded in April 2025 when Mati Carbon won the $50M grand prize for enhanced rock weathering. Runners-up included NetZero (biochar), Vaulted Deep (biomass burial), and UNDO Carbon (ERW), with XFACTOR awards to Planetary and Project Hajar. The competition page is run by the XPRIZE Foundation, a nonprofit that designs and operates incentive prizes — not a CDR supplier itself but a major catalyst of the CDR ecosystem.

name: Yama
tech_note: Hybrid electrochemical DAC using a non-toxic liquid sorbent with pH and temperature swing desorption, integrating electrodialysis and low-grade heat to cut energy use.
description: Yama is a Paris-based Direct Air Capture startup developing a hybrid electrochemical/thermal desorption technology with a proprietary liquid sorbent to lower DAC energy and cost. The company operates a small pilot near Paris (~25 tCO2/yr) and is targeting a first-of-a-kind commercial plant around 2030, with partnerships including Great Carbon Valley in Kenya and early credit buyers like Klarna via Milkywire.

name: Yellow Duck
tech_note: Develops a floating, wave-powered direct air capture device ("Wave-DAC") that harnesses ocean wave motion to generate electricity, produce hydrogen via seawater electrolysis, and capture CO2 from the atmosphere.
description: Yellow Duck Inc. is a Kobe, Japan cleantech startup, led by CEO Shigeo Nakayama, developing the Wave-DAC — an egg-shaped floating device that tilts with waves to generate power used to drive electrolysis and atmospheric CO2 capture. The company won the Marinetech Grand Prix 2023 Grand Prize and exhibited at Expo 2025 Osaka. Still at early prototype/verification stage.

name: Yggdrasil Trees
tech_note: Pre-seed project developer designing urban-integrated DAC units (targeting ~800 t CO2/unit/year), licensing solid sorbent IP from third-party DAC technology providers.
description: <cite index="2-1,2-2">Yggdrasil Trees is developing a decentralized, multi-functional direct air capture (DAC) solution designed for integration into urban environments, aiming to remove 800 tonnes of CO2 per unit per year.</cite> <cite index="2-7,2-8">The company is positioned as a project developer focusing on licensing sorbent materials from other DAC companies to accelerate deployment.</cite> It is a US-based pre-seed startup in the LACI portfolio.

name: Yuanchu Technology
tech_note: Yuanchu uses a chemical-looping reactor (YAM) to mineralize CO2 from flue gas or ambient air with calcium-rich industrial solid waste (carbide slag, steel slag) or silicates, producing stable calcium carbonate for permanent sequestration.
description: <cite index="3-1,3-2">Yuanchu Technology is a Beijing-based company founded in 2014 that develops large-scale, low-cost permanent carbon mineralization technology.</cite> <cite index="16-1,16-2">It is developing direct air mineralization (DAM) technology for removing CO2 from air and permanently sequestering it into solid carbonated material, claiming stability for 1000 years.</cite> <cite index="12-5,12-6">It was selected as an XPRIZE Carbon Removal finalist in the Rocks category competing for the $50M Musk Foundation prize.</cite>

name: ZEN Carbon
tech_note: Injects captured CO₂ into ready-mix concrete during mixing, where it reacts to form stable calcium carbonate minerals, permanently storing CO₂ while reducing cement content and improving strength.
description: <cite index="3-6,3-7">ZEN Carbon is a Kenya-based startup whose mineralization technology injects captured CO₂ directly into concrete, cutting cement use and emissions while strengthening the material itself.</cite> <cite index="3-11">It sources CO₂ from partners like Octavia Carbon's Direct Air Capture systems and infuses it into concrete during mixing.</cite> <cite index="2-3">In late 2025 the company moved from pilot stage to live industrial deployment by partnering with Flamingo Concrete, a ready-mix concrete supplier in Kenya.</cite>

name: ZS2
tech_note: Manufactures magnesium-oxide (MgO) cement building products that sequester CO2 via mineralization, paired with a proprietary DAC front-end for CO2 supply.
description: ZS2 Technologies is a Calgary-based manufacturer of magnesium cement building materials (boards, panels, tiles, sheathing) that mineralize CO2 into the cement matrix, reportedly at ~10% by weight. The company also develops a proprietary direct-air-capture process to source CO2 for sequestration, and was a Carbon Removal XPRIZE Milestone 1 top-60 company. In May 2025 it launched its commercially-ready Gen 2 product platform with $9.9M+ in grant backing.

name: ZeoDAC
tech_note: ZeoDAC uses a proprietary amine-free, solid-sorbent DAC process based on commercially available zeolite/molecular sieve materials, capturing both CO2 and water via a temperature-vacuum swing adsorption cycle.
description: <cite index="7-4,7-9">Founded in June 2023, the Atlanta-based company was established by Professor Christopher W. Jones (Georgia Tech) and Professor Mark E. Davis (Caltech) to extract carbon dioxide from air using zeolites.</cite> <cite index="3-5">Investors include Wilson Hill Ventures, Caltech, Coca-Cola Europacific Partners, Freeflow Ventures and Global Brain.</cite> Note: captured CO2 may be sequestered or used in beverages/chemicals, so end-use pathway is a mix of CDR and CCU.

name: Zero Carbon Systems
tech_note: Solid sorbent DAC
description: Zero Carbon Systems focuses on highly scalable, low-cost, and low-energy Direct Air Capture (DAC) solutions using a solid sorbent contactor technology for efficient CO2 adsorption/desorption.

name: ZeroEx
tech_note: ERW
description: ZeroEx is a German company founded in 2022 that specializes in Enhanced Rock Weathering (ERW) projects, accelerating the natural weathering of silicate rocks by applying finely crushed rock powder to agricultural fields to remove CO2.

name: [C]Worthy
tech_note: Nonprofit Focused Research Organization building open-source ocean modeling and MRV software (C-Star) for quantifying marine CDR like ocean alkalinity enhancement.
description: <cite index="3-9,3-10">[C]Worthy is a nonprofit research and development organization focused on delivering the core computational technologies needed to support quantitative assessments of ocean-based carbon dioxide removal. They build open-source software, conduct basic research on the efficacy of ocean-based CDR technologies, create and curate publicly available datasets, and promote scientific standards for evaluating the safety and effectiveness of ocean-based CDR activities.</cite> They do not themselves remove CO2; they supply MRV modeling infrastructure (C-Star) used by mCDR developers and verifiers like Isometric.

name: agriCARBON/MicroCHAR
tech_note: Biochar
description: agriCARBON/MicroCHAR produces innovative carbon organic fertilizers and soil conditioners from biomass-derived biochar, supplemented with organic nutrients, rhizobacteria, and mycorrhizal fungi. Their method involves pyrolysis of agricultural by-products to create biochar for carbon removal and soil improvement.

name: alterBiota
tech_note: Bio-materials
description: alterBiota is a green materials company that develops a natural admixture called hydrous Bio Graphene Oxide (hBGO) to enable concrete producers to use less Portland cement, thereby decarbonizing the construction industry.

name: atdepth
tech_note: MIT spin-off developing a GPU-based, data-assimilating ocean modeling and monitoring system that provides Measurement, Reporting and Verification (MRV) for marine carbon dioxide removal projects.
description: atdepth MRV is a Cambridge, MA-based MIT spin-off providing MRV services to the marine CDR (mCDR) industry. It combines multi-scale ocean and biogeochemical modeling with monitoring data to quantify carbon removal for mCDR project developers. The company received a $2.6M ARPA-E SEA-CO2 grant and has partnered with Deep Sky to monitor direct ocean capture operations in Canada.

name: bionero
tech_note: Produces EBC-certified biochar from organic residues via PYREG pyrolysis technology and markets biochar-amended potting soil and soil products that fix carbon long-term.
description: bionero GmbH is a small biochar producer based in Thurnau, Bavaria (Germany), founded in 2018. They carbonize organic residues using PYREG pyrolysis systems to make EBC-certified biochar, which they incorporate into peat-free potting soils and related products sold to consumers and horticultural markets.

name: corigin
tech_note: Uses vacuum pyrolysis (licensed Pyrovac technology) to convert almond shells and orchard residues into biochar, bio-oil for underground injection, and liquid bio-distillates for agriculture.
description: Corigin Solutions is a US-based company that converts agricultural residues (almond shells, orchard trimmings, nutshells) into biochar and bio-oil via vacuum pyrolysis. Their Corichar biochar is sold as a soil amendment, and their bio-oil is supplied to Charm Industrial for deep geological sequestration. They are a standalone CDR supplier, not a subsidiary.

name: ecoLocked
tech_note: ecoLocked converts waste-biomass biochar into functional concrete admixtures (eLM Zero) that permanently lock biogenic carbon into buildings while replacing cement/aggregates.
description: <cite index="5-4,5-5,5-6">Berlin-based startup ecoLocked, founded in 2021, is among the few global producers of concrete admixtures utilizing biochar for carbon removal, focusing on eco-friendly building materials. Its flagship product, eLM Zero, is a carbon-negative admixture designed to reduce concrete's net carbon footprint by up to 100%.</cite> <cite index="7-3,7-6">The company raised €4 million in a seed round led by Matterwave Ventures and Climentum Capital, with proceeds used to expand production, introduce new product lines and grow demand.</cite>

name: ecoX
tech_note: Plans to produce biochar from biomass via pyrolysis in Namibia as part of a "Poverty Eradication Franchise" model tied to African Savanna re-wilding, aiming to generate CDR credits.
description: ecoX, LLC is a US-based early-stage biochar developer listed on Puro.earth as a future supplier (ecoX-1) with a planned facility in Namibia. The Puro listing shows 0 CORCs issued and the project is in early-development/feasibility stage. With only 1 employee on LinkedIn and a thin website, the company appears to be a very small, pre-operational venture.

name: enfinium
tech_note: BECCS
description: enfinium is a UK-based BiCRS company that aims to achieve net carbon removals by installing Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS) technology on its energy-from-waste (EfW) plants, transforming them into net-negative emitters.

name: eoc energy ocean
tech_note: Pyrolyzes regional woody biomass into EBC-certified biochar (Pflanzenkohle) in Luthern, Switzerland, with waste heat supplied to the village.
description: eoc energy ocean GmbH is a Lucerne-based biochar producer founded in 2017 that turns untreated regional wood into EBC AgroBio/Futter+ certified Swiss biochar, binding CO2 and delivering process heat to the local village. The company also advises on pyrolysis projects, biomass utilization, and CO2/EBC certification. It won the Albert Koechlin Foundation's 2024 Environment Award.

name: goodcarbon
tech_note: Nature-based carbon removal credit sourcing and quality assurance platform.
description: goodcarbon operates a platform and marketplace that connects projects, investors, and companies to fund nature-based solutions, specifically focusing on nature-based CDR credits and carbon offsets.

name: greenSand
tech_note: Sources, crushes, and distributes olivine-rich rock as gravel/sand/split products that weather on contact with rainwater to remove atmospheric CO2.
description: greenSand is a Netherlands-based enhanced rock weathering supplier founded in 2009 that sells olivine products sourced from mines in Spain, Norway, Italy and Turkey, replacing conventional sand and stone in gardens, pathways, municipalities and sports fields. They also issue CO2 removal certificates registered with ONCRA, including a certified Uithoornlijn project validated in 2025.

name: neo-fossil
tech_note: Soil mineralization
description: neo-fossil is a climate biotech company that engineers biology to create new fossils, storing atmospheric CO2 for centuries through optimized biological processes.

name: pHathom
tech_note: BECCS
description: pHathom is a Canadian climate technology startup that captures CO2 from coastal bioenergy plants using a weathering reactor with limestone, seawater, and biocatalysts to create bicarbonate, effectively performing Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Storage (BECCS).

name: pHathom Technologies
tech_note: Captures biogenic CO2 from coastal biomass bioenergy plants and converts it, via a limestone-seawater weathering reactor, into stable bicarbonate that is stored in the ocean.
description: pHathom Technologies is a Halifax, Nova Scotia cleantech startup (founded 2023/24) developing a hybrid BECCS + ocean alkalinity enhancement pathway it calls Bioenergy Carbon Capture and Ocean Storage (BECCOS). It bolts onto coastal biomass power/heat plants, dissolves captured CO2 in seawater with limestone to form bicarbonate, and releases it for durable marine storage. The company closed a $4M seed round led by Propeller Ventures in Feb 2026 (>$12M total committed capital), was selected for Frontier's advance purchase program, and is running a completed pilot at NSCC Lunenburg with a Huntsman Marine Science Centre trial planned for summer 2026.

name: pyropower
tech_note: Designs and manufactures pyrolysis CHP systems (Pyro-ClinX) combining pyrolysis reactors with an externally fired micro gas turbine to convert biogenic residues into biochar, heat and electricity.
description: pyropower GmbH is a German cleantech engineering firm based in Cottbus that develops decentralized pyrolysis combined heat and power systems producing biochar, green electricity and heat from wood and biogenic residues. Their flagship Pyro-ClinX plant pairs pyrolysis with an air-bearing micro gas turbine and has been deployed in reference projects including Darmstadt and Görlitz.

name: renu.earth
tech_note: Renu Earth produces biochar from sawmill wood residues in Southern Africa (KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa) via pyrolysis, generating Puro.earth-certified CORCs and selling biochar to fertilizer manufacturers.
description: <cite index="4-1,13-8,13-9">Renu Earth is a US-incorporated biochar carbon removal company running its first project with a major sawmill in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, converting sustainable wood residues into biochar and generating certified carbon removal credits through Puro.Earth.</cite> <cite index="3-8,15-16">Carbonfuture committed to purchase the initial 1,000 CORCs and will broker up to 102,000 CORCs annually, with plans to expand to 10 additional sites generating up to 200,000 CORCs annually by 2027.</cite>

name: reverce
tech_note: Provides an end-to-end enhanced rock weathering service — tailored silicate rock material applied to farmland, combined with soil analyses, CO2 efflux measurements, and a proprietary MRV approach.
description: reverce is a German carbon dioxide removal company focused on enhanced rock weathering (ERW), managing the end-to-end process including methodology, tailored rock material composition, land distribution with farmers, and MRV. The company is closely tied to the Carbon Drawdown Initiative and involved in research projects such as Project Carbdown in Germany and the Olivine Project in Greece. Public activity has been quiet, with the most prominent coverage dating to 2023 and a small LinkedIn following.

name: ÖKT Offenhausen
tech_note: Operates NGE T-Cracker pyrolysis plants that convert sewage sludge and organic residues into EBC-certified biochar, with heat integration to the co-located biogas facility.
description: <cite index="18-4,18-5,18-6">ÖKT Offenhausen is a biogas facility in Offenhausen, Bavaria, Germany that dries up to 30,000 tons of locally sourced sewage sludge annually, with drying units powered by sustainable biogas waste heat and CO2-negative Biomass-to-Biochar heat.</cite> <cite index="11-2,11-3,11-4">The pyrolysis system dries sewage sludge and organic residues to create nutrient-rich biochar as a soil additive, produces pyrolysis gas for thermal energy, and is certified by EBC and EBC Agro-Bio.</cite> <cite index="15-1,15-2">Carbon Standards International documented ÖKT as a case study creating a carbon sink of approximately 1,937 tons of CO2e.</cite>

name: ÖkoMAXX Energiewerke
tech_note: Biochar
description: ÖkoMAXX Energiewerke GmbH operates biomass power plants for the generation of electricity and heat. While the company is listed in a biochar registry, the search results primarily indicate its core business is biomass energy production, not explicitly biochar CDR.

name: Öresundskraft
tech_note: BECCS
description: Öresundskraft is a Swedish energy company actively involved in Carbon Dioxide Removal (CDR) through Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Storage (BECCS) at its Filbornaverket combined heat and power plant in Helsingborg. They are securing funding, signing agreements for CO2 storage, and selling carbon reduction certificates.
